rooms.title: ADR — Regime Field for CartridgeManifest
rooms.description: PROPOSED, NOT ADOPTED. A draft architecture decision record for a future @561-group/cartridge schema extension: an optional, computed (never authored) regime field on CartridgeManifest, naming the finite/scott/transfinite/aperiodic settling regime a game's own obstruction/settling computation reaches, where one exists. Staged here rather than in the cartridge package's own docs because that package's source tree is currently under concurrent development and off-limits to this pass; the standing architect should relocate this file into the package's own ADR log once that tree is available for this kind of edit.
rooms.body:
# ADR — Regime Field for `CartridgeManifest`

**Status: PROPOSED. Not adopted. No schema change has been made to `@561-group/cartridge` by
this document or by any code this pass touched.**

**Placement note.** This ADR should live in `@561-group/cartridge`'s own package docs (an
`docs/adr/` directory, or equivalent, alongside its README) once it is adopted or formally
rejected — that is where a future implementer would look for it. It is staged here, in the
gaming-enterprises section's own notes directory, because the cartridge package's source tree
(`561-group-gaming-enterprises-services-section/services/cartridge`) is explicitly off-limits to
this pass (mid-build, concurrent workflow). The standing architect should move this file into the
package's own docs the first time that tree is confirmed landed and open for this kind of edit —
until then, this is the ADR's whole record.

## Context

`wilder-conceptions-01.md` item 2 (the "wilder conceptions" second-Fable note, 2026-08-19) observes
that `@lenticule-science/metrologic/obstruction`'s settling-regime classification (`classify(settling).regime`,
one of `"finite" | "scott" | "transfinite" | "aperiodic"` — confirmed directly against
`obstruction/src/settling.mjs` and its README, and against `equivo-design.md` §5.3's worked
example, which prints `"regime": "transfinite"` from a real computation, not a chosen label) is
already, independently, a real property of at least two shipped or specified game mechanics in
this fleet: Crucible's per-move obstruction cost (`crucible-service/DESIGN.md`, read for this
document — every move's cost is computed via `settling`/`classify`/`h1` on a settling the game
constructs per move) and Equivo's `observe` exercise type (`equivo-design.md` §3 row E). The
conception this ADR formalizes: expose that already-computed classification on the
`CartridgeManifest` a game publishes, so the storefront (or any downstream consumer) can read a
game's own settling regime without importing its full engine.

The same note's item 2 originally proposed naming the field's four values after Caillois' play
categories (Agon/Alea/Mimicry/Ilinx), citing a structural correspondence argued in two places
(the SHRIMP ecology brief's proved regime taxonomy, and an imported NotebookLM-synthesized "Ludic
Architecture" note that independently lands on the same four-way mapping). The same-day
ringleader response in that file explicitly declined that naming: "I don't buy Mimicry-as-
transfinite-bounded; Agon, Alea, and Ilinx map naturally; Mimicry is the cell that smells like it
was filled because the table had four slots... Ship the computed regime under its own honest
names (finite/scott/transfinite/aperiodic); let anyone who wants to say 'Caillois' say it in
prose." This ADR follows that ruling: the field is named after the regime taxonomy itself, not a
borrowed vocabulary layered on top of it.

## Decision (proposed)

Add one optional field to `CartridgeManifest` (`@561-group/cartridge/manifest`):

```ts
export interface CartridgeManifest {
  // ...existing fields, unchanged...

  /**
   * The settling regime a real settling/obstruction computation reaches for this game's own
   * mechanic, where one exists — computed at manifest-generation time by calling
   * `@lenticule-science/metrologic/obstruction`'s `classify()` (or an equivalent settling computation) against
   * a representative or worst-case settling the game itself constructs, never authored by hand
   * and never a design/marketing label. Absent (the whole `regime` key omitted, not a `null` or
   * a placeholder string) for any game with no real settling computation to report — per the
   * house specification standard's own "omit, don't stub" rule (§0).
   */
  readonly regime?: "finite" | "scott" | "transfinite" | "aperiodic";
}
```

**Computed, never authored — the one non-negotiable part of this proposal.** A manifest generator
that hard-codes `regime: "aperiodic"` because a level "feels chaotic" violates this ADR's whole
premise even if the schema technically accepts the string; the field is only meaningful if every
value on it traces to an actual `classify()` call (or equivalent) on a settling the game's own
code constructs. This mirrors the house standard's §13 theory-binding discipline exactly: a
citation to real math is only honest if the code path the citation names is the code path that
actually ran.

**Which fleet lanes would populate it, and how, if adopted:**

- **Crucible** — already computes `classify`/`h1` per move (`crucible-service/DESIGN.md`,
  confirmed read); the natural candidate for `regime` is the daily tangle's own settling
  classification at generation time (before any player move), giving a per-daily "today's tangle
  is a `transfinite` day" signal for free from code that already runs.
- **Equivo** — the `observe` exercise type (§3 row E, `equivo-design.md`) already runs
  `classify(settling)`/`h1(settling)` per exercise; a theme-level manifest could report the
  distribution of regimes its exercise bank covers, though this needs its own design pass to
  decide what "the regime" of a whole theme (versus one exercise) even means — flagged here as an
  open question this ADR does not resolve, not glossed over.
- **onestone** — `DESIGN.md`'s own honesty discipline already disclaims any real theory link for
  its cascade/settle loop beyond fall-graph acyclicity (this fleet's own `ARCHITECTURE.md` §13,
  written this same day, confirms no `@lenticule-science/metrologic` import exists in onestone at all) — under
  this ADR, onestone's manifest would correctly **omit** `regime` entirely, not report one, since
  it has no real settling/obstruction computation to call. This is the proposal's own worked
  example of the "omit, don't stub" rule actually biting: not every game gets this field, and
  that is by design, not a gap.
- **flickering-delve, solitaire, lantern** — no settling/obstruction computation exists in any of
  the three (confirmed by this fleet's own `ARCHITECTURE.md` documents and `DESIGN.md`s); all
  three would correctly omit `regime`.

## Consequences, if adopted

- **Positive.** A storefront or catalog reader gains one honest, computed signal distinguishing
  "this game's core mechanic provably terminates" (`finite`/`scott`, H¹=0) from "this game's core
  mechanic genuinely cannot be resolved from within" (`transfinite`/`aperiodic`, H¹≠0) — without
  needing to understand or import the game's own math. This is a real, checkable fact about a
  game's mechanic, not a marketing genre tag, which is the whole point per `wilder-conceptions-01.md`
  item 2's own framing.
- **Negative / risk.** A schema change to a manifest already published (`@561-group/cartridge@0.1.0`,
  adopted this same day by `flickering-delve-service` and `onestone-service` per this pass's own
  work) is not free — every existing manifest-generating module (`cartridge.manifest.mts` in both
  services) would need review, and `@561-group/cartridge/manifest`'s own `validateManifest` would
  need a rule for the new optional field. This is exactly why the ringleader's response called
  this "an ADR item... proposed, not adopted; cartridge 0.1.0 just shipped and schema changes
  deserve one deliberate pass" rather than landing it immediately.
- **Open question this ADR does not resolve.** Whether a *multi-config* manifest (onestone's own
  60-level `configs` array, or a future theme-level Equivo manifest) reports one `regime` for the
  whole cartridge or one per `CartridgeConfig` — the fleet's two adopters today are both
  single-`regime`-eligible-or-not at the whole-cartridge level (Crucible would report one regime
  for its daily; onestone reports none at all), so this pass has no real multi-config case to
  design against yet. Flagged for whoever picks this ADR up next, not resolved by assertion here.

## Alternatives considered

- **Author the field by hand per game, as a marketing/genre tag.** Rejected outright — this is
  the exact failure mode the "computed, never authored" clause exists to prevent, and it is the
  reading of "genre" `wilder-conceptions-01.md` item 2 explicitly argues against ("a game's genre
  is not a design choice layered onto a mechanic; it is the computed regime of that mechanic's
  own settling").
- **Name the four values after Caillois' play categories.** Rejected by the same-day ringleader
  response, quoted above — the Mimicry mapping does not hold up under scrutiny, and the regime
  taxonomy's own honest names are preferred over a borrowed vocabulary that only partially fits.
- **Ship it now, inside `@561-group/cartridge@0.1.1`.** Rejected for this pass specifically
  because 0.1.1 is already committed to fixing `@561-group/energy-bank`'s consumer-facing
  packaging defect (per this pass's own standing instructions) — bundling an unrelated schema
  proposal into that release would conflate two separate decisions under one version bump, which
  this ADR's own "schema changes deserve one deliberate pass" framing argues against.

rooms.body:
# All Games Census

Five independent sweeps (by-manifest, legacy-geography, owner's-curated-records,
active-tree-by-content, and a deploy-surface round two) were cross-checked directly against
disk — every path below was `stat`'d or `find`'d before publication, not copied verbatim from
any sweep's prose. This note also reconciles against
`estate-inventory-2026-08-19.md` and `computer-gaming-systems-services-section`'s README
(dated the same day, in the same section this note lives in — see "Note on this section" below),
correcting several of their path claims that no longer resolve on disk.

**Note on this section.** `561-group-gaming-enterprises-services-section` (the directory this
note was commissioned to live in) is a **symlink** to
`public-services-section/.../public-computer-games-services-section` — not a separate or
missing location, contrary to one sweep's "confirmed dead end" claim. This note therefore sits
alongside `estate-inventory-2026-08-19.md`, `the-suite-and-the-studio.md`, and the `planned/`
stub notes it cross-references.

**Shelf key** (`the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §3): Card Table (casino/probability) · Puzzle Den
(match-3/puzzle) · Study (board/edutainment) · Deep (MUD/roguelike) · Stars (Okaga-set, later) ·
substrate (cross-game engines/infra, not a game itself) · unshelved.

---

## Mentioned-only — real, game-adjacent, not itself a game

| Name | What it is | Canonical path(s) |
|---|---|---|
| **EVE Assist** | Decision-support/companion web app for the third-party game EVE Online (market, map, chat, dashboard); deployed via a Cloudflare Worker for eve-assist.561.group | `services/engineering-services-section/services/computer-services-section/services/computer-systems-services-section/services/web-services-section/services/web-game-services-section/services/eve-online-services-section` |

---

## Confirmed not games (flagged so future passes don't mistake them for one)

- **`swarm`** and **`farolfi`** — `_archive/from-content-source/apps/tools/{swarm,farolfi}`. Swarm is a "Semiotic Workers Articulating Relational Models" agent-orchestration substrate (1 proof file); farolfi's directory is completely empty, a placeholder only.
- **`waggle`** — `_archive/from-content-source/apps/interface/waggle`. Zero-dependency Node↔Hive blockchain wallet/client. Not a game despite living in a games-adjacent archive.
- **Divination (tarot/spread/deck) services** — a "sign-reading as settling" internal-market labor service that happens to use tarot-deck content; not a game.
- **Card/Dice/Poker/Blackjack/Gambling-games sub-sections** under `agent-services-section/services/play-services-section/services/game-science-services-section/services/gambling-services-section` — content/notes only, no `src`, no engine.
- **Hevî Mala** — `services/public-services-section/.../paracosm-service-section/services/hevi-mala-paracosm-services-section/texts/{worlding-guide.md, triage-synthesis.md}`. A finished worldbuilding-doctrine text, explicitly carrying no game math; a fiction world, not a game.
- **MetroPlat** — a media-publishing/advertising concept (koios-news archive essay), not a game.
- **The Cast**, **The Today page**, **Self-Education Platform** — real named directives in `the-suite-and-the-studio.md` and `estate-inventory-2026-08-19.md`, but cross-cutting features/chassis concepts, not standalone games; not given rows here.
- **ActivityPub server** and **semiotic-exchange-chain family** (`modeled-union-dimension`, `sovereign-membrane-admission-service`) — landed, tested infrastructure, but general federation/ledger substrate rather than game engines; noted under Gamified Fediverse Client above rather than as standalone rows.
- **`561-group-gaming-enterprises-services-section`** — see "Note on this section" above: it is a symlink, not a missing directory. One prior sweep's dead-end claim about this path is itself incorrect.

## Excluded

- **Teraum** — owner's personal fiction, excluded per standing instruction. Named only as encountered (e.g. inside `fizzos/examples/teraum.mjs`, a test-suite fixture name, and one `.ink` file path under a `teraum/` directory); contents never entered, never read.

## Confirmed dead ends (searched, not found — do not re-hunt)

- `okaga.emsenn.net`, `mud.emsenn.net`, `qtmud.emsenn.net`, `mepach.emsenn.net` — all trace only to a single dead 2019-era personal-website archive dump, not current builds.
- `metroplat.emsenn.net` — traces to a media/advertising essay, not a game deploy.
- A copy of **wheatstone** under `computer-mud-services-section/lib/legacy/` — does not exist (checked directly); the only copy is in the `_archive` tree (row above).
- Active (non-legacy) source trees for **abrash, arnold, daleske, tsander, okaga** beyond the `computer-interface-system-services-section/lib/legacy` mirrors and the `_archive` originals — none exist.
- Game code anywhere in the tree for any of the seven "Later"-stage vision items (Undersea MUD, The Commons, Gamified Fediverse Client, Gambling Series, Energy Tiling) beyond their design notes and cited math dependencies — none exists.
- "LLM-native MUD on FizzOS," "shooters via the render ladder," and "voxel games" as *named* corpus items — not found under those names anywhere (the real answers are the active Farstone build / current fizzos, Durante, and Abrash respectively — see rows above).
- No `Caddyfile`, `wrangler.toml`, or `nginx.conf` exists anywhere in the active tree outside one unrelated legacy `gsu-ccs` corpus duplicate.

---

## Totals

- **45 distinct games/engines/prototypes/designs**, plus 3 mentioned-only game-adjacent items (not counted in the 45).
- **Landed: 9** · **In-build: 9** · **Built-legacy-recovery-candidate: 16** · **Design-only: 11** · **Mentioned-only: 3** (9+9+16+11 = 45; +3 mentioned-only = 48 rows total across all tables).
- **New finds not in the orchestrating task's KNOWN list:** Aletheon's *active* build (distinct from the legacy archive copy KNOWN cited), the active Farstone build at `gaming-services-section/services/farstone-services-section`, QwzSpace, the `gaming-services-section` container itself, EVE Assist, Aagaard, Storystream, dg, Crown of Idbol Bark, Dreamfield, the ludics libraries (`@emsenn/gaming`/`@emsenn/playing`), the render-substrate stack's *undated* mirror location (`computer-interface-system-services-section/lib/legacy/{arnold,daleske,tsander,abrash}`, byte-identical to the dated `_archive` copies), Weiqi LSP, and — the single most consequential reconciliation — **Stoke is the kind-incremental idle game**: the estate-inventory's own Part 2 lists "the kind-incremental idle game" as vision-stage with "no prototype," but `stoke-service`'s `eigen.mts`/`prestige.mts`/`kind-design.test.mts` already implement exactly that design (prestige priced as a Perron–Frobenius eigenvalue). It should move from design-only to in-build, which this census does.
- Also corrected: the estate-inventory's claimed paths for **cartridge** and **energy-bank** (`561-group-gaming-enterprises-services-section/services/{cartridge,energy-bank}`) do not resolve on disk; their real home is `computer-game-system-services-section/services/{cartridge,energy-bank}`, used throughout this census.

rooms.body:
# Deploy Runbook — 2026-08-19

Answers the owner's question — "should we get what can get deployed deployed?" — with yes,
and this is the honest record of what that produced. Every URL below was curled in this
session (landing page + a deep asset each, one 404 negative control each, one full
click-path walk for crucible and one for solitaire). Every redeploy command was read out of
the actual `Dockerfile` + `gcloud run services describe` for that service, not guessed.
Cloudflare `*.561.group` DNS is the one piece named but not attempted — see "Deliberately not
done" below.

## Live now

| Service | URL | Landing check | Deep asset check |
|---|---|---|---|
| Storefront (play.561.group) | https://play-561-group-1019481907460.us-central1.run.app/ | `GET /` → 200, `text/html`, real catalog markup (title "play.561.group -- 561 Group games catalog") | `GET /catalog.json` → 200, `application/json`, real cartridge-manifest-shaped catalog body |
| Crucible | https://crucible-1019481907460.us-central1.run.app/ | `GET /web/index.html` → 200, `text/html`, title "crucible.561.group" | `GET /web/js/app.mjs` → 200 `text/javascript` (real bootstrap source) → `GET /vendor/561-group-math/bilattice/src/index.mjs` → 200 `text/javascript` (real `@lenticule-science/metrologic` barrel) → `GET /src/engine.mts` → 200 `text/javascript` (live-stripped TypeScript engine source, not a stub) |
| Solitaire | https://solitaire-1019481907460.us-central1.run.app/ | `GET /web/index.html` → 200, `text/html`, title "solitaire.561.group" | `GET /web/js/landing.mjs` → 200 (real bootstrap) → `GET /web/table.html?variant=klondike-draw1&daily=1` → 200, `text/html`, title "Solitaire" (the actual deep-linked game page a player's "play the daily" click lands on) → `GET /web/js/app.mjs` → 200 `text/javascript` (real table controller) |
| Gambling trainer | https://gambling-trainer-1019481907460.us-central1.run.app/ | `GET /web/index.html` → 200, `text/html`, title "Kelly's Wager — gambling-trainer.561.group" | `GET /web/js/app.mjs` → 200 `text/javascript` (real bankroll controller) → `GET /src/engine.mts` → 200 `text/javascript` (live-stripped bankroll engine, the module `app.mjs` calls `applyIntent` on) |

Stable per-service aliases (also live, same content, no custom domain mapping):
`https://play-561-group-a2d7mjqbfa-uc.a.run.app`. The other three services weren't separately
re-checked on their `-a2d7mjqbfa`-style alias since Cloud Run's alias and primary URL are the
same revision/image — only the primary `run.app` URLs above are the ones curled.

**Negative control**, run against all four: `GET /does-not-exist-xyz` → **404** on every
service. This is real static-file routing (404 on a miss), not a catch-all `index.html`
rewrite silently returning 200 for everything.

All four: region `us-central1`, `min-instances 0`, `max-instances 2`, `cpu 1`, `memory
256Mi`, unauthenticated (public). Confirmed via `gcloud run services describe`.

## Redeploy (exact commands)

Source-based deploys, `--source` pointed at the directory containing each `Dockerfile` — no
git flow, no Cloud Build config file beyond the Dockerfile itself. Run from anywhere; each
command tars its own `--source` directory.

**Storefront:**
```bash
gcloud run deploy play-561-group \
  --source "/home/emsenn/info/lib/emsenn/services/561-group/services/public-services-section/services/public-computer-services-section/services/public-computer-games-services-section/sites/play.561.group" \
  --region us-central1 --platform managed --allow-unauthenticated \
  --min-instances 0 --max-instances 2 --cpu 1 --memory 256Mi
```

**Crucible:**
```bash
gcloud run deploy crucible \
  --source "/home/emsenn/info/lib/emsenn/services/561-group/services/public-services-section/services/public-computer-services-section/services/public-web-services-section/services/public-web-game-services-section/services/crucible-service" \
  --region us-central1 --platform managed --allow-unauthenticated \
  --min-instances 0 --max-instances 2 --cpu 1 --memory 256Mi
```

**Solitaire:**
```bash
gcloud run deploy solitaire \
  --source "/home/emsenn/info/lib/emsenn/services/561-group/services/public-services-section/services/public-computer-services-section/services/public-web-services-section/services/public-web-game-services-section/services/solitaire-service" \
  --region us-central1 --platform managed --allow-unauthenticated \
  --min-instances 0 --max-instances 2 --cpu 1 --memory 256Mi
```

**Gambling trainer:**
```bash
gcloud run deploy gambling-trainer \
  --source "/home/emsenn/info/lib/emsenn/services/561-group/services/public-services-section/services/public-computer-services-section/services/public-web-services-section/services/public-web-game-services-section/services/gambling-trainer-service" \
  --region us-central1 --platform managed --allow-unauthenticated \
  --min-instances 0 --max-instances 2 --cpu 1 --memory 256Mi
```

Before any redeploy, run that service's `npm test` in its own directory and confirm the
count matches (or exceeds, with an explained delta) what's recorded below — do not deploy on
a red suite.

## The PORT/HOST convention

- All three game servers (`web/server.mjs` in crucible, solitaire, gambling-trainer, and
  lantern/stoke by the same house pattern) already read
  `Number(process.argv[2] ?? process.env.PORT ?? 8787)` — Cloud Run's injected `PORT` env var
  is honored with **no source edit needed**. This was re-verified against source directly
  before deploying, not assumed from an earlier plan.
- The storefront's `serve.mjs` reads `process.env.HOST` but **defaults it to `127.0.0.1`**,
  which is unreachable from outside the container. Fixed with `ENV HOST=0.0.0.0` in its
  Dockerfile — a Dockerfile-level environment default, not a source change. `serve.mjs`
  itself is untouched.
- Net effect: **zero application source files were modified** to make any of the four
  services deployable. The only new files anywhere are the four `Dockerfile`s.
- Each `Dockerfile` is the same minimal pattern: `FROM node:24-slim`, `COPY . .` (this
  copies the already-vendored `node_modules` in the tree, sidestepping the local-only
  Verdaccio registry Cloud Build can't reach), `CMD ["node", "<entrypoint>"]`. No `npm
  install`/`npm ci` runs at build time — the build is just "package the tree as it already
  sits on disk."

## Cost posture

- No API was enabled this session — `run.googleapis.com`, `cloudbuild.googleapis.com`,
  `artifactregistry.googleapis.com` were already on before any of this started (verified with
  `gcloud services list --enabled`, not assumed). No new standing-cost trigger was created by
  turning on a service.
- All four Cloud Run services: `min-instances 0` (scales to zero, no charge while idle),
  `max-instances 2` (caps a traffic spike's blast radius), `cpu 1` / `memory 256Mi` (smallest
  practical tier for a static/near-static node server). No always-on component exists in this
  deploy.
- Realistic standing cost at rest: **$0**. Cost only accrues on actual request traffic
  (CPU-time billing while a container instance is warm) plus the trivial Artifact Registry
  storage for the four built container images.

## Deliberately not deployed

**ruinfold** (`.../public-computer-games-services-section/services/ruinfold-services-section/apps/ruinfold`,
real server at `src/server.mts`) — skipped, not attempted. Its persistence layer
(`src/server.mts` + `src/server/store.mts`) writes runs, scores, the daily-attempt lock, and
weekly boons as JSONL under `apps/ruinfold/data/` on local disk. Cloud Run's filesystem is
ephemeral per instance: at the required `min-instances 0` that directory is wiped on every
scale-to-zero, and concurrent instances (allowed up to `max-instances`) would each hold a
disjoint copy of it. That silently breaks the one-scored-run-per-day lock and leaderboard
correctness — not a benign "stateless demo" claim, an actually-wrong one, so it wasn't made.
The two honest fixes are `min-instances 1` (forbidden by the spend-discipline instruction —
that's an always-on cost) or wiring a real managed datastore (a feature build, out of scope
for a "get what can get deployed deployed" pass). No files were touched in ruinfold's tree;
nothing was deployed for it. This stays open as real follow-up work, not abandoned scope.

**Cloudflare `*.561.group` DNS mapping** — intentionally not attempted. The tokens needed to
manage that DNS zone are not on this box. The four `*.run.app` URLs in the table above are
the honest v1 surface; mapping `play.561.group`, `crucible.561.group`,
`solitaire.561.group`, and `gambling-trainer.561.group` to them is the named next step and
needs the owner to either supply the Cloudflare API token to this environment or run the DNS
change from wherever that token lives.

## Rollback

Cloud Run keeps every deployed revision; traffic is reassigned, not destroyed, so rollback is
non-destructive by default.

**Roll back to the previous revision** (list revisions, then shift 100% traffic to the one
that was good):
```bash
gcloud run revisions list --service <service-name> --region us-central1
gcloud run services update-traffic <service-name> --region us-central1 \
  --to-revisions <previous-revision-name>=100
```

**Take a service down entirely** (removes the service and its URL; does not touch the source
tree or the `Dockerfile`):
```bash
gcloud run services delete <service-name> --region us-central1
```

`<service-name>` is one of `play-561-group`, `crucible`, `solitaire`, `gambling-trainer`.

## Local test suites — re-run fresh this session, post-Dockerfile

Run in each service's own directory with `npm test`, immediately before writing this
runbook, to confirm the Dockerfile-only changes (no source edits, per above) broke nothing:

| Tree | Result |
|---|---|
| Storefront (`play.561.group`) | **8/8 pass** |
| Crucible | **103/103 pass** |
| Solitaire | **96/97 pass** — one pre-existing failure, `src/cartridge.test.mts`: "the manifest validates against @561-group/cartridge's own schema checker, with all 6 variants as configs" expects `manifest.configs?.length === 6` but gets `11`. This is a content/data-shape drift in `VARIANT_LIST` vs. an already-stale test expectation, unrelated to the deploy: nothing in this session touched `src/cartridge.test.mts`, `manifest.mts`, or `VARIANT_LIST`, and the Dockerfile added here does not run at test time. Flagged here rather than silently passed over; not fixed — fixing test-vs-source drift in a non-deploy tree is out of this task's scope. |
| Gambling trainer | **79/79 pass** |

No PORT/HOST change caused any regression — the one failure above predates this session's
Dockerfile work and lives entirely in game-content-shape territory, not server/networking
code.

## What needs the owner

1. **Cloudflare `*.561.group` DNS mapping** — needs a Cloudflare API token supplied to this
   box, or the DNS change run from wherever that token already lives. Until then the four
   `run.app` URLs above are the real public addresses.
2. **ruinfold's statefulness** — needs an owner decision between "pay for `min-instances 1`"
   and "build a real managed datastore," neither of which is a same-session task. No billing
   surprise exists yet because nothing was deployed for it.
3. **The solitaire cartridge test drift** (11 vs. 6 configs, above) — not a deploy blocker
   (solitaire is live and its game-serving tests all pass), but it's a real, currently-red
   assertion in that tree that nobody has looked at yet.

No org policy blocks and no billing surprises were hit in this session — every enablement
check came back "already on," every deploy succeeded on the first attempt, and every service
sits at `min-instances 0`.

production graph (feasibility verified — `@lenticule-science/metrologic` exports a `./spectral` subpath) rather
than an authored curve. Sources: `gaming-enterprises-vision.md` §3; `wilder-conceptions-01.md` item
5 (adopted as "phase 1 of the kind-incremental lane when it launches"). **Unbuilt** — no prototype
exists; only the math-dependency check passed, no code written. Staircase: Next (research spike) /
Later (a shipped idle game on top of it).

**19. The gambling/probability series** — a series of gambling-adjacent games teaching kind-economy
principles, starting from the existing tested Kelly-criterion/odds/staking library
(gambling-services-section, Part 1 §4, landed 18/18). See item 13 for the Terminal Bets spend-typing
directive layered onto this series. Sources: `gaming-enterprises-vision.md` §3;
`the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §3 ("The Card Table" shelf); `wilder-conceptions-01.md` item 7.
Unbuilt — no specific game named yet, only the design directive and the underlying odds library.
Staircase: Next.

**20. Okaga-setting games (credits-as-warp)** — games set in Okaga, the owner's interstellar
laser-solar-sail setting, chosen because "the math of Obsmetrologia" fits it; the cross-cutting
conceit (money = energy = time, so purchasing credits enables warp travel or other setting-native
"magic") is meant to skin the one shared Energy Bank ledger per setting. Sources:
`gaming-enterprises-vision.md` §4; `the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §3 ("The Stars (later)" shelf), §2.
Unbuilt, concept-stage only — no specific *new* Okaga game is named (distinct from the already-built
legacy `okaga` space-flight game inventoried in Part 1 §8, which predates and is not what this
vision item is proposing). Staircase: Later.

**21. The cast** — named recurring agent players with stable personas playing real games via the
same intent-log API as human players; `wilder-conceptions-01.md` item 3 speculatively proposes
computing each member's "temperament" as a K₄ gauge-holonomy invariant over cross-game play-history.
Sources: `the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §2, §5 directive 3; `wilder-conceptions-01.md` item 3.
Unbuilt — "a real backlog item attached to the first multiplayer-shaped surface"; the only concrete
adopted next step is logging cross-member play-history as data once the cast exists. Staircase:
Later.

**22. The Today page** — a single page surfacing every daily-seeded game's puzzle in one place.
Source: `the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §2, §5 directive 2, §6. Unbuilt — gated on "two or more daily
games" being live (currently only ruinfold is daily-seeded and it isn't shipped). Staircase: Next.

### Cross-cutting math/design proposals (not separate games)

- **Computed `regime` field** on every `CartridgeManifest` (finite/scott/transfinite/aperiodic) —
  `wilder-conceptions-01.md` item 2; adopted as an ADR item, not yet built.
- **Carrier Audit discipline** (every "free"/"not consumed" claim classified structurally-free /
  priced / terminal) — `wilder-conceptions-01.md` item 1; partly executed same-day as a correction
  to `the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §2, and assigned to `house-specification-standard.md` §8 (shipped
  text, confirmed on read).
- **Isostatic org-chart check** (the fleet's own pebble-game rigidity math run against the fleet's
  own vendor-dependency graph) — `wilder-conceptions-01.md` item 8; explicitly parked, "not yet a
  graph statistic" at 3–4 documented edges.

### Summary count

5 landed/playable games, 2 cross-fleet infrastructure packages in-build, 6 items in active
next-tier specification or skeleton-build, 9 items at vision/later stage, 1 named directive
(Terminal Bets) attached to an unbuilt series, plus 3 cross-cutting math proposals riding on top of
the above. "LLM-native MUD on FizzOS," "shooters via the render ladder," and "voxel games" were not
found under those names anywhere in the assigned corpus; see Part 1 §8 for the actual shooter/voxel
built assets (durante, abrash) that answer those two, and the README's own Contradictions section
for the one open finding on the FizzOS-MUD question.

rooms.body:
# Computer Gaming Systems Services Section

This is Red Cup Engineering's answer to "what game stuff do we have, and where is it." It is an
**orchestrator section**: a map, a dated evidence record, and thin stubs for what's genuinely
unbuilt. It moves nothing. Every built asset named below stays exactly where it already lives;
every path in this document is a pointer, not a copy.

Sibling to `computer-code-services-section`, `computer-data-services-section`,
`computer-networking-services-section`, and `computer-systems-services-section` under
`computer-services-section`.

The full evidence this map is drawn from — complete tables, per-asset test runs, proof-file
checks — lives in
[`content/text/documents/articles/notes/estate-inventory-2026-08-19.md`](content/text/documents/articles/notes/estate-inventory-2026-08-19.md).
This README is the summary and the map; that note is the receipts.

## 0. How to read this map

- **Paths are relative to `561-group/services/`** unless given in full, to keep the tables
  legible. The evidence note gives fuller relative paths; use `find` from the repo root if a
  short path is ambiguous.
- **Status vocabulary**, used consistently: `landed` (shipped, tests run and passing this
  session), `in-build` (real code + tests on disk, actively being built, often by a concurrently
  running workflow this document does not touch), `mid-build (read-only)` (real code on disk,
  inventoried but not executed, per instruction), `dormant` (a section that exists but holds no
  code, only content/notes), `built (legacy archive, recovery candidate)` (real working code once
  existed, now sits in a `lib/legacy/` or `_archive/` snapshot, not wired into anything live), and
  `planned — no code exists` (named in the design corpus, nothing built).
- **Every test count is either "verified" (this section's evidence note ran it fresh) or
  "claimed" (copied from a README inside a read-only tree, not independently executed).** Never
  read a bare number in this document as verified unless it says so.

## 1. Shelves within the shelf

The owner's own framing for the whole estate (`the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §3): not a genre-tag
catalog but named shelves, each reincarnating a specific CD-suite disc from memory.

| Shelf | Games | The CD it reincarnates |
|---|---|---|
| The Card Table | solitaire, gambling/probability series | Hoyle Casino |
| The Puzzle Den | TileSlots (onestone), Crucible, flickering-delve | Entertainment Pack / puzzle discs |
| The Study | weiqi + Learn, Lantern, Equivo | Chessmaster / edutainment discs |
| The Deep | ruinfold daily, later the undersea MUD and the Commons | the MUD/BBS door-games lineage |
| The Stars (later) | Okaga-set games; credits-as-warp | the space-sim disc |

Everything below is organized by build status first, shelf noted per row, because "is it real yet"
is the more load-bearing question for an orchestrator map than genre.

## 2. Now — landed and playable

| Shelf | Game | Real location | Tests | Docs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Puzzle Den | flickering-delve | `public-services-section/.../public-web-game-services-section/services/flickering-delve-service` | **63/63** verified | README, ARCHITECTURE.md, DESIGN.md, ROADMAP.md |
| Puzzle Den | TileSlots (onestone) | `.../public-web-game-services-section/services/onestone-service` | **249/249** verified | README, ARCHITECTURE.md, DESIGN.md, ROADMAP.md, TILESLOTS-DESIGN.md |
| Study | Lantern | `.../public-web-game-services-section/services/lantern-service` | **74/74** src + **10/10** web, verified | DESIGN.md, web/README.md |
| Card Table | Solitaire | `.../public-web-game-services-section/services/solitaire-service` | **59/59** verified | README.md, DESIGN.md |
| Study | Weiqi kernel + Learn | `science-services-section/.../board-games-services-section/services/weiqi-services-section` (`apps/weiqi-kernel`, `services/weiqi-platform/apps/weiqi-learn`) | kernel **71/71 claimed** (read-only, not run this session); Learn runs only via local `npm run serve`, not deployed to a subdomain | README.md, weiqi-kernel-constitution.md, weiqi-platform-constitution.md |

Weiqi's **Play** face (real-time/competitive) is declared in `weiqi-platform-constitution.md` but
not admitted or coded — this is a face of an already-active, already-mapped section, not a
standalone unbuilt game, so it is **not stubbed here**; the pointer above is the whole story.

## 3. Next — in-build, pointer only (no stub — the real tree is the answer)

These are actively being built, in most cases by a workflow this orchestrator does not touch.
Per the task's own rule, an in-build or landed-elsewhere game is never stubbed — a stub next to a
real, growing tree would be a stale lie the day after it's written.

| Shelf | Item | Real location | State |
|---|---|---|---|
| Puzzle Den | Crucible ("Hinterland") | `.../public-web-game-services-section/services/crucible-service` | In-build; DESIGN.md, README.md, src/, web/ confirmed on disk. Tree not read further (concurrently-building lane) |
| Deep | Ruinfold (daily roguelike) | `public-computer-games-services-section/services/ruinfold-services-section/apps/ruinfold` | Specification-and-skeleton: engine modules exist (`src/engine/*`), `src/tests/` empty, no server/client wired |
| — | Cartridge (`@561-group/cartridge`) | `561-group-gaming-enterprises-services-section/services/cartridge` | In-build; real `.mjs`/`.d.ts`/`.test.mts` on disk. Not yet wired into any game (`catalog.json`: every entry `cartridgeWrapped: false`) |
| — | Energy Bank (`@561-group/energy-bank`) | `561-group-gaming-enterprises-services-section/services/energy-bank` | In-build; real source+tests on disk. No fleet service posts a payout entry to it yet |
| — | semiotic-exchange-chain family | `.../computer-systems-services-section/services/semiotic-computer-system-services-section/services/semiotic-exchange-chain-services-section` (+ `modeled-union-dimension`, `sovereign-membrane-admission-service`) | Landed spec + 3 packages, **30/31** verified across the family (the 1 fail is a documented, expected `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for an unwritten package) |
| — | FizzOS MUD kernel | `.../computer-systems-services-section/services/computer-mud-services-section/apps/fizzos` | Landed, **59/60** verified (1 SIGTERM-handling test fails, possibly sandbox-specific) |
| — | ActivityPub server | `.../computer-systems-services-section/services/web-services-section/services/web-protocol-services-section/services/activitypub-services-section` | Landed, **50/50** verified. No public deploy target — see §17 in the evidence note and §9 below |

## 4. Now/Next — the shared substrate

The load-bearing packages and infrastructure every game above rides or is meant to ride.

| Substrate piece | Real location | State |
|---|---|---|
| **@561-group/cartridge** — manifest/intent-log/replay contract | `561-group-gaming-enterprises-services-section/services/cartridge` | In-build, 74/74 own tests verified |
| **@561-group/energy-bank** — double-entry ENERGY ledger, pluggable settlement | `561-group-gaming-enterprises-services-section/services/energy-bank` | In-build, 79/79 own tests verified |
| **@lenticule-science/metrologic** — bilattice/obstruction/spectral/Chu-space core every game's mechanics cite | `science-services-section/.../math-services-section/services/voidmath-services-section/services/math-core` | Landed, 64/64 verified |
| **play.561.group** — the Shelf/Storefront, catalog reader | `561-group-gaming-enterprises-services-section/sites/play.561.group` | Landed, 6/6 verified. Reframed as "the CD-suite reborn" (`the-suite-and-the-studio.md`); named-shelf reorg, a shared "Today" page, and cast v1 are directives, not yet built |
| **ActivityPub federation** — the substrate the gamified-Fediverse-client vision would run on | `.../web-protocol-services-section/services/activitypub-services-section` | Landed, 50/50 verified, no reachable public deploy yet |
| **Self-Education Platform** — corpus-compiler/FSRS/Checker chassis under Lantern, Equivo, weiqi-Learn | not a separate service — "what `lantern-service/src/` already substantially is, generalized in place" | Specified (`self-education-platform-design.md`); the pluggable `Checker` interface has no code yet |
| **ZBD micropayment rails** — Lightning payout adapter, ads-fund-payouts ledger policy | not built | Specification only (`zbd-micropayment-rails.md`); no fleet service posts a `liabilities:*`/`expenses:payout:*` entry yet |
| **The cast** — recurring agent players sharing the intent-log API | not built | Named directive (`the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §5); no code |
| **The Today page** — one page, every daily game's puzzle | not built | Named directive; gated on two-or-more daily games shipping (only ruinfold is daily-seeded, and it isn't shipped) |
| **Cross-cutting math proposals** — computed `regime` field on `CartridgeManifest`; Carrier Audit discipline; isostatic org-chart check | Carrier Audit is partially shipped as text in `house-specification-standard.md` §8; the other two are parked design items | See evidence note, "Cross-cutting math/design proposals" |

## 5. Planned — no code exists (stubs created in this section)

Every one of these got a thin `services/<name>-service/NOTE.md` stub in this section: honest
status, the faithful concept paragraph, source citations, staircase tier, smallest first step.

| Stub | Concept | Staircase |
|---|---|---|
| [`services/the-commons-service`](services/the-commons-service/NOTE.md) | The owner's eventual massively-cooperative persistent shared world | Later |
| [`services/energy-tiling-service`](services/energy-tiling-service/NOTE.md) | "r/place but bejeweled" — one shared board, energy-costed tiling, the windy hinterlands | Later, piloted at Next-tier scale via Crucible |
| [`services/undersea-mud-service`](services/undersea-mud-service/NOTE.md) | The SHRIMP-ecology cooperative wuxia MUD | Later |
| [`services/gamified-fediverse-client-service`](services/gamified-fediverse-client-service/NOTE.md) | An ActivityPub client that turns the public Fediverse into an MMORPG | Later, hard-blocked on a public deploy |
| [`services/kind-incremental-idle-service`](services/kind-incremental-idle-service/NOTE.md) | Kind-incremental idle game; prestige priced as a real spectral eigenvalue | Next (research spike) / Later (shipped game) |
| [`services/gambling-series-service`](services/gambling-series-service/NOTE.md) | The gambling/probability series, plus the "Terminal Bets" spend-typing directive | Next |
| [`services/equivo-service`](services/equivo-service/NOTE.md) | "Duolingo for mathematics" — real obstruction-theory checker, no lesson corpus yet | Later |

`farstone-service` also sits in this section's `services/` directory, **reserved and left
untouched by this workflow** — see §9.

## 6. Built (legacy archive, recovery candidates) — stubs created in this section

The owner's corrections, honored directly: **shooters are not unbuilt** — durante is a
first-playable Quake-like. **Voxel is not unbuilt** — abrash casts rays over a federated voxel
world. Both are real, tested-at-the-time code sitting in an archive, not absent concepts.

| Stub | What was actually built | Legacy path(s) | Recovery against the active tree |
|---|---|---|---|
| [`services/durante-service`](services/durante-service/NOTE.md) | First-playable Quake-like FPS: walk a level, strafe, shoot a demon | `_archive/from-content-source/apps/games/durante` (62 assertions/4 proofs claimed, proof files absent); plus two *further* broken snapshot copies in the active tree at `public-computer-games-services-section/services/durante-services-section/lib/legacy/*` | Rides abrash, which rides daleske. Recovery requires the whole render-substrate stack first |
| [`services/render-substrate-service`](services/render-substrate-service/NOTE.md) | arnold (TUI base) + daleske (raster over arnold) + tsander (wireframe-3D over arnold) + abrash (raycaster GAME ENGINE, federated voxel world, over daleske) | `_archive/from-content-source/apps/tools/{arnold,daleske,tsander,abrash}` | The dependency floor under durante and okaga; recovering either game means recovering this stack first |
| [`services/wheatstone-service`](services/wheatstone-service/NOTE.md) | MUD client: telnet/GMCP/MSDP/MXP | `_archive/from-content-source/apps/tools/wheatstone` (116 assertions/7 proofs, files present) | Targets the active fizzos (`computer-mud-services-section/apps/fizzos`) or the active farstone build (see §9) as a client |
| [`services/okaga-service`](services/okaga-service/NOTE.md) | Elite-like space-flight game on tsander — "a GAME, not just a setting" | `_archive/from-content-source/apps/games/okaga` (proof files absent) | Rides tsander, part of the render-substrate stack |
| [`services/fyreside-service`](services/fyreside-service/NOTE.md) | A single orphaned Python `Card` base class, no game loop — flagged as a discrepancy, see §10 | active tree at `public-computer-games-services-section/services/fyreside-services-section/lib/legacy/cards.py` | Not comparable to the other four; there is no working build to recover, only a fragment to build from |

## 7. Full legacy archive inventory (read-only; not everything above got a stub)

The archive (`561-group/lib/legacy/2026-08-17-vps-561-group/_archive/from-content-source/apps/`)
holds more than the five game-shaped assets stubbed above. Listed here for map-completeness, per
this document's job of being the *single* legible map — none of the rows below got a stub, because
the orchestrating task scoped stubs to game-shaped assets, not the whole tools/interface archive.

- **tools/**: `farolfi` (empty placeholder, not a built asset), `swarm` (agent-orchestration
  substrate, 1 proof file), `tab` (EAVT world-engine underlying fizzos/ruinfold/farstone, 36 proof
  files present — the best-attested asset in the whole archive), `fizzos` (legacy MUD-driver copy
  over tab, no tests, no README).
- **games/**: `farstone` (excluded from this workflow — §9), `ruinfold` (superseded by the active
  `apps/ruinfold` rebuild, §3), `aletheon` (browser 3D fantasy MMORPG, WebGL2 + WebSocket net layer
  over voidmath, test directory completely empty despite a README naming three specific test
  files).
- **interface/**: `waggle` (Node↔Hive blockchain client, the most fleshed-out interface app —
  SECURITY.md, AGENTS.md, man pages, 4 test files), `claude-code` (harness binding a session into
  SWARM as a "Layer 7 carrier"), `shell` (the first userspace interface app, a "settling
  shell/REPL").
- **language/**: completely empty — not a built asset.

## 8. Dormant — content-only sections (not stubbed; nothing to recover, nothing planned)

These hold notes, not code, and are not "planned games" in the stub-worthy sense — they're
established content homes with no build attached yet by any design note in the assigned corpus.

- `agent-services-section/services/play-services-section/services/game-science-services-section/services/gambling-services-section/services/poker-services-section`
- `.../gambling-services-section/services/blackjack-services-section`
- `.../gambling-services-section/services/gambling-games-services-section`
- `agent-services-section/services/play-services-section/services/game-science-services-section/services/dice-games-services-section`
- `agent-services-section/services/play-services-section/services/game-science-services-section/services/card-games-services-section`

The gambling/probability series stub (§5) is the one place a future game in this space is
concretely staged.

## 9. Excluded from this workflow

- **`services/farstone-service`** — reserved by another workflow; left exactly as found (an empty
  directory). This map does not write into it or describe its intended contents.

## 10. Contradictions and open questions found while compiling this map (reported, not resolved)

1. **A live, current-generation farstone build exists that neither source inventory mentions.**
   `public-services-section/.../public-web-services-section/services/public-web-game-services-section/sites/farstone.561.group`
   has a real `package.json` — `@red-cup-engineering/farstone-emsenn-net`, described as "a data-defined
   world and capability runtime built on **current** FizzOS," with named test files
   (`depths.test.mts`, `director.test.mts`, `farstone-arcs.test.mts`, `farstone-climate.test.mts`,
   `player-journey.test.mts`, `simulation.test.mts`, `stability.test.mts`) and a `src/serve.mts`.
   Its own README frames it as "a gather-only consolidation point... nothing has been fixed,
   deduplicated, or reconciled yet," pulling together *seven* prior farstone generations into
   `lib/legacy/`. This tree was not run or opened further by this workflow (farstone is explicitly
   out of scope here), but its mere existence is a materially relevant fact this document's own
   corpus audit missed entirely — and it is plausibly the actual answer to the task brief's
   "LLM-native MUD on FizzOS" question, which the planned-inventory audit reported as "not found in
   the assigned corpus." Reported for whichever workflow owns `farstone-service` and for the owner
   to reconcile; not resolved here.
2. **A same-named, differently-scoped section already exists.**
   `computer-systems-services-section/services/computer-game-system-services-section/` (note:
   *game*-system, singular, not *gaming*-systems) already exists as a sibling-of-a-cousin location,
   holding `lib/legacy/` triage copies of farstone, fizzos, flickering-delve, and qwzspace-server,
   plus an `interactive-fiction-services-section` child, and has no README of its own. This
   orchestrator section (`computer-gaming-systems-services-section`, the owner's actual request)
   is a different, new location; the two names are close enough to invite confusion. Not merged,
   not touched, per the do-not-modify-existing-trees rule — flagged for the owner to decide whether
   `computer-game-system-services-section` should eventually fold into this map.
3. **fyreside's assigned stub status doesn't match its actual disk state.** The orchestrating task
   groups fyreside with durante/render-substrate/wheatstone/okaga under one status label ("built in
   legacy archive — recovery candidate"). On disk, fyreside is a single orphaned Python `Card`
   class with no game loop, no package.json, no tests, sitting in the *active* tree's own
   `lib/legacy/`, not the separate `_archive` tree the other four live in. Its stub (§6) states
   this honestly rather than repeating "built" language the evidence doesn't support — flagged as a
   contradiction between the task's suggested framing and what's actually on disk, per this
   workflow's standing instruction to verify every status claim.
4. **The legacy `okaga` game and the vision-stage "Okaga-setting games" concept share a name but
   are different things at different staircase tiers.** The legacy archive's `okaga` (§6) is an
   already-built Elite-like space game. `gaming-enterprises-vision.md` §4's "Okaga-setting games"
   is a distinct, later-stage vision for *future, unnamed* games using the Okaga setting's
   credits-as-warp economic conceit — not a request to rebuild the legacy game. Both facts are
   recorded (the legacy game in the `okaga-service` stub, the vision item in the evidence note's
   Part 2 §20) but kept as two separate claims rather than merged into one, since merging them
   would overstate what the vision note actually asks for.
5. **The "render ladder" naming in the task brief does not match any genre-ladder concept in the
   corpus.** It names an SVG-first *rendering discipline* proposed for Crucible in the vision note,
   not a progression of shooter/voxel games. This document uses "render-substrate" instead (§6) to
   name the arnold→daleske/tsander→abrash dependency stack, deliberately avoiding the "render
   ladder" phrase so as not to imply a corpus source that doesn't exist for it.

## Sources

`gaming-enterprises-vision.md`, `the-suite-and-the-studio.md`, `wilder-conceptions-01.md`,
`semioverse-state-and-fediverse-client-feasibility.md`, `cartridge-and-energy-bank-spec.md`,
`house-specification-standard.md`, `fleet-spec-coverage-and-roadmap.md`, `equivo-design.md`,
`self-education-platform-design.md`, `zbd-micropayment-rails.md`, `tileslots-market-teardown.md`,
`weiqi-platform-plan.md`, `weiqi-market-teardown.md` — all under
`561-group-gaming-enterprises-services-section/` and the relevant service sections' own
`content/text/documents/articles/notes/`. Full built-asset and planned-inventory detail:
[`content/text/documents/articles/notes/estate-inventory-2026-08-19.md`](content/text/documents/articles/notes/estate-inventory-2026-08-19.md).
