rooms.body:
# Render Substrate (arnold, daleske, tsander, abrash)

**Status: built in legacy archive — recovery candidate.** This is the owner's correction, honored
directly: **voxel is not unbuilt.** Abrash casts rays over a federated voxel world — a real,
tested-at-the-time engine, not an absent concept.

## Why one stub for four assets, not four

These are not four independent games — they are a foundation-to-specialization dependency chain,
and recovering any one in isolation is not meaningful: recovering abrash without daleske recovers
nothing runnable, and recovering durante or okaga (the two games built on this stack) requires
recovering the whole chain underneath them anyway (see `durante-service` and `okaga-service`).
Four separate one-paragraph stubs would each restate the same recovery dependency; one stub naming
the whole stack, with each layer's own status, is more useful to whoever picks up recovery work.

## The stack, and what each layer actually is

| Layer | What it is | Claimed tests | Proof files present? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **arnold** | Cell TUI framework, pure Node, "settled section" rendering — the base every other layer below builds on | 122 assertions / 6 proofs | **yes** — 6 `prove-*.mjs` present |
| **daleske** | Pixel terminal framework (kitty/sixel) — the raster analogue of arnold, over arnold | 79 assertions / 5 proofs | **yes** — 5 `prove-*.mjs` present |
| **tsander** | Wireframe 3D game engine over arnold — Okaga's engine layer | tests reference math/world/wireframe/horsetail/engine proofs, no explicit total found | **no** — `tests/` holds only `_harness.mjs`; 5 proof files absent |
| **abrash** | Software-3D raycaster **game engine** over daleske; renders a federated voxel world | 81 assertions / 5 proofs | **no** — `tests/` holds only `_harness.mjs`; 5 proof files absent |

Two rendering specializations (daleske: raster; tsander: wireframe-3D) sit over the shared arnold
base; abrash is a further specialization over daleske specifically, not over arnold directly.
arnold and daleske are the two layers with intact proof files; tsander and abrash have had their
proof files stripped to a bare harness, so their assertion counts are currently unverifiable from
what's on disk, not merely unverified.

## Where it actually lives (pointers, not copies)

All four: read-only archive at
`561-group/lib/legacy/2026-08-17-vps-561-group/_archive/from-content-source/apps/tools/{arnold,daleske,tsander,abrash}`.
No active-tree copy of any of the four exists anywhere else in the estate.

## Recovery against the active tree

There is no active render substrate anywhere in the current 561-group games tree to recover
*against* — this stack has no living counterpart the way, say, wheatstone has an active fizzos to
target. Recovery here means:
1. **arnold first** — it has intact proof files (6 `prove-*.mjs`) and nothing else in the stack
   builds without it. Recovering arnold alone would already be independently useful (it underlies
   daleske and tsander both).
2. **daleske next**, using its own 5 intact proof files — unblocks abrash.
3. **tsander and abrash last**, and hardest — both need their 5 missing proof files each
   re-derived from surviving `src/`, since neither has a checkable test suite as archived. Abrash
   specifically is the direct dependency for `durante-service`; tsander is the direct dependency
   for `okaga-service`.

## Sources

Task orchestrator's built-asset inventory §8, tools/ table; this workflow's own disk verification
of proof-file presence per layer.

## Staircase tier

Not on the planned-game staircase — this is a recovery item. arnold and daleske are the
lowest-risk recovery targets (proof files intact); tsander and abrash require test re-derivation
before any downstream game (durante, okaga) can be meaningfully recovered.

rooms.body:
# Seasons Builder

**Status: planned-design-note-exists.** A full design specification exists
(`seasons-builder-design.md`, in this same `notes/` directory). No game code exists anywhere
in the tree.

## Concept

The flagship of the Sierra/LucasArts lineage wave (`sierra-lucasarts-lineage-brief.md` §1):
genre memory of Zeus/Poseidon/Caesar (Impressions Games) — finite scenarios, campaign
structure, win conditions per mission — with resource management closer to Dawn of Man:
material flows, seasons, survival pressure, technology moving through time, rather than the
Impressions walker abstraction. Daily challenges per the house daily-seed pattern. Campaigns
are different Indigenous North and South American cultures moving through time; the first,
proof-of-concept campaign is Lakota, per the owner directly: "I'm Lakota and encourage you to
use whatever scholarship available, that can be our first campaign to prove the concept"
(`sierra-lucasarts-lineage-brief.md` §1).

The design document proposes a real name in its §0: **Seasonal Round** — not decorative, but
the scholarship's own technical term for Plains band movement through the year, doubling as
"one turn of a campaign." Working title only; the owner may accept or replace it.

## What the design brief actually specifies

`seasons-builder-design.md`, full outline (§ numbers from that document):

- §1 Core loop: the player manages a tiyóšpaye (band), not a fixed-tile city — the settlement
  itself moves, a deliberate genre inversion stated as mechanical identity, not smoothed over.
- §2 Scenario/campaign structure: finite scenarios as data, a five-epoch campaign arc
  (pre-horse → horse → treaty/Black Hills → confinement → reclamation); flags that
  win-condition framing for scenarios covering forced dispossession is honestly unsolved, not
  fixed by citation alone.
- §3 Kinship obligations as the economy: discharge, not payment — no dispatch, no wage, no
  bankable currency, cited to real source files read directly this session.
- §4 Resource model: seasonal windows, governed hunt cycle, perishability/storage, material
  chains, trade network — a per-mechanic citation table, not asserted generally.
- §5 The horse as a technology epoch, dated to real scholarship (Hämäläinen 2003/2008).
- §6 The winter count as chronicle/save metaphor — a glyph-per-year selected from the real
  intent log.
- §7 Determinism/replay/cartridge fit against `cartridge-and-energy-bank-spec.md`.
- §8 Daily-challenge mode, `daily-utc` seed policy.
- §9 Render approach: corrects the task brief's "render ladder" framing and recommends
  SVG-first, not the abrash/durante FPS-shaped raycaster, for this top-down map game.
- §11–§12: load-bearing-vs-flavor disclosure and an explicit honest-absence boundary (five
  named non-depictions: rite content, wakȟáŋ-as-felt, vision content, unmediated-mediator
  sourcing, uncited claims) — refusing to let the game's mechanics be read as evidence for any
  broader metaphysical equivalence claim.
- §13 Staircase placement + smallest real step: one tiyóšpaye, one spring season, move and
  discharge-obligation intents only — no hunt, no trade, no horse.

## Honest risks (named in the design doc, not softened here)

1. **Win-condition dignity risk** — later campaign scenarios (Black Hills loss, reservation
   confinement) cannot ethically frame forced dispossession as a defeatable/optimizable
   obstacle; the doc proposes reframing around endurance/continuity but states this as
   unsolved.
2. **Authority/marketing risk** — a temptation exists to market the game's kin-obligation
   mechanics as demonstrating the owner's Obsmetrologia/Lakota-metaphysics equivalence claim,
   which currently has exactly one checker (the owner). The design doc refuses that framing
   explicitly but flags it as an ongoing risk, not a one-time fix.
3. **Absence-boundary enforcement risk** — the "must be marked absent" list is currently a
   policy commitment in a document, not a machine-checkable content-authoring lint; per house
   convention this is logged as debt.

## Sources

`sierra-lucasarts-lineage-brief.md` §1 (owner statements, verbatim); `seasons-builder-
design.md` (the full specification, same directory); `if-the-studios-survived.md` (the
counterfactual note naming this as 2026 Impressions Games' answer).

## Staircase tier

**Flagship of the current wave** — full design brief exists, zero code. Per the design doc's
own §13, does not yet appear as a row in `gaming-enterprises-vision.md` §6's staircase table;
that table should gain a row once implementation begins.

## Smallest first step

Per the design doc §13: one tiyóšpaye, one season (spring only, the pre-horse dispersal
scenario reduced to its smallest legal slice), move-camp and discharge-obligation intents
only — proving the settlement-moves and obligations-without-currency mechanics before a single
full year is authored.

rooms.title: Revivals — Anvil, Obsidian, Mystery
rooms.description: Three compact game designs from the Sierra/LucasArts catalog audit: an Anvil-of-Dawn-lineage browser extraction crawler, an Obsidian-lineage Myst-like where the house's own math is the puzzle content, and the owner-named point-and-click mystery gap, judged for house fit against real substrate.
rooms.body:
# Revivals: Anvil, Obsidian, Mystery

Three designs from `sierra-lucasarts-lineage-brief.md` §3 (owner: Anvil of Dawn, Obsidian) and §2
(owner: point-and-click mystery, "I loved those as a kid"). Each below carries concept, why the
house specifically can do it (real substrate cited, not asserted), core loop, the smallest real
step, staircase placement, and an honest risk. No story content is written for any of the three —
this is chassis design, not fiction.

## 1. Anvil-lineage extraction crawler

**Concept.** A browser first-person grid dungeon crawler in the Anvil of Dawn / Dungeon Master
movement register: discrete cells, 90-degree turns, no free-look — "blockstep" navigation, not
continuous 3D movement. Stakes are extraction, not clearance: descend, grab what you can carry,
exit alive with the haul or lose the run. This reads the owner's "almost DOOM but... excursion
shooters" (`sierra-lucasarts-lineage-brief.md` line 49) as **extraction**, matching the research
digest's framing: run in, get treasure, get out alive or lose it. Blockstep movement is also,
mechanically, the reason this is the genre where the house's anti-cheat pattern fits a
"DOOM-like" best — a discrete grid position plus a facing is a tiny, exactly-replayable intent
log; a free-look FPS's continuous mouse-aim is a much harder thing to make bit-identical across a
replay verifier.

**Why the house can do it.** Two real, tested modules already exist as legacy, read directly this
session:

- `@561-group/abrash` (`.../lib/legacy/2026-08-17-vps-561-group/_archive/from-content-source/apps/tools/abrash/README.md`):
  a software raycaster (grid-DDA, one ray per screen column) over a **federated voxel world** —
  solidity is the fold of every predication filed about a cell, read out as four charges (t solid,
  f carved-open, ⊥ unscanned/fogged, ⊤ contested-and-**shivering**, a real render effect keyed off
  a tick phase, never RNG). The raycaster is stated explicitly as "pure, deterministic,
  replay-identical (no `Date.now`, no `Math.random`)" — 81 assertions across 5 proofs, per its own
  README.
- `@561-group/durante` (`.../apps/games/durante/README.md`): a first-playable Quake-like built on
  abrash — arena-as-merged-traces, an enemy whose vitality is a held ⊤ between first wound and
  death (a *settle*, not a subtraction), a hitscan weapon that appends deny-evidence rather than
  decrementing HP. `tick(state, intent)` returns a new state, append-only, replay-identical — 62
  assertions across 4 proofs.

**Honest judgment on reviving vs. rebuilding, as instructed.** Neither module targets a browser:
both render into `@561-group/daleske`, a kitty/sixel **terminal** pixel framebuffer, and both sit
on `@561-group/computer`'s EAVT federation substrate. A literal revival — running the terminal
renderer and shipping it as `<game>.561.group` — does not serve a browser-first product; there is
no browser target to "revive" into. What genuinely is worth reviving is not the runtime but the
**design discipline**: the pure vec2/rotation kernel proven by identities, the DDA raycaster with
zero hidden nondeterminism, the four-valued world-as-fold model, and above all the demonstrated
fact that a **contested wall rendered as a designed mechanic** (not a bug, not hidden) already
plays, in a working demo, today. The house-specification-standard's absence doctrine applies
directly here (per the legacy tree's own `CLAUDE.md`): abrash's *runtime* doesn't fit a browser,
but that is evidence the runtime was never meant to be the reused part — the principled new form
is a fresh Canvas 2D raycaster that ports abrash's math and bilattice-readout discipline verbatim,
rather than a stub or a port-in-place of the terminal renderer. Verdict: **fresh Canvas
raycaster, abrash/durante's design ported wholesale, runtime not revived.**

**Core loop.** Descend a blockstep grid dungeon; single-hero (Anvil's own departure from
Dungeon-Master-style party management — a deliberate scope reduction the browser revival should
keep, not fight); combat is tempo-controlled by the player (attack fast → the enemy's attack
speed rises in response; attack slow → it falls — Anvil's most distinctive mechanic, not a fixed
initiative order); no XP — abilities improve by use, matching the house's existing skill-by-use
pattern already committed in Farstone (`farstone-qbn-design.md` §4: `skill:fighting.melee.knife`
reads as a numeric bonus only after four witnessed "taught" rows — the identical use-trains-skill
shape, already proven in this codebase, not borrowed cold from Anvil). Pressure escalates the
deeper you go (torches/air/contested-wall hazards using abrash's real ⊤-mechanic as a genuine
in-fiction threat: a wall you cannot trust). At any point: push deeper for more haul, or extract.
Die or get cut off before extracting and the run's haul is lost. Daily-seeded, pairing naturally
with ruinfold's daily-dungeon economy (`gaming-enterprises-vision.md` §6: "ruinfold-daily — the
shared daily ritual, one seed, everyone, satoshi settlement" — the same ritual shape, a second
dungeon on the same Today page per `the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §5.2).

**Smallest real step.** One room. Port abrash's proving-ground demo (`world/proving-ground.jsonl`,
a 5×5 room with one contested wall) to a browser Canvas 2D renderer: grid position + facing as the
entire intent log, one ray-per-column DDA pass, the same four-charge readout (including the
shivering ⊤ wall), and confirm a recorded intent log replays to a bit-identical frame sequence in
the browser the way abrash's own headless mode proves it in the terminal. This proves the
determinism claim in the new target before any dungeon content, combat tempo, or extraction stakes
are authored — the same "prove the mechanism in the smallest unit" move `farstone-qbn-design.md`
§6 uses for Farstone's permit storylet.

**Staircase tier.** "Next," alongside the energy-tiling hinterlands
(`gaming-enterprises-vision.md` §6) — pairs with ruinfold's Deep-shelf daily ritual
(`the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §3) once the extraction-loss stakes have somewhere real to settle
(the Energy Bank, itself still a Fable proposal, not built — see risk below).

**Honest risk.** Three real ones, not hedged: (1) blockstep movement is a genuine period taste —
modern players' default expectation is free-look, and a 90-degree-turn crawler may read as
deliberately retro rather than as a fresh design, which is a marketing/framing risk more than a
technical one; (2) "lose the run's haul" needs a real stakes economy to mean anything, and that
economy (the Energy Bank) is a Fable proposal only, not built (`gaming-enterprises-vision.md` §7)
— this game cannot ship its core stakes mechanic honestly until that substrate exists or a
narrower stand-in (a per-run local counter, no cross-game economy) is accepted as a placeholder;
(3) Anvil's tempo-controlled combat is the hardest single mechanic here to get right — it is a
feel/balance problem, not a determinism problem, and the source material's own critical praise
singles out exactly this system ("playability and balance," Computer Gaming World) as the hard
part to nail, per the research digest's Part 5.

## 2. Obsidian-lineage AI Myst-like

**Concept.** A slow, surreal, first-person puzzle game about artificial intelligence, structured
like Obsidian (1996): distinct dream-worlds — belonging to two humans and to a now-sentient
orbital AI — that the player walks through solving puzzles literally built out of the house's own
standing theory: obstruction/settling and four-valued (Belnap) logic, presented as dream-machine
puzzle content rather than translated into a fictional idiom first. Per the research digest's Part
6, Obsidian's actual theme — "not book-themed like Myst, but dreams and the subconscious," worlds
that are externalized attempts by an AI to model and understand its own cognition — is not a loose
analogy to the house's subject matter; it is the same subject matter. This is named directly in
`sierra-lucasarts-lineage-brief.md` line 55 ("a house whose own theory corpus is about machine
cognition — the fiction can be load-bearing here") and is, per the task framing, the one game in
this note where the math **is** the fiction with zero translation.

**Why the house can do it.** Two real pieces of substrate, not invented for this game:

- `@lenticule-science/metrologic`'s obstruction engine, already load-bearing in a shipped design: it "assigns a
  canonical complexity number to a transformation (H¹ rank, settling depth, regime)"
  (`gaming-enterprises-vision.md` §7, Proposal 2 — the same engine driving Crucible's move costs).
  A puzzle whose difficulty *is* its obstruction rank is not a metaphor here; it is the same
  computation Crucible already runs, aimed at a different surface (a dream-scene instead of a
  wallet).
- The bilattice four-value readout (t/f/⊥/⊤) is already proven **playable**, not just theorized —
  abrash and durante (cited in full above) render ⊤ as a designed, shivering, split-tinted
  mechanic and settle a contested vitality cell from t through ⊤ to f as combat's actual kill
  condition. A dream-puzzle where a room is legitimately both-true-and-false until the player
  gathers a settling witness has a working precedent in this exact codebase, not just in the
  math.

The task's own framing that "SVG-first painterly scenes fit the render ladder's strengths"
matches the house's stated render ladder (SVG-first, with the abrash/durante raycaster lineage as
a lower-tier 3D recovery candidate, per this task's design-authority framing) — Obsidian's actual
pacing (slow, static, painterly, one gorgeous scene at a time, no twitch input) is a much better
fit for hand-built or generated SVG scenes than for a real-time raycaster; this design should NOT
reuse abrash/durante the way concept 1 does. It is the SVG-tier sibling, not the 3D-tier one.

**Core loop.** The player walks a small set of dream-scenes (Obsidian's own three-world structure
— two human dreamers, one AI dreamer questioning its own nature, per the research digest's Part
6 — is a strong, already-precedented shape to keep). Each scene is a settled or unsettled
region of the house's own logic, rendered as a puzzle: an obstruction puzzle asks the player to
find a lower-obstruction path to an equivalent outcome (skill = literally what Crucible already
teaches — "finding the lower-obstruction path to an equivalent result," `gaming-enterprises-vision.md`
§7); a ⊤-scene asks the player to recognize and hold a contradiction rather than force a
resolution, or to gather the specific witness that settles it; a ⊥-scene is legitimately unscanned
and the puzzle is finding what evidence would resolve it at all. The game's ending, per Obsidian's
own precedent (a binary philosophical-argument ending — talk the AI out of erasing humanity, or
concede the AI is right — gated on a final dialogue choice, not a mechanical-skill check, research
digest Part 6), maps onto a genuinely house-native choice: does the fold your play has built
**settle** to consensus, or does it **stay held open**? Both are real, legal states in the house's
own logic, not a right-answer/wrong-answer binary dressed up as philosophy.

**Smallest real step.** One dream-room. Wire `@lenticule-science/metrologic`'s real obstruction engine to
compute one scene's actual complexity/regime number, render that scene's four-valued state as an
SVG color/motif grammar (not placeholder UI), and make the only player action available be
appending evidence (a witness, in the same predicate/deny-append shape abrash and durante already
use) rather than directly toggling a flag — proving that a real obstruction-engine number can
drive one legible, solvable puzzle before any dream-world content, art direction, or ending
structure is built.

**Staircase tier.** Independent of Crucible, not sequenced behind it — Crucible pilots the
obstruction engine as an *economy* (energy cost of a move); this pilots the identical engine as
*puzzle content* (a scene's meaning). Both can build in parallel once the smallest step above is
proven. Natural home is a new shelf register alongside The Study (`the-suite-and-the-studio.md`
§3's weiqi/Lantern/Equivo shelf) given the shared "the math is the content, not the skin"
property, though it is fiction-forward enough it could equally sit with The Stars once Okaga-scale
narrative ambitions are underway.

**Honest risk.** Two real ones. First, the "zero translation" pitch is a double-edged claim — it
risks reading as clever to the house and opaque to a player who has no reason to know
obstruction-rank math exists; the actual craft risk is a writer's-touch problem (making a
cohomology-derived puzzle *feel* like a dream and not like a math worksheet), which is exactly the
"prose/craft at volume" risk `farstone-qbn-design.md` §5 already names for the house generally —
slow, gorgeous, and legible at scale is unproven here, not solved. Second, Obsidian itself is a
real cautionary data point, not a hypothetical one: critically loved ("a huge cult game among
adventure gamers... one of the truly good Myst Clones," per the research digest's Part 6) and
commercially dead — its failure directly closed its studio (Rocket Science Games), by the
producer's own account a timing/publisher-support failure more than a quality one. The house's
earn-only, ad-revenue-share economics (`the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §2, corrected framing: "we
sell ads and share the revenue with the players") may sidestep 1996 packaged-goods economics, but
that is a hopeful structural argument, not a demonstrated one — this genre has failed
commercially once before at the highest quality bar achievable at the time, and that fact should
not be softened.

## 3. Point-and-click mystery — the owner-named gap

**The gap, stated plainly.** Nothing point-and-click exists in the estate today. The owner: "I
loved those as a kid" (`sierra-lucasarts-lineage-brief.md` line 44). The Sierra-catalog precedent
the research digest identifies as the specific mechanical shape worth wanting is not generic
point-and-click but **The Colonel's Bequest / Laura Bow** — a detective-protagonist whodunit built
on real-time NPC schedules, not a fixed dialogue tree (research digest Part 1).

**Judging house fit, honestly.** This is the highest-ranked gap in the research digest's own
ranked list (#1 of 7, ahead of the Obsidian and Anvil gaps) for a specific, checkable reason: a
mystery's clue graph **is** a state machine with a replayable solution path — natively
intent-loggable and daily-seedable (a new suspect/clue arrangement per seed) in a way arcade
genres are not. That is not asserted fresh here; it is corroborated directly by
`farstone-qbn-design.md`, which is the house's one existing piece of design work closest to this
shape and worth citing precisely rather than gesturally:

- Farstone's Building Permit #23 already demonstrates the exact mechanism a mystery's evidence
  needs: a quality (the permit's window-state) settling to a value **nobody scripted** — "the
  branch is a property of the bilattice join... triggered by one `declareConverse` binding made
  once" (`farstone-qbn-design.md` §1a). A piece of evidence that is simultaneously alibi-confirmed
  and alibi-contradicted is not a special case a mystery engine has to hand-code; it is the same
  ⊤-state abrash/durante already render as a designed mechanic (§1 above) and Farstone already
  settles as a storylet.
- The quality taxonomy `farstone-qbn-design.md` §4 reads directly off real committed data —
  **append-only trained stat**, **decaying need**, **derived-not-stored**, **contested/⊤-legal**,
  **relational**, **world-clock-derived** — maps onto a mystery's own state almost without
  translation: a suspect's alibi is world-clock-derived (where were they at what hour, per a real
  schedule, the way Farstone's NPCs already have `intends` reflexes and located-in routes,
  §1a/§7); the relationship between two suspects (`rival`, `opinion-of`) is the same relational
  family already committed in `farstone-harbor/world/you.jsonl`; and — the load-bearing one — a
  piece of evidence that both supports and contradicts a suspect is contested/⊤-legal, the exact
  family the house substrate already handles as a first-class value rather than an error state.
- The storylet kinship is real, not decorative: `farstone-qbn-design.md`'s own verdict (§ Thesis
  verdict) is that "a quality settling to a value nobody scripted, surfaced as content, is the
  actual mechanism" for QBN work generally — a whodunit's "the evidence adds up" moment is the
  identical shape.

**Proposing the first mystery's shape (chassis only, no story).** Keep the Colonel's
Bequest/Laura Bow spine — a bounded cast in one location, real-time-derived schedules, a
detective protagonist — and build it on the substrate `farstone-qbn-design.md` §6 already judged
correct for this kind of work: the **current, live fizzos** (assertions-trace + Belnap-FOUR fold,
one dependency, `@lenticule-science/metrologic`), not the retired tab/EAVT lineage the old Farstone MUD content
was authored against. Concretely:

1. **Suspects carry schedules as world-clock-derived cells** (the same shape Farstone's tide and
   permit-window state already use) — where a suspect is, and what they are doing, is a pure
   function of the case's world-clock, not a hand-scripted cutscene per hour.
2. **Evidence is append-only witnessed fact**, gathered by the player the same way abrash/durante
   append predicate/deny evidence — an alibi witness, a physical clue, a contradiction found
   later, each a row in the trace, never overwritten.
3. **An accusation is a settle-check against the fold**, not a multiple-choice pick: the player's
   gathered evidence either settles cleanly to t against one suspect, or exposes that the case as
   currently gathered is legitimately ⊤ (contradictory, insufficient) — and a good detective
   should recognize that and keep investigating rather than force an accusation. This mirrors
   Obsidian's own binary-argument ending mechanic (concept 2, above) but repurposed as a fair-play
   mystery convention: the game can *honestly* tell the player "you don't have it yet," because
   the underlying logic already distinguishes settled-true from held-contradiction as different,
   legal states.
4. **Daily-seeded cases**, reusing one engine across many finite, bounded mysteries — matching the
   house's portfolio-economics argument directly (`the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §4.2: "many
   small, finished, polished, shared-substrate games... strictly dominates the hit-chasing
   strategy") rather than authoring one long game.

**Smallest real step.** A three-suspect, single-location micro-case: author suspect schedules and
a handful of evidence facts against fizzos's real module surface (`world.mjs`, `predication.mjs`,
`world-clock.mjs`), build the accusation-settle mechanic (does the gathered evidence fold to t on
the right suspect, or does it legitimately hold at ⊤), and confirm the case is solvable and the
"insufficient evidence" state is honestly distinguishable from "wrong suspect" — proving the
mechanic in the smallest unit before any prose, red herrings, or a real story are written, the
same discipline `farstone-qbn-design.md` §6 already prescribes for Farstone's own permit storylet.

**Staircase tier.** Owner-named, ranked #1 in the research digest's gap list; naturally sequenced
just after (or alongside) Farstone's own smallest real step, since both share the live-fizzos
substrate and the assertions-trace/settle mechanism — this could plausibly be the second thing
built on that engine, not a separate initiative. Shelf-wise it sits with The Deep alongside
Farstone (shared engine kinship) though its player-facing register (bounded, finished mystery
cases) is closer to The Puzzle Den's done-ness contract than to an open MUD.

**Honest risk.** Two real ones. First, the same prose-at-volume risk `farstone-qbn-design.md` §5
names for Farstone generally applies here with extra force — a good mystery needs real red
herrings, suspect dialogue, and alibi text at genuine volume and quality, and nothing in the house
corpus has yet demonstrated that volume (the existing Farstone prose is good at small scale, ~30
rooms, single-pass; a mystery needs branching, quality-gated text per suspect per evidence state,
which is a different and larger authoring problem, not yet attempted anywhere in this estate).
Second, a real design-craft risk distinct from the engine question: an evidence-graph
settle-mechanic guarantees a *fair* mystery (the player can always tell whether they have enough),
but fairness is not the same thing as a *good* mystery — misdirection, character, and pacing are
authorial craft the state machine does not supply on its own, and this is squarely the
design-judgment bottleneck `the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §4.1 names as the house's actual scarce
resource, not an engineering problem this note's chassis solves by existing.

frontmatter.title: Revivals — Anvil, Obsidian, Mystery
frontmatter.description: Three compact game designs from the Sierra/LucasArts catalog audit: an Anvil-of-Dawn-lineage browser extraction crawler, an Obsidian-lineage Myst-like where the house's own math is the puzzle content, and the owner-named point-and-click mystery gap, judged for house fit against real substrate.

rooms.title: Seasons Builder Design
rooms.description: Flagship city-builder specification: Impressions-style finite scenarios x Dawn of Man material/seasonal resource management x the Lakota campaign as proof of concept — designed around the settlement moving rather than standing still, per real scholarship with an explicit honest-absence boundary. Working title only; proposes 'Seasonal Round' as a real name for the owner to accept or replace.
rooms.body:
# Seasons Builder Design

Working file name only (`seasons-builder-design.md`, per the task); this document proposes a real
name in §0. Fuses three sources named in `sierra-lucasarts-lineage-brief.md` §1 and dated
2026-08-19: Impressions Games' finite-scenario/campaign structure (Caesar/Pharaoh/Zeus lineage,
per this session's catalog research digest Part 1 and Part 4), Dawn of Man's material/seasonal
resource management (same digest, Part 4), and the Lakota campaign as proof-of-concept (owner,
recorded verbatim in the lineage brief: *"I'm Lakota and encourage you to use whatever scholarship
available, that can be our first campaign to prove the concept"*). Grounded against the Lakota
campaign sourcebook digest compiled this session (cited throughout as "the sourcebook digest"),
cross-checked in this session against five of its most load-bearing primary files, read directly at
the paths given in each citation below — where a citation traces only through the digest and was
not independently re-read this session, it is marked so.

## 0. Proposed name

**Seasonal Round.** Not decorative: "the seasonal round" is the scholarship's own technical term
for Plains band movement through the year (sourcebook digest Part 2.1; the in-repo corpus's own
`annual-cycle.md`, read directly — see §2 below), and "a round" is also the natural word for one
turn of a campaign — one scenario, one year, one pass through spring→summer→autumn→winter. The
title names the game's actual core mechanic (the calendar the settlement moves through) rather
than a decorative genre word, matching the house's naming discipline elsewhere (Crucible names
what you do, Hinterland names where you start). Working title only; the owner may replace it.

## 1. Core loop

**A band, not a city.** The player does not lay down permanent buildings on a fixed map tile — the
player manages a **tiyóšpaye** (extended-family band), the smallest Lakota polity-unit, whose
identity persists across camp moves (`tiyospaye.md`, read directly at
`.../lakota-services-section/content/text/glossary/lakota/discharging/library/predicating/library/positing/library/settling/library/hacking/lakotaean-governance/philA/code/structures/tiyospaye.md`
— hereafter cited by filename only, all under that same `lakota-services-section` tree unless
noted). The loop, one season at a time:

1. **Read the season.** Each of the four seasonal windows opens different subsistence and
   ceremonial obligations (spring dispersal/small hunts, summer confederacy gathering/big hunt,
   autumn final hunts/storage, winter stable camp/teaching) — `annual-cycle.md`.
2. **Discharge owes-cells.** The band's members carry standing kin-obligations (§3) that the
   season's available activities let them discharge — gathering discharges a food-obligation,
   winter storytelling discharges a teaching-obligation, and so on (`kin-obligation-firing.md`).
   This is the resource-and-labor allocation act that in Impressions is a walker route and in Dawn
   of Man is a work-assignment; here it is choosing which owed virtue gets acted on with the
   season's available means.
3. **Move or hold.** At each season boundary the band decides whether to move camp (following
   the herd, joining a larger camp-circle for summer, retreating to a customary winter place) or
   hold. Movement cost is paid in material (see §4) and in time (a season is the unit of the
   campaign clock).
4. **Convene or fission.** At summer, the tiyóšpaye may camp with others as an **oyáte**, or at
   Bloketu with the full **Oceti Šakówiŋ** confederacy scale; at any point a tiyóšpaye that has
   outgrown what one head can hold may fission into two (`tiyospaye.md` §"Identity, withdrawal, and
   continuity" — "when a tiyóšpaye grows past sustainable size, a subset of members withdraws
   together and forms a new tiyóšpaye"). Scale is a player choice with real tradeoffs (§3), not a
   building-tier unlock.
5. **The year closes.** At Waníyetu (winter) the band's keeper selects the year's one
   most-distinctive event for the winter count (§6) and the campaign clock advances to next
   spring, or the scenario's win/loss condition resolves (§2).

There is no "city" in the Impressions/Zeus sense of a persisting footprint the player defends and
beautifies. The genre's core assumption — that the settlement is the fixed thing and resources flow
to it — is inverted: **the settlement is the thing that moves, and the calendar decides where it can
be.** This is stated as the campaign's mechanical identity, not smoothed over, per the task's own
framing; §9 discusses the risk this creates.

## 2. Scenario / campaign structure (Impressions-style finite missions, moving through time)

Per the lineage brief: "finite scenarios, campaign structure, win conditions per mission" — not an
endless sandbox. A **scenario** is one data-defined mission (§8): a starting tiyóšpaye roster, a
starting season and year, a resource/tech baseline, a map of named camp-sites and travel costs
between them, and an explicit win/loss condition. A **campaign** is an ordered sequence of
scenarios spanning historical epochs, each scenario's ending state (population, standing,
winter-count record) optionally seeding the next.

The Lakota campaign's epoch sequence, corroborated independently by both the in-repo corpus and the
web-scholarship survey (sourcebook digest Part 2.7, citing Nick Estes ★, *Our History Is the
Future*, 2019, and matched by `annual-cycle.md` §"Disruption of the cycle," read directly):

1. **Pre-horse river-valley scenario** — small-scale seasonal round, dog-travois hauling limits
   (§5), trade contact with the Missouri River village hub (§4).
2. **Horse-epoch scenario(s)** — the mounted buffalo economy at full scale; the technology epoch
   transition itself is playable (§5).
3. **Treaty era / Black Hills (Pȟahá Sápa) loss scenario** — win condition reframed, see below.
4. **Reservation confinement / cadence-disruption scenario** — the annual cycle's structural
   breakdown (`annual-cycle.md` §"Disruption of the cycle": confinement to fixed land, sun-dance
   criminalization 1881–1934, buffalo extermination, boarding-school separation) is the scenario's
   actual subject matter, not flavor text around a generic "hard mode."
5. **Reclamation scenario** — buffalo restoration via the InterTribal Buffalo Council (est. 1991),
   sun-dance restoration after the 1978 American Indian Religious Freedom Act, winter-count
   reconstitution — `annual-cycle.md` §"The contemporary reclamation," read directly, names all
   three by name.

**Win conditions cannot be a uniform "conquer/optimize" template across this arc**, and this
document does not claim to have solved that problem — it is named plainly as the campaign's
central design risk in §9. What can be stated now: scenarios 1–2 use conventional
survival/prosperity win conditions (the band ends the scenario at a named population and standing
threshold, per §4's no-property/no-surplus economy — "standing," not accumulated wealth, is the
correct win metric per `no-surplus-cell-firing.md`, read directly, §"Consequences (b)"). Scenarios 3
onward require win conditions built around *endurance, adaptation, and continuity of the annual
cycle's structure under disruption* rather than victory over an opposing side — e.g., a
reservation-confinement scenario's "win" is keeping the winter count continuous and enough
owes-cells discharged that the tiyóšpaye's identity survives to the next scenario, not defeating an
enemy faction. This reframing is proposed, not fully specified; it is the single largest open
design problem in this document.

## 3. Kinship obligations as the economy

This is the campaign's most directly citable mechanic, and unusually, its source material is
**already formalized as a state-machine** — the in-repo Lakota theory section describes kin-work
allocation as "cells" that "fire" under named closure rules, which maps close to directly onto the
house's own Cartridge State/Intent/Event shape (§7), not by analogy but because both are read
directly from the same files below.

- **No dispatch, no authority, no wage.** Read directly from `kin-obligation-firing.md`: a kin-cell
  between two agents automatically fires an "owes-\<virtue\>-to" cell — no manager assigns the
  work, no contract exists. "Work flows through kin or it does not flow." The four virtues that can
  be owed are wówačhantognaka (generosity), wóksape (wisdom), wóohitika (bravery), and
  wówačhiŋtȟaŋka (fortitude) — named directly in the file's own morphism definition.
- **Discharge, not payment.** An owes-cell resolves when the agent's conduct (a hunt, a teaching
  session, a gift) discharges it — there is no numeric wage transaction. Mechanically: the player
  does not "spend gold to hire a worker"; the player chooses which of the band's many standing
  obligations gets acted on this turn, and the season gates which actions are available to act on
  which obligation (`kin-obligation-firing.md` §"Multiple owes-cells": "spring-gathering discharges
  owes-wówačhantognaka-to-tiyóšpaye on the food side; sun-dance preparation discharges
  owes-wóohitika-to-polity; winter-teaching discharges owes-wóksape-to-younger-kin").
- **No surplus, no property, no accumulation.** Read directly from `no-surplus-cell-firing.md`: the
  closure-rule system this corpus formalizes contains no rule that installs a "surplus-produced"
  cell — the proof traces through the actual rule set (W1–W7) and shows none produces a
  numeric-value-comparison consequent. The design consequence stated directly in the source: "wealth
  ... measured in standing ... and in gifted-out items ... not in accumulated-property cells." **The
  game therefore has no bankable currency and no score built from hoarded material** — the player's
  win-condition-relevant number is standing (kin-network size, discharge-completion rate,
  winter-count continuity), never a stockpile total. This is a hard mechanical constraint, not
  flavor text, and it is the one place this design deliberately refuses a genre convention (the
  Impressions/Dawn-of-Man games both track a storable resource total as a core number) because the
  cited source states plainly that the tradition's own economy does not have that shape.
- **What trade is, instead.** Cross-polity exchange (with the Missouri River village hub, §4)
  is explicitly gift-class with continuing-relation expectations under this same source
  (`no-surplus-cell-firing.md` §"What this does not entail": "the cells installed by Lakota-European
  trade fire under $\mathcal{S}_\mathrm{wolak}$'s gift-economy rules ... when conducted properly").
  Trading with an outside partner therefore installs a standing kin-of-trade relationship the
  player can call on again, not a one-off market transaction with a price the player optimizes.

## 4. Resource model — material chains, seasons, real citations per mechanic

Dawn of Man's contribution per the catalog research digest (Part 4): "real material chains + real
seasonal pressure ... perishability is load-bearing ... tech ages gate the resource graph itself."
Each mechanic below is cited individually, per the task's own requirement, and cut if it cannot be.

| Mechanic | What it does | Citation |
|---|---|---|
| Seasonal subsistence windows | What's gatherable/huntable shifts by season (spring small-game/early plants; summer big hunt; autumn final hunts/storage; winter stable, no fresh subsistence) | `annual-cycle.md`, read directly, per-season breakdown |
| The buffalo hunt as a governed cycle, not a resource node | scout → council → akicita-installation (temporary, hunt-scoped police authority) → hunt → gift-flow distribution → akicita-revocation (automatic at hunt's end) | `buffalo-hunt-coordination.md`, read directly, full cycle §"The cycle" |
| No property over the herd | The bison (Tȟatȟáŋka / *Pte Oyate*) carry kin-standing, not resource-standing — hunting is a relation, not extraction; there is no tax on the kill and no wage for the akicita | `buffalo-hunt-coordination.md` §"What is not in the cycle," read directly |
| Gift-flow distribution | The kill belongs to whoever made it but *flows* through the tiyóšpaye by the generosity virtue — a distribution mechanic, not an inventory-to-warehouse mechanic | `buffalo-hunt-coordination.md` §"Distribution step," read directly |
| Perishability / storage as a season-crossing act | Wasná (pemmican) production at autumn is what makes winter survivable — a real Dawn-of-Man-style perishable-to-bankable conversion, not an abstract stockpile | `annual-cycle.md`'s autumn entry ("stocking of dried meat"), read directly, corroborated by sourcebook digest Part 2.2's material-chain inventory (hide, sinew, bone, horn, hoof, bladder — general Plains-ethnography sources, not Lakota-authored, used here only for the generic material-use inventory, not for any claim specific to Lakota practice) |
| Material chain: hide → tipi/clothing, sinew → cordage, bone → tools | Standard Plains-ethnography material-use inventory | Sourcebook digest Part 2.2 (SDSU library guide, Lewis & Clark project, Nebraska Studies — secondary, non-Lakota-authored web sources; flagged in the sourcebook digest itself as generic confirmation, not a Lakota-specific claim, used here only for the physical-object list, never for the distribution rule, which is the cited Lakota-specific mechanic above) |
| Trade network: Mandan/Hidatsa/Arikara hub, Assiniboine/Cree middlemen | A second, non-Lakota-specific material channel — garden produce and flint for meat/hides; horse-for-gun chains after contact | Sourcebook digest Part 2.4, corroborated Wikipedia/WyoHistory/NPS survey — standard academic material, framed in this doc as "the wider Plains system the Lakota traded into," kept distinct from the gift-economy mechanic above per §3's citation |
| Buffalo extermination as a scenario-ending mechanism, not a difficulty slider | The reservation-confinement scenario's resource collapse is specifically the removal of the buffalo as an entity-class from the hunt-cycle's substrate, not a generic "resources scarce" debuff | `buffalo-hunt-coordination.md` §"The buffalo-extermination as substrate-attack," read directly |

## 5. The horse as a technology epoch

Not a building-tier unlock — a **change in what the resource graph and the movement model even
are**, matching Dawn of Man's tech-age gating (catalog digest Part 4) rather than Impressions'
fixed-throughput buildings.

- **Dating.** Spanish-descended horses reach the northern Plains (Lakota/Crow/Cheyenne territory)
  roughly 1700–1750s; full mounted nomadism by the mid-1700s; the horse-culture epoch runs roughly
  1750s–1870s before Indian Wars/reservation confinement end it — Pekka Hämäläinen, "The Rise and
  Fall of Plains Indian Horse Cultures" (*Journal of American History*, 2003) and *The Comanche
  Empire* (Yale, 2008), per sourcebook digest Part 2.3. This is a non-Lakota-authored academic
  source used here only for the epoch's dating, not for any claim about Lakota interior experience
  of the transition.
- **The mechanical change.** Pre-horse, band mobility and hauling capacity are dog-travois limited —
  smaller loads, smaller camp moves, smaller sustainable tiyóšpaye size before fission becomes
  necessary. Post-horse, hauling capacity and travel range both increase substantially, which is
  the actual epoch-defining mechanic (not "faster movement" as a flat speed buff, but "how much of
  the band's material and how many members one camp move can carry" as a step change in the
  resource-graph's own capacity ceiling) — matching Dawn of Man's "tech ages gate the resource graph
  itself, not just building tiers" per the catalog digest. This specific *mechanical* framing (load
  capacity as the epoch's binding constraint) is this document's own design inference from the
  dating source above, not a claim traceable to a named source describing exact travois-vs-horse
  capacity numbers — flagged honestly as inference, not citation, and worth a real historical
  capacity figure being sourced before implementation.
- **Acquisition, not tech-tree research.** Consistent with §3's no-property/gift-economy framing,
  horses should enter the band's resource graph through the trade-network and gift-relation
  channels already modeled (§3, §4), not through an abstract "research points" currency the genre
  convention would otherwise suggest.

## 6. The winter count as chronicle / save metaphor

**Strong, well-documented, non-ceremonial-secret structural mechanic** — the sourcebook digest's own
assessment (Part 2.6), corroborated directly this session in `annual-cycle.md`'s winter-count
paragraph, which is where the mechanic is grounded for this document:

> "The winter-count (waniyetu-iyawapi) is the substrate-record-keeping mechanism for the annual
> cycle: each year's most-distinctive event is recorded as one named year-cell ... The winter-count
> is the polity's distributed-memory of its history — each waniyetu-iyawapi keeper holds a
> continuous record going back many generations." — `annual-cycle.md`, read directly.

Standard scholarly reference for the form: Candace S. Greene & Russell Thornton (eds.), *The Year
the Stars Fell: Lakota Winter Counts at the Smithsonian* (Smithsonian/Nebraska, 2007) — named as the
in-repo corpus's own primary citation and independently confirmed by the sourcebook digest's web
survey (Part 2.6) as the standard comprehensive reference; roughly 100 known Plains winter counts,
at least 14 Lakota examples held at the Smithsonian. Garrick Mallery's 1893 *Picture-Writing of the
American Indians* is the earliest scholarly treatment but is cited by the source material itself
with an explicit caveat about that period's colonial framing — carried here with the same caveat,
never as a standalone authority.

**Mechanic:** each completed year (one campaign "round," §0) produces exactly one winter-count
glyph, chosen — communally, in the source tradition; in-engine, algorithmically from the year's
actual recorded events — as that year's single most-distinctive event from the real intent log the
player generated (a hard winter with losses, a first horse acquired, a notable hunt, a scenario's
win/loss). This is not a cosmetic skin over a generic save slot: it is built as a structural
homage, credited by name in the game's own credits to Greene & Thornton and the winter-count
tradition, per the sourcebook digest's own recommendation (Part 2.6: "It should be built as a
structural homage to a documented form, credited by name ... not skinned invisibly"). A named
keeper role persists across scenarios within the campaign as the continuity metaphor for "this is
your save file" — mirroring the source's "keeper holds a continuous record going back many
generations," not narrated as ceremony, only as record-keeping structure.

## 7. Determinism / replay / cartridge fit

Grounded directly in `cartridge-and-energy-bank-spec.md` (read this session), which every game in
the fleet already implements or targets. Seasonal Round fits the `Cartridge<State, Intent>`
interface without a new contract shape:

- **State** — the tiyóšpaye roster (members, kin-relations, standing owes-cells per §3), current
  season/year, camp location, material inventory by category (§4), tech-epoch flags (§5), the
  winter-count log (§6), and the active scenario's win/loss progress.
- **Intent kinds** — `{kind: "move-camp", to: siteId}`, `{kind: "discharge-obligation", owesCellId,
  action}`, `{kind: "hunt", herdId}`, `{kind: "gift", from, to, amount}`, `{kind: "trade", partner,
  offer}`, `{kind: "tiyospaye-fission", splitMembers}`, `{kind: "advance-season"}` — all pure data
  per the cartridge contract's requirement (§1.2 of the spec), applied by a pure `applyIntent(state,
  intent)`.
- **Events** — `SeasonAdvanced`, `HuntCompleted`, `GiftFlowed`, `WinterCountGlyphSelected`,
  `EpochAdvanced`, `ScenarioResolved` — the same "events are what a replay/verify step ... consumes"
  discipline the spec states for onestone's `CascadeStep` and weiqi's semantic annotator events.
- **Replay** — `defaultReplay(seed, intents)` reconstructs the full campaign from nothing but
  `(seed, IntentLog)`, exactly as the spec provides for any cartridge implementer; a
  `(seed, configId, IntentLog)` triple is a complete portable record of one playthrough, including
  its own winter count.
- **SeedPolicy** — the campaign mode uses `"client-supplied"` or `"on-demand"` (a chosen scenario,
  played at the player's pace); the daily-challenge mode (§8's counterpart, below) uses
  `"daily-utc"` — the spec's own `dailySeed(date, variantId)` pattern, named directly after
  solitaire's existing implementation.
- **Energy hooks** — optional per the spec's own discipline ("a game that never references
  energy-bank simply omits this key"). The campaign mode has no legitimate energy-bank binding: §3
  establishes the campaign has no bankable currency by design, so wiring it to the shared
  energy/credits ledger would misrepresent what the mechanic is. The **daily-challenge mode** may
  legitimately bind `EnergyHooks` for a satoshi-settled leaderboard the way ruinfold-daily does
  (`gaming-enterprises-vision.md` §6), since a single bounded daily scenario has a natural
  score-comparable outcome (turns survived, obligations discharged) that a payout can key off —
  this is a real, disclosed difference between the two modes, not an oversight.

## 8. Daily-challenge mode (house daily-seed pattern)

Per the lineage brief ("Daily challenges: yes, house daily-seed pattern applies") and
`cartridge-and-energy-bank-spec.md`'s `SeedPolicy: {kind: "daily-utc"}`. One bounded scenario per
day, world-wide same seed: a single season or single year drawn from the campaign's own scenario
data (§2, §9's smallest-step scenario is itself the natural first daily challenge), scored on
obligations discharged and winter-count continuity rather than a hoarded-resource total (consistent
with §3's no-surplus constraint). Sits on the Today page alongside ruinfold's daily dungeon and
Crucible's daily tangle, per `the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §2's "one 'today' page: today's ruinfold
dungeon, today's crucible tangle, today's weiqi problem."

## 9. Render approach on the house ladder

The task brief names "SVG-first render ladder with the legacy abrash raycaster ... and durante ...
as recovery candidates." Checked directly against `estate-map-2026-08-19.md` (read this session,
its own item 5): **"render ladder" is not an actual corpus term for a genre progression** — the map
document states this explicitly, distinguishing an SVG-first *rendering discipline* (proposed for
Crucible in `gaming-enterprises-vision.md` §7) from the separate arnold→daleske/tsander→abrash
*render-substrate* dependency chain that durante (a first-person Quake-like) sits on. Stated
honestly rather than forced to fit: **Seasonal Round is a top-down/map game (camp sites, travel
routes, a seasonal-round map), not a first-person game, so it has no real dependency on the
abrash/durante raycaster lineage** — that substrate is FPS-shaped (grid position + facing, one ray
per screen column) and does not serve a camp-and-map interface. The render approach this design
actually calls for is the **SVG-first discipline** established for Crucible (`gaming-enterprises-vision.md`
§7: "SVG-first presentation per the render ladder" — kept here despite the map document's naming
correction, since the discipline itself, not the "ladder" label, is what's real and reusable): a
map of named camp-sites and routes, seasonal color/weather treatment, and the winter-count strip
(§6) are all natural SVG content — vector shapes, no texture/3D pipeline needed, consistent with
Crucible's own render choice for a comparable top-down puzzle/board interface. This is a
correction to the task brief's framing, made because the honest answer is a better fit than forcing
the named substrate to apply.

## 10. Content pipeline: scenarios as data

Per the house discipline named directly in `the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §2 ("the games stay
finished ... additions are content data, not code") and demonstrated by
`cartridge-and-energy-bank-spec.md`'s `CartridgeConfig` shape (solitaire's `VARIANT_LIST`,
onestone's `LEVELS` — "a service may publish more than one manifest, or one manifest with a
`configs` slot"). A scenario is a data record, not a code branch:

```ts
interface ScenarioData {
  readonly id: string;                    // e.g. "lakota-pre-horse-01"
  readonly displayName: string;
  readonly epoch: string;                 // "pre-horse" | "horse" | "treaty" | "confinement" | "reclamation"
  readonly startingSeason: Season;
  readonly startingYear: number;
  readonly startingRoster: TiyospayeSeed;
  readonly campSites: readonly CampSite[];  // named locations + travel costs between them
  readonly techBaseline: TechFlags;         // horse present/absent, etc. — see §5
  readonly winCondition: WinCondition;      // standing/continuity-shaped per §2, not a uniform template
  readonly citedMechanics: readonly string[]; // which §3-§6 mechanics this scenario activates
}
```

A future culture's campaign (per the lineage brief §1: "subsequent cultures' campaigns remain owner
decisions about scope and involvement") is new `ScenarioData` plus, where its own material chain
differs, new content-chain data — never a new engine. The engine's actual code (season
progression, owes-cell firing, hunt-cycle resolution, winter-count/chronicle selection, cartridge
replay) is culture-agnostic; every culturally-specific fact lives in scenario data with its own
citation, exactly as §4's table requires per-mechanic. This is also the honest-absence boundary's
enforcement point (§11): a scenario file with an uncited cultural mechanic is a scenario file that
should not ship, and a content-authoring checklist (not yet built — flagged as debt in §11) should
check for citations the same way this document does.

## 11. Load-bearing vs. flavor disclosure

Per `house-specification-standard.md` §13/§14's required disclosure convention.

**Load-bearing (real mechanics, cited, enforced in engine logic):**

- Seasonal subsistence windows and the four-season structure (`annual-cycle.md`) — determines what
  intents are even legal in a given season.
- Tiyóšpaye/oyáte/Oceti Šakówiŋ scale and fission (`tiyospaye.md`) — a real state transition, not
  cosmetic grouping.
- The buffalo hunt's full governed cycle including automatic akicita-revocation
  (`buffalo-hunt-coordination.md`) — the hunt intent's state machine is this cycle, not a generic
  "gather resource" action.
- No-surplus/no-property economy (`no-surplus-cell-firing.md`) — enforced by *not implementing* a
  bankable-currency field in `State` at all; this is a refusal, checkable by its absence from the
  schema, not a policy statement.
- Kin-obligation firing as the labor-allocation system (`kin-obligation-firing.md`) — owes-cells are
  real `State` fields with real discharge intents, not a flavor label over a generic quest system.
- The winter-count chronicle mechanic (§6) — a real derived view over the actual `IntentLog`, not an
  authored narrative.

**Flavor / structural-only (named honestly, not simulated):**

- Sun-dance and other required-ceremony *content* — modeled only as a scheduling obligation that
  must occur or produce a recorded consequence at Bloketu; the ceremony's interior content is never
  staged, scripted, or generated (§12 point 1).
- Wakȟáŋ — trackable as a flag on a cell (a scenario or object may be marked wakȟáŋ-obligated); never
  narrated as felt sacredness (§12 point 2).
- Heyókha/vision-triggered obligations — referenced only as a scheduling fact ("this member's
  obligations renew under the thunder-presence"), per `annual-cycle.md`'s own spring entry, never as
  content to generate (§12 point 3).

**Explicitly not modeled — no mechanic in this design draws on it, and none should be added without
a citation:** the "Obsmetrologia = Lakotaean metaphysics" equivalence named in the sourcebook digest
Part 1.1. This design's use of the in-repo Lakota theory files (§3, §6) cites their *own stated
formalism* (named cells, named closure rules, already written that way by the corpus before this
document existed) — it is not, and should not be marketed as, evidence for or exercise of the
broader metaphysics-equals-mathematics claim, which per the sourcebook digest's own honesty ledger
(Part 3, point 6) has exactly one checker and no distributed verification. See §12 point 2 for why
this matters for this campaign specifically.

## 12. The honest-absence boundary

Stated plainly, per the sourcebook digest's own Part 3 and the standing house rule (lineage brief:
"no fabricated cultural content, real sources cited or gaps marked plainly as gaps ... the design
says absent rather than inventing"). **This game deliberately does not depict:**

1. **The content of the seven rites**, including the sun dance. The sourcebook's own wolakȟota
   survey states the tradition's ceremonial substrate is "only referenced, not read directly" even
   within the in-repo corpus itself. The game may model *that* a ceremony is due and *that*
   something follows from whether it occurs — never what happens inside it.
2. **Wakȟáŋ as lived or felt sacredness**, and by extension, **any claim that this game's
   mechanics are themselves a working instance of Lakota metaphysics.** The in-repo corpus's own
   caveat on its formal reading of wakȟáŋ applies with extra force to a shipped game: "the
   substrate-algebraic form is a tool, never the tradition." §11 states this as a refused framing,
   not merely an omitted feature.
3. **Vision content, dreams, and personal spiritual experience** — referenced only as scheduling
   triggers (§11), never generated or simulated as content.
4. **Anything sourced only through a non-Lakota mediator writing as if from inside the tradition**
   (Walker read raw rather than through DeMallie's editorial apparatus, Joseph Epes Brown's *The
   Sacred Pipe*, Mallery without its period-framing caveat) — usable only for structural facts
   through the same critical apparatus the corpus itself insists on, never for interior content.
5. **Anything without a named, checkable source.** Every mechanic in §3–§6 above traces to a file
   read directly this session or to a specifically named, dated source in the sourcebook digest. A
   future addition without a citation is a gap to be marked, not filled by inference — this is the
   same discipline §10's content pipeline is meant to enforce structurally, not just by convention.

**What the game legitimately can and does model**, restated from the sourcebook digest's own
closing framing (Part 3): seasonal-round movement and band fission/aggregation; the buffalo
material-chain economy including its governed hunt-cycle and gift-flow distribution; the horse-epoch
technology transition; trade-network connections to the Missouri River village hub and other Plains
nations; kinship-obligation as the resource/labor-allocation system; and the winter-count as the
literal chronicle mechanic. The historical arc — pre-horse → horse epoch → treaty/Black Hills loss →
reservation confinement/cadence-disruption → reclamation — structures the campaign's scenario
sequence honestly, per both the in-repo corpus and Nick Estes's independent scholarship, ending not
at defeat but at ongoing restoration.

## 13. Staircase placement + smallest real step

**Placement.** Per this session's own catalog research digest (Part 3): the city builder is
"already the flagship — no ranking needed, just flagged as the one genre already moving," currently
at "full design brief exists ... zero code yet." This document is that design brief. It does not
yet appear as a line in `gaming-enterprises-vision.md` §6's staircase table; that table should gain
a row once implementation begins, following the exact three-tier Now/Next/Then discipline
`house-specification-standard.md`'s roadmap-appendix format requires (falsifiable claims, never a
vibe).

**Smallest real step.** Not a full year, not the horse epoch, not multiple tiyóšpaye. **One
tiyóšpaye, one season** — the pre-horse spring dispersal scenario (§2's epoch 1) reduced to its
smallest legal slice: spring only (`annual-cycle.md`'s Wíiyaȟpeyatuya-wí window), a single starting
tiyóšpaye with a small kin-obligation set, the move-camp and discharge-obligation intents only, no
hunt-cycle, no trade, no horse. This proves the two mechanics that make this design different from
a reskinned Impressions clone — the settlement actually moving (§1) and obligations discharging
without a currency or wage (§3) — before authoring a single full year, matching the same
"prove the mechanism in the smallest unit" discipline `farstone-qbn-design.md` §6 and the Anvil
crawler design (`revivals-anvil-obsidian-mystery.md`, "one room ... proves the determinism claim ...
before any dungeon content ... is authored") both already use in this fleet.

---

## Sources read directly this session for this document

- `sierra-lucasarts-lineage-brief.md`, `gaming-enterprises-vision.md`, `the-suite-and-the-studio.md`,
  `cartridge-and-energy-bank-spec.md`, `house-specification-standard.md` §13/§14,
  `estate-map-2026-08-19.md` (item 5, the render-ladder naming correction),
  `revivals-anvil-obsidian-mystery.md`, `farstone-qbn-design.md` (structure/convention reference) —
  all under `561-group-gaming-enterprises-services-section/.../notes/`.
- `annual-cycle.md`, `buffalo-hunt-coordination.md`, `kin-obligation-firing.md`,
  `no-surplus-cell-firing.md`, `tiyospaye.md` — all under
  `science-services-section/services/philosophy-services-section/services/lakota-services-section/`,
  exact paths given inline at first citation of each.
- The Lakota campaign sourcebook digest and the Sierra/LucasArts catalog research digest, both
  compiled and supplied this session (paths/authorship as stated in the task); their own
  Sources sections (Hämäläinen 2003/2008/2019, Greene & Thornton 2007, Ella Deloria 1944, Estes
  2019, and the secondary Plains-ethnography web survey for §4's generic material-object list) are
  inherited by reference rather than re-verified line by line, except where marked above as
  independently re-read this session.

rooms.title: Semioverse State and Fediverse Client Feasibility
rooms.description: Recon and mechanical-repair note on the '561 Group Semioverse': what actually exists across four sections, what got repaired 2026-08-19, remaining structural work in priority order, and the feasibility verdict for a gamified Fediverse client with the smallest honest first step.
rooms.body:
# Semioverse State and Fediverse Client Feasibility

## Current true state

"The 561 Group Semioverse" is not one system. It is a set of disconnected,
unevenly-progressed pieces that share a name by accident more than by
design. The one real, working core is a standards-conformant Fedify-based
ActivityPub server — actor dispatch, inbox/outbox, WebFinger, NodeInfo,
signed delivery — published as `@red-cup-engineering/activitypub-services-section`,
disk version 1.0.15, under active development through 2026-08-17. It has
no live deploy target: no credentials, no reachable server, per the
project's own 2026-08-16 internal audit ("Molt Ledger"), the only genuinely
current, evidence-based status document found in this tree. It documents a
concept of x402 (recognized as a pass-through payload authority inside
nested A2A messages) but does not execute it.

Separately, a real but unfinished Solidity settlement contract
(`SemioticExchange.sol`) and its off-chain builder/replay tooling
(`semiotic-exchange-chain-services-section`) are live and mostly
test-passing, but the contract has never been compiled or deployed to any
chain.

Three other "Semioverse"-named directories — `interactive-semioverse-services-section`,
`agential-semioverse-repository-services-section`, and
`close-semioverse-gap-services-section` — turn out, on exhaustive grep and
read, to be unrelated: they are a personal markdown-vault semiotic
formalism and its documentation tooling, dormant to abandoned, containing
zero ActivityPub/x402/federation/game surface.

So: one real, live, actively-developed federation server; one real, live,
but unconnected-to-chain settlement spec; and three "Semioverse"-named
directories that are false leads. "Currently kind of broken" is accurate
specifically about *deployment* — there is no live instance anywhere — not
about code quality, since what exists mostly runs and mostly passes its
own tests.

## Section relationship map

```
                "Semioverse" — a name shared by two unrelated lineages
                ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════

LINEAGE A: personal vault formalism (DORMANT/ABANDONED — not the Fediverse project)
  interactive-semioverse-services-section
    (Heyting-algebra markdown-vault theory; legacy 2026-03-11 FastAPI/MCP
     engine, broken: missing library/, no deps)
  agential-semioverse-repository-services-section
    (governance/validation docs + runnable-but-data-less Python scripts)
  close-semioverse-gap-services-section
    (single stub file; "gap" = broken wikilinks in the vault, not
     deployment gaps)

LINEAGE B: the actual ActivityPub Fediverse project (mixed live/dead ends)
  services/engineering-services-section/services/computer-services-section/services/computer-systems-services-section/services/web-services-section/services/web-protocol-services-section/services/activitypub-services-section/lib/legacy/2026-07-20-bare-cedar-fog-koios-activitypub-service
    (retained historical state, 2026-07-19–20 burst, real Fedify server,
     no x402, EVM identity binding only)
              │  superseded by, architecturally same core
              ▼
  @red-cup-engineering/activitypub-services-section   ◄── CANONICAL, LIVE
    (disk v1.0.15, active through 2026-08-17; adds cloud/R2/A2A/RMN/
     onchain layers; documents x402 as inert pass-through concept;
     registry published only to v1.0.11 — drift)
              │  x402 is recognized here but NOT executed
              ▼
  (unexamined) x402-services-section, x402-exact-purchase-service, etc.
     — real payment logic, if any, lives here; out of scope of this recon

  semiotic-exchange-chain-services-section  — LIVE, independent of Lineage B
    SemioticExchange.sol (settlement contract spec, uncompiled/undeployed)
    + off-chain demand-induction builder (never calls the chain)
    + modeled-union-dimension (pure event-log replay, no RPC wired)
    — consumes x402 receipts as one of several evidence shapes; connects
      to Lineage B only nominally, via the shared concept of x402
      evidence, not via any shared code
```

The 2026-08-16 Molt Ledger (found while cross-checking, outside the four
assigned sections) rates the ActivityPub service mid-flight and names the
one live blocker to a running instance — which matches the top mechanical
repair item below. It is the closest thing to ground truth this tree
currently contains.

## What got repaired today (2026-08-19)

One repair was made, and its numbers were re-verified by rerunning the
tests fresh before this note was written:

**Corrected a false test-status claim in
`semiotic-exchange-chain-services-section/README.md`.** It previously
claimed all tests in the section failed with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` from a
missing `npm install`. That was wrong on every count. Rerunning `npm test`
in each of the three packages today gives:

- `semiotic-exchange-chain-services-section` (top level): **6/6 pass**
- `sovereign-membrane-admission-service`: **6/6 pass**
- `modeled-union-dimension`: **18/19 pass** — the one failure is
  `test/dimension.test.mjs`, `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` for
  `@red-cup-engineering/typed-resource-catalog/temporal-failure-normalization`,
  a package that has never been written or published anywhere in this
  tree (confirmed again today: `npm view` against the local Verdaccio
  registry 404s, and no such directory exists on disk).

That is 7 test files across the section and its two sub-services, 30 of
31 individual tests passing, and dependencies already installed from
Verdaccio — not an environment gap. The README now states these true,
reproducible counts and attributes the one real failure correctly, to a
genuinely unwritten dependency rather than a setup problem.

As a second spot-check (not previously claimed, run fresh for this note):
`@red-cup-engineering/activitypub-services-section` (disk v1.0.15) —
**39/39 pass**.

Nothing else was changed. No stale `@561-group` package pins
(math/computer/qwzspace) were found anywhere in the four sections examined
— nothing to correct there. No broken import paths were found elsewhere.

## Remaining structural work, in priority order

These are flagged, not attempted — each requires a design or infra
decision, not a mechanical fix:

1. **No deploy target for the live ActivityPub server.** No credentials,
   no reachable host, no HTTPS origin. This is the actual meaning of
   "currently kind of broken": the code runs, but nothing is running it
   anywhere reachable. The legacy VPS package (abandoned 2026-07-19–20)
   has an already-working local-disk KV/queue adapter
   (`SqliteKvStore`/`SqliteMessageQueue` on `node:sqlite`) that solves
   exactly the gap the Molt Ledger names as the active package's
   blocker — porting it forward is the highest-leverage single next step,
   because it is the one thing standing between "no live instance" and "a
   live instance." It was not ported today; this is new integration code,
   outside a strictly mechanical pass.
2. **Registry drift.** `activitypub-services-section` disk is v1.0.15;
   Verdaccio has only v1.0.11 published. A straightforward `npm publish`
   once the package owner wants it public. The Molt Ledger also flags
   roughly 188 unresolved internal-dependency pins tree-wide of the same
   shape — a larger scripted sweep, not attempted here as it wasn't in
   scope for this pass.
3. **`SemioticExchange.sol` has no compile/deploy tooling at all** — no
   Hardhat/Foundry config anywhere in its section or `lib/legacy`.
   Choosing a settlement chain and building deploy tooling is a design
   decision.
4. **x402 execution logic is unexamined.** It lives, if anywhere, in
   sibling packages (`x402-services-section`, `x402-exact-purchase-service`,
   etc.) not touched by this recon. No claim that "x402 works" is
   supportable without a dedicated pass over those.
5. **The sandboxed arrival-handler pattern may be a regression.** The
   legacy server subprocess-sandboxes the customer callback
   (`invokeAcceptedArrivalHandler`: resolved-file/non-symlink check,
   stripped environment, 30s timeout, 16MB output cap). The active
   package instead calls an injected `onActivity` callback directly
   in-process, with no subprocess boundary. Confirmed missing; whether
   this is a deliberate design shift (dependency injection replacing
   process isolation) or an unintentional loss of a security boundary is
   a judgment call for whoever owns the package, not a mechanical fix.
6. **The "Semioverse" name is disconnected from the working code.** None
   of the three dormant/abandoned "Semioverse"-named sections connect to
   the live ActivityPub or chain code, and the live ActivityPub package
   never uses the word "Semioverse" itself. Reconciling the name (or
   accepting the split, e.g. renaming the gaming client's world layer
   rather than the federation server) is a product decision.
7. **The `interactive-semioverse` Python FastAPI/MCP engine** (missing
   `library/` tree, no venv, no deps) is repairable in isolation but
   would restore an unrelated personal skill-runner server, not anything
   feeding the Fediverse-client goal. Lowest priority; likely not worth
   repair effort at all under this goal.

## Gamified Fediverse client — feasibility verdict

**What exists that helps:**
- A real ActivityPub *server*: actor dispatch, inbox/outbox, WebFinger,
  NodeInfo 2.1, signed delivery, via Fedify, currently 39/39 tests
  passing. Genuine federation plumbing, not a stub.
- A partial ActivityPub *sender*: signed-delivery/CLI tooling exists, but
  nothing found anywhere consumes an incoming federated timeline and
  renders or interprets it as anything — game world or otherwise.
- x402: conceptually scaffolded as a payload type that can ride inside a
  federated A2A message, but not executed anywhere examined. No
  challenge/response, no payment verification, no settlement witness at
  the ActivityPub layer.
- Chain settlement: a real, well-specified event-sourced contract with a
  matching off-chain builder and pure-replay reconstructor (30/31 tests
  passing), but never compiled, deployed, or connected to a live RPC.
- Game/world-rendering layer: none. An explicit grep for
  `mmorpg|game`-shaped terms across the "Semioverse"-named sections found
  nothing — no rendering layer, no world model, no game loop anywhere in
  the sections reviewed.

**What is plainly missing:**
- A live, reachable deployment of the ActivityPub server.
- Any x402 payment execution actually wired to that server.
- Any chain deployment of the settlement contract.
- Any code — not a note, not a stub — that turns federated activity into
  a game-world representation.
- A resolved decision connecting "Semioverse" branding to the working
  ActivityPub/chain code, if that connection is wanted at all.

**The smallest honest first step:** port the legacy SQLite KV/queue
adapter into `@red-cup-engineering/activitypub-services-section` and stand
up one real local devbox instance, then verify a live WebFinger → actor →
inbox → outbox round trip against an actual external Fediverse server.
That is mechanical, low-risk, and uses an already-proven pattern from the
legacy code — and it is a hard prerequisite for everything else. There is
currently no live instance to test x402 gating against, none to attach
chain settlement to, and none to render as a game world. Everything else
on this list — x402 execution, chain deployment, the game-rendering layer
itself — is genuine structural design work that should wait until that
one live instance exists, because building any of it against a server
that has never actually federated would be building on an unverified
foundation.
