rooms.title: Okaga Game Design
rooms.description: Design specification for the Okaga commission — quality-based-narrative storylets meet Discworld MUD presence meet EVE industry, wired to light-lag as the shard boundary and to channeling as a reach-not-power premium currency, with an honest single-system v1 cut.
rooms.body:
# Okaga Game Design

> "Picture quality narrative meets Discworld MUD meets EVE." As hard scifi as it can be, with
> exactly one conceit: some people can channel energy from outside the dimensions of this world
> to do warp travel and other forms of accelerating the arrow of time. Ships otherwise reach only
> ~0.2c. A galactic confederacy. A few billion players shouldn't skew galactic economics.
> — the commission, owner, 2026-08-19

This document designs the game. It does not re-derive the setting or re-argue the system fit —
those are done, and cited by section number throughout: `okaga-worldbook.md` (physics, the one
conceit priced, the gazetteer) and `okaga-substrate-fit-brief.md` (which house system carries
which commission pillar, and what's real versus proposed in each). This document's own job is
the part neither of those did: turn the setting and the fit-read into a tick schedule, a storylet
schema, a cast, a content pipeline, and a v1 that could actually be built next — small enough to
be honest, large enough to prove all three of the Triple at once.

**Canon-tag legend, inherited unchanged from the worldbook §0**: **OWNER CANON** (said, in-repo,
about Okaga specifically), **OWNER-KEPT** (2023 tone material, not load-bearing), **HOUSE
SUBSTRATE** (a real system pointed at Okaga), **NEW CANON PROPOSED** (this document's own
invention). Nothing below contradicts an OWNER CANON sentence from the worldbook's §0 list. Where
this document invents game-design specifics beyond what the worldbook already priced — exact
tick ratios, a settlement's name, a cast roster — those inventions are tagged **NEW CANON
PROPOSED** or **NEW DESIGN PROPOSED** (a design choice with no fictional-truth claim attached,
freely revisable without touching canon) as they occur.

---

## 1. The Triple, wired precisely

The commission names three genres. Each one already has a real house carrier — the
substrate-fit-brief found them (§1–§2) — but "a carrier exists" and "the three carriers compose
into one playable loop" are different claims. This section makes the second claim, concretely.

### 1.1 Quality-based narrative — storylets on the farstone-qbn chassis, Rimworld-textured

`farstone-qbn-design.md` §1a proved the mechanism this game needs, in committed code, not as a
metaphor: a quality is a settled EAVT cell (current fizzos: `world.mjs`'s assertion trace plus
`predication.mjs`'s functional-predicate machinery), and a storylet is a situation the bilattice
join makes visible without anyone authoring an `if`-branch — Permit #23 aging into a contested ⊤
state because `within-window` was declared to have the converse `overdue`, once, is the whole
mechanism. That note's §4 also sorted every quality the corpus actually tracks into six families
(append-only trained stat, decaying need, derived-not-stored, contested/⊤-legal, relational,
world-clock-derived). Okaga's qualities are read off that same union, not invented fresh:

| family | Okaga instance |
|---|---|
| decaying need | Apotei Orchard's blight-progression cell; a settler's `need:hunger`/`need:rest` under a REQ shortage (OWNER CANON texture, worldbook §5.1) |
| contested/⊤-legal | the signalling array's `within-window` maintenance predicate × its declared converse `overdue` — the direct Okaga transplant of Permit #23, see §10 |
| world-clock-derived | today's array phasing-coil calibration state, the Orchard's irrigation cycle, whatever stands in for tide/weather at Buinga Station (all pure functions of `world-clock.mjs`'s `phaseAt`/`seasonAt`/`weatherAt`, recomputed each settle, never stored) |
| append-only trained stat | a settler's skill-by-use record (`skills.mjs`), a channeler's cumulative χ drawn (relevant only once §3's premium currency exists) |
| derived-not-stored | a channeler's apparent Toll-age (worldbook §2.5) — **must** be this family, not a hand-authored number; see §11's risk note |
| relational | `reputation.mjs`'s `standing(actor, faction)` — a settler's standing with the North Sanazi Confederacy or an unnamed rival Union |

**Rimworld texture is the local storylet's whole register**, and it is already the register of
"The Okaga"'s own draft scenes (worldbook §5.1, quoting Dapu's Scene 3 blight and Skah's Scene 2
seed-envelope requisition directly). A storylet in this game is never "the Confederacy declares
war" — it is "the irrigation line to the east terrace is down and there are eleven seed envelopes
left in the box," gated on and modifying exactly the qualities in the table above. This is the
correct scale match: §5.1 of the worldbook already argues Frontier/Established-Colony content
should almost never involve the Patrol or the Counting House arriving in time to matter — the
local cast solves it or doesn't, before help is even in transit. Storylet authoring inherits that
discipline directly: **no storylet at settlement scale is permitted to resolve on an off-screen
institution's timely intervention.**

### 1.2 Discworld MUD — presence, rooms, talk, the cast as real inhabitants

Presence is rooms: the gazetteer's places (worldbook §6.1 — Apotei Orchard, Buinga Station) are
fizzos locations exactly the way `farstone-qbn-design.md` §3 proposes reading a pyfars `place`
record as a room — the compiler's job (§7 below) generalizes the same way. Talk and social state
ride `social.mjs`/`communicating.mjs`; local governance and standing ride `progression.mjs`'s
law/support/enact primitives (a real fit for the North Sanazi Confederacy's Union structure,
worldbook §6.2) and `reputation.mjs`'s standing ledger.

**The cast is the load-bearing half of this pillar**, and it is not aspirational plumbing — it is
a structural fact `farstone-qbn-design.md` §7 already established: a Farstone NPC record (an
`intends` cell mapping perceived state to action) is *already*, in shape, indistinguishable from
an agent player's own decision loop, and `the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §2 names exactly this
pattern as the house's differentiator (*"named recurring agent players who actually play, by the
same intent-log API as humans... peers-not-pets is already the architecture"*). Concretely for
Okaga: a cast member playing a Union delegate, a Counting House clerk, or a loom operator submits
the identical `Intent` shape (`@561-group/cartridge/intent-log`) a human player's client would —
`move`, `talk`, `trade`, `propose-law` — validated at the same trust boundary, with no privileged
NPC-only API. §6 below names a starting roster.

### 1.3 EVE — industry, trade, contracts across light-lag; the wallet

The market half already exists, twice over, and the substrate-fit-brief only cited one of the two
carriers. It found `@561-group/energy-bank`'s `transfer`/`createPool`/`sellEnergy` (§1) as the
player-to-player economic primitive. What it did not have occasion to cite — a fresh read for this
document — is that **the current fizzos ships its own `market.mjs`, `crafting.mjs`, and
`progression.mjs`** (verified directly: `src/market.mjs` defines `initializeMarket` over
per-ware `price`/`base-price`/`stock` functional cells; `src/crafting.mjs` defines recipe-shaped
input→output transformation; `src/progression.mjs` carries a propose/support/enact law cycle).
This means Okaga's *local* Rimworld economy — the Orchard's requisition manifest, a REQ line's
price drifting with stock, a settler crafting a repaired irrigation part from scavenged parts —
already has a native, in-engine home, distinct from and complementary to the *player-to-player*
economy `energy-bank` carries. The design split: **`fizzos market.mjs` prices the settlement's
own goods against itself (the local Rimworld shop); `energy-bank` moves `ENERGY` between real
identities (the EVE-shaped player market, trades, pooled ventures, contracts)** — two real
systems, cleanly separated by who's on each side of the transaction, neither needing to be built
from scratch.

**Contracts across light-lag** are where EVE's texture actually shows up as a mechanic, not a
vibe: a contract posted at one settlement is not visible or executable anywhere else until the
light-lag delay (§2) has actually elapsed — this is the concrete form of "the market crash arrives
years later as history" applied to an active player market rather than passive news. **The
wallet is `energy-bank`'s ledger, and the earn-only discipline is restated as a hard line, not a
suggestion**: quoted directly from its own README, *"there is no random-outcome, stake-at-risk, or
house-edge mechanic anywhere in it... this posture is a property of every module in this package,
not a flag one can turn off."* Okaga inherits that posture unmodified for its `ENERGY` account;
§3 below is the whole design argument for why the one conceit's separate `chron` currency does not
get to relax it.

## 2. Light-lag as architecture

### 2.1 Spacelike separation is the shard boundary, not an authored zone map

The substrate-fit-brief's key finding (§3–§4) is the load-bearing fact this whole section builds
on, and it is worth restating in one sentence because everything below is an application of it:
**two regions of the setting that have not yet exchanged a lightspeed signal or a warp-capable
ship are, by the commission's own stated physics, provably non-interfering** — not by a
server-assignment decision, by the same Lorentzian causal structure `shrimp-ecology-brief-v2.md`
§1 proved things about, applied to a setting where it is the literal physics rather than an
imposed design choice. Two systems in that relationship do not need to reconcile state with each
other at all — not eventually, structurally never, until a signal or a ship actually connects
their light cones. **This is the shard model, and it costs nothing to implement beyond getting
the delivery-tick math right (§2.2)**, because the causal partition is already free, supplied by
distance itself.

### 2.2 A formula for "propagates at c," made precise

Everything in this section reduces to one function, computed once the moment an event is
authored, never touched again:

```
delivery_tick(event, distance_ly, carriage) =
    origin_tick + ceil(distance_ly * ticks_per_ly(carriage))
```

Two values of `ticks_per_ly`, both anchored to worldbook §1.1's real numbers, using this
document's own tick skin (§2.3): a **signal** (news, a price quote, a Counting House rate change —
nothing physical moves) travels at c; a **carriage** (a ship, its cargo, a traveler, an unSkipped
crew member) travels at whatever velocity the sail (plus any Push, worldbook §2.3) actually
achieves, always strictly slower than c:

```
ticks_per_ly(c)      = 8,766     (one light-year at c, in this document's tick unit)
ticks_per_ly(0.2c)   = 43,830    (= 8,766 / 0.2 — unaided sail, the setting's floor)
ticks_per_ly(v)      = 8,766 / (v / c), for any Push-boosted v up to worldbook §2.3's 0.6–0.9c ceiling
```

Checked against the worldbook's own headline claim: at the standard 2 ly corridor spacing
(worldbook §1.2), a signal takes 17,532 ticks ≈ **2.00 years**, an unaided ship takes 87,660 ticks
≈ **10.00 years** — a 5:1 ratio, exactly what worldbook §1.3 states independently (*"a ship...
takes roughly five times that long"*). The formula reproduces the setting's own arithmetic rather
than inventing new numbers, and it generalizes Push cleanly: a Pushed ship's `ticks_per_ly` falls
between the signal rate and the unaided-sail rate, approaching but — by construction, since
`v < c` always — never reaching it. **This is the mathematical form of "channeling buys reach, not
power" (§3.1): the formula's floor is c, and no purchase, of any kind, is permitted to move that
floor.**

### 2.3 The tick unit, and why it was chosen rather than invented

Current fizzos's own `world-clock.mjs` already fixes a day at `PHASE_LENGTH * 4 = 24` ticks (dawn/
day/dusk/night, six ticks each) and a season at 720 ticks — real, verified constants, not this
document's invention. Nothing in that module names a tick as an hour; this document proposes,
as a **NEW DESIGN PROPOSED** skinning choice, reading **one tick as one in-fiction hour** — the
lowest-friction reading of an already-24-ticks-per-day engine, not a new ratio bolted on. Every
number in §2.2 depends on this choice and would rescale cleanly if a future build picks a
different one; nothing about the shard model itself depends on which skin is chosen, only the
concrete tick counts do.

Under this skin, fizzos's own proven capability is directly checkable against what the game
needs: `content/verification-report.md` records *"two identical 26,880-tick autonomous runs
replayed exactly"* — 26,880 ÷ 24 = **1,120 days ≈ 3.07 years** of settlement time, already proven
deterministic and exactly replayable, untended, today. That is not a coincidence worth
overclaiming: it does not, by itself, cover a full 10-year corridor hop (87,660 ticks, about 3.3×
the proven horizon) — a real, honestly-flagged gap, addressed in §9's smallest-step and §11's
risk list, not papered over here.

### 2.4 Two clocks, and the reason a years-long voyage never asks anyone to wait years

This is the actual mechanism that makes "a persistent world where travel takes in-world years" a
**daily** game rather than a subscription nobody could survive, and it rests on a distinction
already proven in the corpus rather than invented for Okaga: `farstone-qbn-design.md` §2
separates **daily seed → which situations are live** (shared, content-deterministic) from
**action budget → a per-player quality** (personal, session-paced) as two orthogonal axes on the
same engine. Okaga needs the identical separation at a larger scale:

- **The settlement's world-clock** advances by exactly 24 ticks per real UTC day the settlement
  is being actively played — precisely `ruinfold-daily-design.md` §1.1's `dailySeed(dateUTC)`
  pattern, reused unmodified: one seed, one shared docket (today's blight-progression tick,
  today's array-calibration state, today's REQ manifest), everyone who logs in that day sees the
  same one. This is what §5's daily ritual runs on, and it is the only clock a settlement-only
  player ever has to think about.
- **A voyage is a scheduled event, not a walked simulation.** Booking passage at `origin_tick`
  computes `delivery_tick` once, via §2.2's formula, and the character is simply *elsewhere* until
  the world-clock (advancing at its own ordinary 24-ticks-per-played-day pace, or faster if a
  future build adds background/idle advancement — an unproven capability, flagged, not assumed,
  in §11) reaches that tick. **Nobody, including the server, "lives through" the intervening
  87,660 ticks in real time to make this true** — this is the entire point of a deterministic
  engine: `@561-group/cartridge`'s `defaultReplay` already computes final state from `(seed,
  intent-log)` in one pass regardless of how many ticks separate the two endpoints (`cartridge`
  README: *"given only `createEngine` + `applyIntent`, it rebuilds final state from a seed and an
  intent list"*) — advancing 87,660 ticks is not a different kind of operation from advancing 24,
  only a bigger one, and computing it does not require anyone to have waited through it.

The player experience this produces: booking a corridor hop is a real, weighed decision (your
character is off the settlement's active roster — talked-to by the cast, not by you — for
whatever in-fiction years the hop costs) but never a real-world waiting-room. A player returns
whenever they next log in after `delivery_tick` has passed and finds their character arrived,
with the settlement's own history in the interim available to read as a digest — literally the
worldbook §1.3 "Foundation problem" (a government can only arbitrate retroactively, never in real
time) experienced personally, at the scale of one absent player instead of one absent government.

### 2.5 Time-debt, made concrete — the Hyperion move as a mechanic

Worldbook §2.6 states time-debt as fiction (*"the person you left returns older, or not at
all"*); this is its mechanical form, and it is deliberately narrow, matching the worldbook's own
hard boundary (§2.8): **Skip never changes `delivery_tick`.** The ship still arrives on the
Confederacy's shared clock exactly when §2.2's formula says it does, at whatever velocity it's
actually going — Push is the only lever that moves `delivery_tick` earlier, because Push is the
only lever that changes velocity. What Skip changes is a second, personal number: how much of that
same fixed `[origin_tick, delivery_tick]` interval the *traveling character's own worldline*
actually experienced. A Skip of compression ratio `r` charges the traveler `time-debt = (1 - 1/r)
× hop_duration`, credited against a portable, Counting-House-tracked ledger (not the traveler's
purse — worldbook §2.6), repaid only by **settling**: living out ordinary, uncompressed ticks,
during which the traveler cannot legally book another Skip. This is the mechanical guarantee
behind the fiction's own "pilgrim who Skips to reach a dying relative" example (worldbook §2.6):
the ship arrives on schedule either way; Skip only decides whether the traveler's own character
was present, biologically, for the years in between, or spent them compressed and now owes them
back.

## 3. The conceit as premium currency, priced kindly

### 3.1 Reach, not power — the hard boundary stated as a design rule

§2.2's formula already carries the whole argument mathematically: `ticks_per_ly(v) = 8,766 / (v/c)`
has c as a hard floor that no purchase can cross, and channeling's two levers (worldbook §2.3)
only ever operate inside that floor. **Push moves you toward the floor** (a ship gets there
faster, still bounded by c) — this is reach in the literal, spatial sense: it is the lever that
lets a single season of real play cover a crossing that unaided sail would take a decade to cover,
without ever making a Pushed character *stronger* than an un-Pushed one once they arrive. **Skip
moves the floor's cost off the traveler's calendar and onto their worldline** (§2.5) — this is
reach in the personal sense: it is the lever that lets a mortal player's limited playtime and a
character's limited career span cover a distance that would otherwise consume it. Neither lever
touches combat, crafting, the local market's prices, a settlement's storylet outcomes, or standing
with a faction. **Chron is not a currency the local Rimworld game has any use for, structurally —
there is nothing in §1.1's local-scale storylet or §1.3's local market that chron is denominated
in or could purchase an advantage in.** This is the design answer to instruction: not a promise
enforced by policy, but a currency with no denomination-compatible sink anywhere in the game that
isn't crossing distance.

### 3.2 What chron can and cannot buy, restated as a table

| Chron buys | Chron does not buy |
|---|---|
| Push — a faster `delivery_tick` for a specific hop, bounded by the 0.6–0.9c ceiling | A storylet outcome, of any kind, at any settlement |
| Skip — less of a specific traveler's own worldline spent inside a fixed `[origin_tick, delivery_tick]` interval | A local market price, a crafting yield, a faction standing shift |
| Loom-queue priority at a chokepoint (an EVE-shaped scarcity good — worldbook §2.2's loom-as-infrastructure) | Combat, skill-by-use progression, or any `fizzos` quality tagged append-only-trained or decaying-need in §1.1's table |
| — | Information faster than the physical arrival that would carry it (worldbook §2.3's hard rule, restated §2.8) |

### 3.3 The credits-as-warp tension, named rather than silently resolved

There is a real tension between two things the house has already said, and this document names it
rather than picking a side without the owner's sign-off. `gaming-enterprises-vision.md` §4 states
the conceit's fictional logic plainly: *"if money is energy and time is energy, then purchasing
credits is what allows warp travel."* `the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §2 (corrected) states the
house's actual monetization posture just as plainly: *"We never take your money to play... never
pay out more than we verifiably earned."* Read literally, side by side, the first sentence could
be taken to mean a player buys warp with a real credit card; the second forecloses that reading
for the whole catalog. **This document's proposal, offered for the owner to keep or cut**: treat
these as two different kinds of sentence, not one. The vision note's sentence is **diegetic** — it
explains, inside the fiction, *why* chron costs what it costs (money is energy is time, in-world,
worked out fully in worldbook §2). The trust-copy sentence is a **real-world business rule**, and
it wins whenever the two would otherwise conflict: credits, in this game, are earned by playing —
identically to `ENERGY` under `energy-bank`'s existing earn-only discipline (§1.3) — and chron is
bought with *those*, never with a real-money purchase that bypasses play. The fiction's causal
chain (worldbook §2.7: *credits buy chron, chron buys a channeler's draw, the draw buys Push or
Skip*) stays exactly as written; what changes is only where credits themselves come from, and the
answer is the same answer every other `ENERGY` balance in the catalog already has. This keeps the
commission's own sentence true in-world while keeping the house's harder, more recently stated
promise true in the real one.

### 3.4 Why v1 can honestly ship with zero looms

Worldbook §2.2 already states looms are rare — *"a handful per Core World, fewer per Established
Colony, essentially none on the Frontier"* — and Ben is an Established-Colony-tier system
(worldbook §4.2's population table), which makes **zero operational looms at Ben** a plausible
reading of canon's own rarity claim, not a contrivance invented to duck scope. §4 below makes this
the actual v1 cut: the premium-currency system designed in full above is real design, ready to
build, but it is not required for v1 to be a complete, playable game — the strongest possible form
of "never pay-to-win the local game" is a v1 where the pay-adjacent system does not exist in the
build at all yet. A dormant, historical, or unlicensed loom stub at Ben (a Founding-era ruin, or a
smuggler's unregistered rig — either reads fine against worldbook §2.4's corona-detection hook) is
a free piece of foreshadowing furniture, not a functioning system, in v1.

## 4. Scope honesty: the v1 cut

### 4.1 What's in

**One system (Ben), one settlement cluster (Apotei Orchard + Buinga Station, Ben-Two — the exact
locations worldbook §6.1's gazetteer already names, and the setting "The Okaga"'s own draft
scenes already dramatize in detail: the requisition economy, the ticket numbers, the seed
envelopes, the blight).** This is deliberately the same content-well strategy
`farstone-qbn-design.md` §6 used for pyfars/legacy-Farstone — mine the existing draft fiction's
specifics directly for room prose, NPC bios, and the storylet seeds already sitting in it, rather
than inventing a setting from nothing. In scope: storylet play (§1.1) over the six quality
families, MUD presence and talk (§1.2) across Buinga Station and the Orchard's rooms, a
`fizzos market.mjs`-priced local REQ economy, a small starting cast (§6), one shared daily docket
(§5) driven by `dailySeed("okaga-ben-two", dateUTC)`.

### 4.2 What's explicitly not in

No interstellar travel of any kind — no ships depart or arrive as a playable action. No channeling,
Push, or Skip — §3.4's zero-loom cut. No player-to-player `energy-bank` market yet — v1's economy
is entirely the local `market.mjs` shop, not a player-driven one; EVE's *industry-and-contracts*
texture (§1.3) is a real, designed, next-tier feature, not a v1 claim. No Counting House or Patrol
as playable factions — per §1.1's own discipline, Frontier/Established-Colony content should
almost never resolve on an institution arriving in time to matter, and v1 has no interstellar
event for either institution to arrive *to* yet regardless.

### 4.3 The graph is real from day one — this is the actual scope-honesty claim

The easy failure mode here is building a single-system game with the shard model bolted on later,
when a second system finally exists. This document's proposal is the opposite, and it costs
nothing extra to build now: **v1 encodes Ben as a node with a real edge, at a real distance, to
one named-or-placeholder neighbor, from the first day of the build**, using exactly §2.2's
formula, exercised against real numbers instead of a stub. Worldbook §1.2/§6.1 already states
Ben's own topology: *"a spur system... one array, one route."* That one route already has a
canonical event to test the whole delivery-tick pipeline against, needing zero invented
justification: **HCS Okaga's own decadal patrol visit is the placeholder edge's scheduled
arrival** — the Arrival Convention (OWNER CANON) *is* a countdown storylet, computed by §2.2's
formula against the corridor's real 2 ly spacing, visible to players as "the Okaga is due in
`delivery_tick`" long before the far end of that edge has one line of authored content. When a
second system is eventually built, it is not a retrofit — it is filling in a distance the graph
already had.

A second, smaller proof of the same pipe, available even cheaper: Ben's own three inhabited/mined
bodies (Ben-Two, Ben-Three, Ben-Four — OWNER CANON, worldbook §0.2) are separated by ordinary
orbital distances (a few AU, illustrative — **NEW CANON PROPOSED**, flavor per worldbook §8's own
convention), which run to light-*minutes*, not light-years — under §2.2's formula, almost always
rounding to the very next tick. This is not meant to be a dramatic mechanic; it is meant to be a
cheap, low-stakes place to unit-test that the delivery-tick pipe computes correctly before
anything real depends on it — a garden hose proved before it has to carry a river.

## 7. Content pipeline: worldbook lists become storylet data

The worldbook was built for exactly this, in its own words (§0 intro): *"eaten forever after by a
storylet compiler — §6's gazetteer entries are written as literal, schema-consistent blocks for
that purpose."* The pipeline this document proposes is the Okaga instance of the general pattern
`farstone-qbn-design.md` §3 already worked out for pyfars: a `place` YAML block (worldbook §6.1)
compiles to a fizzos room; a `faction` block (§6.2) compiles to a standing-ledger entry plus a
roster slot a cast persona can fill; an `era` block (§6.3) is metadata a storylet's flavor text can
reference but never branches on, since eras carry no `canon-status: owner-canon` mechanical claims
of their own. **The worldbook's own §8 load-bearing/flavor table is the compiler's canon-status
field**: a `canon-status: owner-canon` place name is never rewritten by procedural content; a
`flavor`-tagged number (population figures, exact distances) is exactly what a daily seed is free
to perturb within its stated ratio. Nothing about this pipeline is new machinery — it is the same
shape-rule, don't-hard-code-field-names discipline `lantern-service`'s compiler already
demonstrates (cited at one remove via `farstone-qbn-design.md` §3), pointed at YAML frontmatter
blocks instead of a markdown corpus's own frontmatter.

## 8. Determinism, replay, cartridge fit

A settlement session is a `Cartridge<State, Intent>` exactly per the spec: `createEngine(seed,
"okaga-ben-two")` seeds off `dailySeed`, `applyIntent` walks storylet choices and MUD commands
through the same validated `Intent` shape §1.2 already commits to for the cast, `defaultReplay` +
`hashState` give the anti-cheat argument `ruinfold-daily-design.md` §2 already proved out for a
different game on the identical contract (*"any single intent... fails validate() → whole run
rejected... (tick, seq) pairs not strictly increasing → rejected"* — the same tolerance table
applies verbatim, since it is a property of the cartridge contract, not of ruinfold's specific
content). §2.4's voyage-as-scheduled-event design is what actually asks something new of the
contract — computing state at a `delivery_tick` far past any tick a human interactively walked
through — and §2.3 already named the honest status of that ask: mechanically it is `defaultReplay`
used for its literal purpose (state from seed + intent-log, at whatever tick is requested), not a
new capability; empirically it is proven only up to 26,880 ticks today, and a hop needs up to
87,660. §11 turns that gap into a concrete, cheap proof obligation rather than leaving it as an
assumption.

The wallet side needs one piece of new engineering, named honestly per the substrate-fit-brief's
own scoping discipline (§2, §7): a `chron` balance needs its own chart-of-accounts path, parallel
to `energy-bank/accounts.mjs`'s existing `liabilities:energy:<id>` (`energyAccountPath`) —
propose `liabilities:chron:<id>`, same double-entry discipline, same
`checkNoNegativeBalances`/`checkPayoutInvariant` invariants, priced by the still-unbuilt
`EnergyHooks`/`priceOf` surface the substrate-fit-brief already flagged as unimplemented in
`0.1.1`. This is **NEW CANON PROPOSED at the schema level, unbuilt at the code level** — not
required for v1 (§4.2), real design debt for whichever step first needs §3's system live.

Okaga does not appear in `gaming-enterprises-vision.md` §6's staircase table at all today; its
only current house placement is `the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §3's shelf table, **The Stars

exists; the galactic confederacy stays exactly where the shelf table already puts it, arriving
later by the graph-extension path §4.3 describes, not by Okaga v1 waiting for it.

## 10. The smallest real step

The single most load-bearing fact in the whole corpus is already named as such (worldbook §0.4):
the signalling array is dual-use, propulsion and comms backbone in one act, and destroying it is
what silences a spur system in "The Okaga"'s own plot skeleton. `farstone-qbn-design.md` §6's own
smallest step ported Permit #23 — the one piece of content proven twice, in two engines — as three
or four cells against current fizzos's real module surface. **Okaga's equivalent smallest step is
the direct transplant of that exact pattern onto its own most load-bearing fact**: author the
array's `within-window` maintenance predicate and its declared converse `overdue` (a **NEW CANON
PROPOSED** calibration cadence — illustrative, flavor-tagged, not a fixed number) as one
`declareConverse` binding against `predication.mjs`/`world-clock.mjs`, run the daily docket (§5)
forward, and confirm the array's calibration state settles to a visibly contested ⊤ on its own —
a sabotage-vulnerability window nobody hand-coded — after N ticks, zero authored `if overdue`
branch anywhere. This proves the entire QBN chassis against Okaga's single most canon-critical
fact, in the smallest possible unit, before a single room or NPC is authored.

---

## 11. Risks

**Prose at volume, inherited directly — cited, not restated as new.** `farstone-qbn-design.md` §5
names the real, evidenced risk: agent-authored prose is demonstrably good at small scale (that
note quotes real `farstone-harbor` room copy) but *volume and branching* — 500–2,000 words across
three to six branch-outcomes, times hundreds of situations — is undemonstrated anywhere in the
corpus, "the specific, nameable risk." Okaga inherits this unmodified, and worldbook §7's own
house-style guidance (terms like *chron*, *the Fold*, *a snap* left unglossed, trusted to the
reader) mitigates verbosity somewhat but does not touch the underlying volume math.

**The Toll's visible-aging continuity, an Okaga-specific compounding of the same risk.** A
channeler cast member's apparent age (worldbook §2.5) has to stay consistent across possibly years
of real calendar time and many authoring sessions — this is exactly why §1.1's table insists it be
a **derived-not-stored** quality, computed off cumulative χ drawn, the same discipline
`farstone-qbn-design.md` §4 already validated for a title-from-skill-bonus pattern (*"rises as you
train, no separate promotion"*) — never a number an author hand-updates and inevitably drifts.
Deferred entirely for v1 by §3.4's zero-loom cut; live risk only once §3 ships.

**The 26,880-vs-87,660-tick gap, named as a proof obligation, not an assumption.** §2.3/§8 already
state this precisely: v1 needs nothing past the proven horizon (a single system, played daily,
never needs a big jump); the first corridor hop does, at roughly 3.3× what's proven today. The
concrete, cheap fix, matching `ruinfold-daily-design.md` §2.3's own house pattern (*"determinism
as a test, not a claim"*): a `prove-long-horizon-tick.mjs` exercising the real Ben-Two content
across an 87,660-plus-tick horizon, written and green *before* any build lets a player book a
corridor hop — not before v1 ships.

**Scope creep toward the "then" tier before the "next" tier is proven.** The temptation this
document explicitly warns against: building §3's chron ledger, or a second system, before §10's
smallest step and §4's v1 cut are live and played. §9's staircase correction is deliberately
conservative about what v1 claims for exactly this reason.

---

## 12. Load-bearing vs. proposal

| Element | Status | Why |
|---|---|---|
| §2.2's delivery-tick formula (signal at c, carriage at v<c, Push narrows the gap, never closes it) | **Load-bearing** | Reproduces worldbook §1.1/§1.3's own stated numbers exactly (the 5:1 signal:ship ratio); no purchase is permitted to move the c floor |
| Skip never changes `delivery_tick`; only Push does | **Load-bearing** | The mechanical form of worldbook §2.8's hard boundary — remove this and "reach not power" collapses into "power" |
| The two-clock split (settlement world-clock vs. voyage-as-scheduled-event) | **Load-bearing design choice** | The actual mechanism that makes years-long travel a daily game; §2.4 |
| chron earned via play, not real-money-purchased directly | **Proposal, flagged for owner sign-off** | §3.3 names a real tension between two existing house statements; this is this document's resolution, not a settled fact |
| Tick = 1 in-fiction hour | **NEW DESIGN PROPOSED, freely rescalable** | Chosen for fit with fizzos's existing 24-ticks/day constant; every §2.2 number rescales if changed |
| v1 = Ben-Two only, zero looms, zero interstellar travel | **This document's scope proposal** | §4; the strongest available form of "never pay-to-win the local game" |
| Okaga v1 belongs at "next," not "then," on the staircase | **Proposal, contradicts the current shelf table's placement** | §9 — flagged explicitly as a correction, not assumed silently |
| `liabilities:chron:<id>` account path | **NEW CANON PROPOSED, unbuilt** | Parallels `energy-bank`'s real `energyAccountPath` shape; not implemented anywhere |
| Array calibration cadence, orbital AU distances, cast member names | **Flavor** | Illustrative per worldbook §8's own convention; adjust freely |

---

## 13. Outline and the v1 cut

**Document map:** §0 relationship to the worldbook and the substrate-fit-brief → §1 the Triple
wired precisely (QBN storylets on the farstone-qbn chassis, Rimworld-textured; Discworld MUD
presence with the cast as real intent-log peers; EVE industry split between `fizzos market.mjs`'s
local shop and `energy-bank`'s player wallet) → §2 light-lag as architecture (spacelike separation
as a free shard boundary, one delivery-tick formula anchored to worldbook's own numbers, the
two-clock split that makes years-long travel a daily game, time-debt made mechanical) → §3 the
conceit as premium currency (reach-not-power as a property of the delivery-tick formula itself,
what chron can and cannot buy, the credits-as-warp/earn-only tension named and resolved as a
proposal, why v1 can ship with zero looms) → §4 scope honesty (the v1 cut, what's excluded, the
graph real from day one via HCS Okaga's own canon countdown) → §5 daily ritual → §6 cast roster →
§7 content pipeline → §8 determinism/replay/cartridge fit → §9 staircase placement (proposed
correction: next, not then) → §10 the smallest real step (the array's own within-window/overdue
pair, Permit #23's exact pattern transplanted onto Okaga's single most load-bearing fact) → §11
risks (prose at volume, inherited and cited; the Toll's continuity burden; the proven-tick-horizon
gap; scope creep) → §12 load-bearing/proposal table.

**The v1 cut, in one paragraph:** Okaga v1 is a single system — Ben, Established-Colony tier per
worldbook §4.2 — with exactly one playable settlement cluster, Apotei Orchard and Buinga Station
on Ben-Two, mined directly from "The Okaga"'s own draft scenes for room prose, NPC texture, and
storylet seeds; it runs storylet play over fizzos's six real quality families gated on the
settlement's own shortages and its one canon-critical contested quality (the signalling array's
maintenance window), MUD presence and talk across those rooms with a three-member cast playing
through the same validated intent-log path a human would, and a local REQ economy priced by
fizzos's own `market.mjs`, all synchronized by one shared daily-UTC seed exactly like
`ruinfold-daily-design.md`'s pattern; it has zero interstellar travel, zero looms, and zero
player-to-player `energy-bank` market, so the premium-currency system designed in full in §3 is
simply absent from the build rather than merely disabled — the strongest honest form of
"never pay-to-win the local game" available; and it already encodes, from the first day of the
build, Ben's real single corridor edge and the exact delivery-tick math for it, with HCS Okaga's
own canon decadal patrol visit standing in as that edge's first real, playable arrival event, so
that the day a second system is built it is filling in a distance the game already had rather than
retrofitting the shard model onto a game that was never designed to need one.

frontmatter.title: Okaga Game Design
frontmatter.description: Design specification for the Okaga commission — quality-based-narrative storylets meet Discworld MUD presence meet EVE industry, wired to light-lag as the shard boundary and to channeling as a reach-not-power premium currency, with an honest single-system v1 cut.

rooms.title: Okaga Substrate-Fit Brief
rooms.description: The house-substrate fit read for the owner's Okaga commission (persistent browser world, one warp conceit, 0.2c ships, billions of players, galactic confederacy): which existing house math/systems carry which commission pillar, stated precisely, with owner canon and newly-proposed canon kept separate.
rooms.body:
# Okaga Substrate-Fit Brief

The commission (owner, 2026-08-19, verbatim substance): a persistent online world people play
in browser — "picture quality narrative meets Discworld MUD meets EVE." As hard scifi as
possible, with exactly one conceit — "some people can channel energy from outside the
dimensions of this world to do warp travel and other forms of accelerating the arrow of
time." Ships otherwise reach only ~0.2c, giving "Rimworld-y elements, Foundation-y elements,
but also closer to Hyperion-y elements BECAUSE OF THE PLAYERS." A galactic confederacy. World
scale such that a few billion players (assume 50% of humanity) doesn't skew galactic
economics.

**What this note is.** Not a design document — a fit read. For each commission pillar: which
already-built or already-proved house system carries it, cited to source, and whether the
claim is **OWNER CANON** (already said, in-repo, about Okaga specifically), **HOUSE SUBSTRATE**
(a real, built or proved system this brief proposes pointing at Okaga — not yet Okaga canon
until the owner says so), or **NEW CANON PROPOSED** (this brief's own invention, offered for
the owner to keep or cut, per the standing instruction that Okaga canon in-repo is thin).

## 0. What is actually OWNER CANON on Okaga today — the whole list

Thin, per the owner's own framing, and it is genuinely all four items:

1. A legacy, unverified, archived Elite-like space-flight game named Okaga, built on the
   `tsander` wireframe-3D engine, recovery-blocked on `render-substrate-service`
   (`planned/okaga.md`). **This is a different artifact from the commission** — the note
   filing it says so explicitly and this brief does not conflate them.
2. The credits-as-warp conceit, already stated house-wide, not Okaga-specific but named
   against Okaga first: *"if money is energy and time is energy, then purchasing credits is
   what allows warp travel — or other forms of 'magic' — within each world system... warp in
   Okaga, magic elsewhere"* (`gaming-enterprises-vision.md` §4).
3. Okaga chosen as the fiction-heavy setting because *"the interstellar laser-powered
   solar-sail material is 'so in line with how the math of Obsmetrologia works'"*
   (`gaming-enterprises-vision.md` §4, owner statement) — asserted, not derived anywhere in
   the read set. No document in this fit read shows *which* Obsmetrologia math the sail
   physics maps to. **Genuinely open — do not invent a derivation to fill this in.**
4. Shelf placement: "The Stars (later) — Okaga-set games; credits-as-warp — the space-sim
   disc" (`the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §3), last-named shelf, explicitly deferred.

Everything below pillar-by-pillar is HOUSE SUBSTRATE or NEW CANON PROPOSED, labeled as such,
because nothing else in the corpus ties these systems to Okaga yet.

## 1. "Picture quality narrative meets Discworld MUD meets EVE"

**Discworld-MUD half — carried by the current fizzos chassis, not by Farstone's fiction.**
`farstone-qbn-design.md` establishes the mechanism, but the load-bearing part transplants
cleanly because it's engine-level, not setting-level: a quality is a settled EAVT-shaped cell,
and a storylet is a situation the settling/join fold makes visible *without anyone authoring
an if-branch* — proven in committed code (`permit-23`'s `within-window` × its declared
converse `overdue` settling to ⊤ "past tick 30... nobody coded 'permits go bad,' the bilattice
fold produced it"). §6 of that note is explicit that the *transplantable* artifact is the
**active** fizzos module surface — `world.mjs`, `engine.mjs`, `npc.mjs`, `predication.mjs`,
`world-clock.mjs`, `ecology.mjs`, `skills.mjs`, `social.mjs` — not the retired `tab`/EAVT API
the old Farstone game was written against, and not any of Farstone's place-names or NPCs.
**HOUSE SUBSTRATE, precisely scoped:** this is the correct narrative-QBN engine for Okaga's
text layer (situations, NPC routines, contested/⊤-legal qualities dramatizing contradiction
rather than resolving it) — but nothing in the corpus has pointed fizzos at Okaga content yet;
doing so is new work, not a discovered fact. Browser-first is already the house default
(`bin/farstone.mjs` serves HTTP/SSE; `gaming-enterprises-vision.md`: "all browser-based, with
terminal/API interfaces welcomed wherever they fit") — matches "picture quality narrative"
only insofar as a real reading UI gets built on top; today the transport is a bare endpoint,
not a QBN-shaped reading surface (farstone-qbn-design.md §2).

**EVE half — carried by two separate, already-built systems.** (a) The player-driven-economy
half: `@561-group/energy-bank`'s `transfer` module already implements player-to-player
`transferEnergy`, pooling (`createPool`/`contributeToPool`/`distributePool`, largest-remainder
split), and `sellEnergy` (a transfer whose narration carries an agreed price) — a real market
primitive, house-generic, unskinned. (b) The peers-not-pets half: `the-suite-and-the-studio.md`
§2's cast — *"named recurring agent players who actually play, by the same intent-log API as
humans"* — is EVE's "everyone plays the same economy, including the whales and the corp
alliances" instinct, done honestly, because the house's own players-vs-NPCs distinction is
already architecturally collapsed (peers-not-pets). **HOUSE SUBSTRATE**, both halves built,
neither yet wired to a game, let alone Okaga.

## 2. Exactly one conceit — the wallet it prices against

**This is a precise fit, not a loose one.** The commission's "exactly one conceit" constraint
and the Energy Bank's single-commodity, earn-only discipline are the same rule stated twice,
independently, once in fiction and once in code:

- Fiction: *"some people can channel energy from outside the dimensions of this world to do
  warp travel"* — one conceit, one exception to otherwise-hard physics.
- Code (`energy-bank/README.md`): *"there is no random-outcome, stake-at-risk, or house-edge
  mechanic anywhere in it... `ENERGY` is earned by playing, spent inside games, transferred or
  pooled between players, and (optionally) redeemed... That is the whole vocabulary. This
  posture is a property of every module in this package, not a flag one can turn off."*

Concretely: a channeler spending "energy from outside the dimensions of this world" on a warp
jump **is** a debit against `liabilities:energy:<id>` on the fixed chart-of-accounts path the
`accounts` module already derives, checked by the same `checkNoNegativeBalances`/
`checkPayoutInvariant` invariants every other game in the fleet uses. No new ledger mechanics
are needed for the conceit itself — Okaga's one exception to hard physics is priced by the
system that already exists to be the one exception to every other game's raw stat economy.
**HOUSE SUBSTRATE, tightly scoped.** What is genuinely unbuilt and must be named as such,
per the energy-bank README's own scope statement: the `EnergyHooks`/`priceOf` action-pricing
surface (spec §2.5) and the aggregate `EnergyBank` manager class (§2.6) are **not implemented
in 0.1.1** — "no game is wired to this package yet." Warp-jump pricing (distance × some
obstruction-shaped cost, per the energy-tiling precedent in `gaming-enterprises-vision.md`
§2/§7 proposal 2) is **NEW CANON PROPOSED**: no document specifies what a warp jump costs in
`ENERGY`, only that it would be a debit of the same commodity everything else already uses.

## 3. 0.2c ships, Rimworld/Foundation/Hyperion "because of the players" — the key fit

**This is the load-bearing answer to the whole brief, so it gets stated exactly.**
`shrimp-ecology-brief-v2.md` §1 proves, at the mathematics layer (not as a game metaphor):
*"Light cones are Lorentzian (proved): on a causal-set settling, the apex cone is the timelike
(causally connected) substructure and the void cone the spacelike one; H¹ generators are
causal-precedence-acquisition events."* §3 (revised build order) turns this into a design
decision for that MUD: *"adopt the Lorentzian causal settling as the event model — a player's
light cone is the apex cone of their causal history; spacelike players are provably
non-interfering (this is the CALM/coordination-free property worn as fiction: the abyss
between you is real mathematics)."*

**Why this is not a metaphor for Okaga specifically, unlike its origin use.** In the SHRIMP
brief, the light-cone model is chosen as a *design* decision (marked `[D]`) for a fictional
undersea ecology — the causal structure is imposed on a game that has no physical reason to be
relativistic. In Okaga, it is not imposed at all: the commission's own physics — bounded
sub-light travel (~0.2c) and lightspeed comms — means two regions of the galaxy that have not
yet exchanged a lightspeed signal or a warp-capable ship **are, by the stated setting physics
itself, spacelike separated in exactly the technical sense this theorem proves things about.**
The same proved theorem applies to Okaga natively, because Okaga's one hard-scifi rule (no
FTL except the one conceit) is the physical precondition the theorem's Lorentzian structure
already assumes. That is simultaneously: (a) hard scifi — it is literally special-relativistic
causality, not invented game lore; (b) the SHRIMP causal math verbatim, reused because the
shape is the same, not paraphrased; and (c) the mechanism for pillar 5 below.

This also gives the tonal blend its mechanism, not just its vibe:
- **Hyperion-y** — Hyperion's Hegemony worlds are politically and socially asynchronous
  *because of* pre-Farcaster light-lag; that is precisely a population of players living inside
  each other's void cones.
- **Foundation-y** — a wide, slow galaxy where local political drift is possible *because*
  information cannot outrun light is the same causal-set fact read at civilizational scale.
- **Rimworld-y** — an isolated frontier colony is self-governing not by authorial choice but
  because no timely intervention from the metropole is *causally possible* — the void cone
  again, at the scale of one settlement.
- **"Because of the players"** is the owner's own tell that this must be a real multi-agent
  causal fact, not scripted isolation — which is exactly what "spacelike separation" is: an
  emergent property of where players and ships actually are, not an authored zone boundary.

**HOUSE SUBSTRATE, proposed as a genuine transplant, not yet Okaga canon anywhere.** Nothing in
the corpus currently states Okaga uses this model — the SHRIMP brief was written for the
undersea cooperative MUD. This brief proposes reusing the identical proved math for Okaga's
galaxy because Okaga's stated physics is the case the theorem was already about, more
literally than the MUD it was written for.

## 4. Billions of players without skewing galactic economics

**Carried by the same theorem in §3, applied as a scaling argument rather than a tone
argument.** "Spacelike separation = provably non-interfering" is not just flavor — it is
CALM-shaped coordination-freedom (`shrimp-ecology-brief-v2.md` §1: *"The distributed strand is
the proved strand: CRDT convergence / Mayer–Vietoris / cohomological-CALM"*). Two galactic
regions that cannot causally affect each other within the observed time window **do not need
to reconcile state with each other at all** — not "eventually," structurally never, until a
warp-capable channeler or a lightspeed signal actually connects their light cones. This is
precisely how a few billion players fail to skew galactic economics without sharding: the
galaxy partitions itself causally, by physics, not by a server-assignment decision anyone
makes. Locally, within one causally-connected region, `@561-group/cartridge`'s deterministic
seed/replay contract is the consistency mechanism already built for exactly this shape — a
`daily-utc` seed is *"a pure function of a UTC calendar day and a game/config id — every
player worldwide resolves the same seed on the same day"* (`cartridge/README.md`), and
`defaultReplay`/`createVerifier` make every region's local simulation independently
replay-checkable without any other region's cooperation. Region-local determinism plus
cross-region causal non-interference is a complete, two-piece answer to the scale question,
built from two systems that already exist for other reasons.

**The refinement that makes this the safe version of an idea the house already flagged as
risky.** `wilder-conceptions-01.md` item 6 proposed something adjacent and *literal*: measure
real ActivityPub federation latency between live servers and let that be the Commons' actual
regional geometry — *"a remote Mastodon instance with slow, unreliable delivery to you is,
honestly and un-metaphorically, 'far away.'"* The ringleader's same-day response adopted the
cheap sub-step (log latency as a metric) but explicitly deferred the literal-geometry claim,
naming the reason: *"your own failure mode (an admin's bad day reshaping the world map) is
disqualifying for a shipped game until someone designs damping; measured-latency-as-*input* to
an authored map may be the survivable version."* **Okaga's version of this idea does not carry
that risk**, because the causal-separation signal is diegetic distance (light-years ÷ c, a
static galactic geometry) rather than live network health — it cannot have "a bad day." Okaga
gets the exact shape wilder-conceptions item 6 wanted (real physics as real geometry, not an
authored zone map) while sidestepping the specific objection that got it deferred elsewhere,
because the input is stable by construction. **NEW CANON PROPOSED**: this specific
resolution — "Okaga is the safe case of the deferred wilder-conceptions #6 idea" — is this
brief's synthesis, not stated anywhere in the source documents.

## 5. Galactic confederacy — the one pillar with no clean house-system answer

Named for completeness rather than papered over: nothing in the read set specifies a house
system for confederacy-scale governance mechanics. The nearest structural cousin is pyfars —
governance-as-markdown-records dispatched by a rules engine, with closure-rule records
carrying `reads`/`writes` frontmatter (`farstone-qbn-design.md` §1b, §3) — which demonstrates
the house *can* make a polity's charter, duties, and violations game-legible data at the scale
of one town's city hall. Whether that same record shape scales to a galactic confederacy's
charter bodies is untested anywhere in this corpus at any scale beyond a single municipality.
**Genuinely open — flagged, not resolved, per the standing instruction not to invent past what
the corpus supports.**

## 6. Solar sails / Obsmetrologia

Left exactly where §0 item 3 puts it: an owner assertion, unelaborated, no document in this
read maps solar-sail laser-propulsion physics to specific Obsmetrologia mathematics. The
SHRIMP brief §4 records a related but distinct owner claim — that Obsmetrologia, relationality,
semiotics, and Lakotaean metaphysics are "the same mathematics under different lenses" — which
is a claim about *cross-framework equivalence*, not about sail physics specifically. **Do not
conflate the two claims or invent the missing derivation; both are owner-attested, neither is
derived in-repo.**

## 7. The wallet, precisely — what `cartridge`/`energy-bank` are and are not today

For the record, since the conceit prices against this system directly (§2): `@561-group/
cartridge` (0.1.0, 74 tests) is the seed/intent-log/replay contract — manifest schema,
canonical stringification, `hashState`, `createVerifier` — with zero opinion on RNG or on any
game's payload shape. `@561-group/energy-bank` (0.1.1, 79 tests, rebuilt from `.mts` to `.mjs`
because Node refuses to type-strip `.mts` resolved through `node_modules`) is identity +
double-entry ledger + transfer/pool/sell + pluggable settlement (`mockBackend` real today;
`zbdBackend` shape-correct but makes no live network call; on-chain a future third
implementation of the same `SettlementBackend` interface, per the README, "with zero schema
change"). **Neither package currently imports the other** — no `@561-group/cartridge`
integration exists in energy-bank 0.1.1, per its own README's "not implemented" list. Any
Okaga build wiring warp-cost to a cartridge-driven game engine is new integration work on both
sides, not a flip of an existing switch.

## 8. The stopped MUD lane — noted, not opened

Per instruction: a MUD lane (tidepool) has design ideas cached but is unbuilt and currently
stopped. No file matching that name was found anywhere in the active or legacy tree during
this read; noting its stopped status here only, as directed, without further investigation.

## 9. Summary table — pillar → carrier → canon status

| Commission pillar | House carrier | Canon status |
|---|---|---|
| Discworld-MUD narrative layer | current fizzos module surface (`world.mjs`/`engine.mjs`/`npc.mjs`/`predication.mjs`/`world-clock.mjs`) | HOUSE SUBSTRATE |
| EVE player-driven economy | `energy-bank/transfer` (transfer/pool/sell) | HOUSE SUBSTRATE |
| EVE peers, not NPCs | the cast, intent-log API (the-suite-and-the-studio.md §2) | HOUSE SUBSTRATE |
| The one conceit, priced | `energy-bank` ledger, `liabilities:energy:<id>` | HOUSE SUBSTRATE (wallet real; warp-specific pricing unbuilt — NEW CANON PROPOSED) |
| 0.2c causal texture (Rimworld/Foundation/Hyperion) | SHRIMP brief's proved Lorentzian light-cone / apex-void math | HOUSE SUBSTRATE, transplant proposed — NOT yet stated as Okaga canon |
| Billions of players, no shard | same Lorentzian math, read as CALM-shaped non-interference, plus cartridge's daily-seed/replay determinism | HOUSE SUBSTRATE, transplant proposed |
| Latency-as-geometry, safely | wilder-conceptions-01 item 6 + ringleader deferral, resolved for Okaga because the "latency" is static galactic distance not live network health | NEW CANON PROPOSED (this brief's synthesis) |
| Galactic confederacy | pyfars governance-as-records (untested past one town) | OPEN — no clean fit found |
| Solar sails / Obsmetrologia | none found | OPEN — owner assertion only |
| Credits-as-warp conceit itself | already named | OWNER CANON |

frontmatter.description: The house-substrate fit read for the owner's Okaga commission (persistent browser world, one warp conceit, 0.2c ships, billions of players, galactic confederacy): which existing house math/systems carry which commission pillar, stated precisely, with owner canon and newly-proposed canon kept separate.

rooms.title: Okaga Worldbook
rooms.description: The commissioned setting bible for Okaga — a persistent browser confederacy of laser-sail ships, light-lag politics, and one priced exception to hard physics: channelers who buy warp and time itself from outside the world's four dimensions. Owner canon is quoted and never contradicted; everything else is labeled new canon proposed.
rooms.body:
# Okaga Worldbook

> "Picture quality narrative meets Discworld MUD meets EVE." As hard scifi as it can be, with
> exactly one conceit: some people can channel energy from outside the dimensions of this world
> to do warp travel and other forms of accelerating the arrow of time. Ships otherwise reach only
> ~0.2c. A galactic confederacy. A few billion players shouldn't skew galactic economics.
> — the commission, owner, 2026-08-19

This is the setting bible for that commission. It is built to be **read once for the shape of the
world** and **eaten forever after by a storylet compiler** — §6's gazetteer entries are written as
literal, schema-consistent blocks for that purpose. Everything in it traces to one of two things:
the thin but real Okaga canon already in this repo, or the physics of laser-pushed light sails at
0.1–0.2c. Where it invents beyond both, it says so, in the margin, every time.

## 0. The canon ledger

Four disclosure tags are used throughout this document. They are not decoration — a storylet
compiler, or a future co-writer, needs to know which sentences it may never contradict and which
it is free to rewrite.

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **OWNER CANON** | Said, in-repo, about Okaga specifically, in the owner's own words or the owner's own draft fiction. Never contradicted below. |
| **OWNER-KEPT** | AI-drafted under the owner's own 2023 system prompt, but selected and retained by the owner in the archive — tone reference, treated as available raw material, not load-bearing fact. |
| **HOUSE SUBSTRATE** | A real house-wide system or law (the 561 Group catalog, the money=energy=time principle) pointed at Okaga for the first time in this document. |
| **NEW CANON PROPOSED** | This document's own invention. Offered for the owner to keep or cut. |

**The whole of OWNER CANON on Okaga, restated once, so nothing below has to re-derive it:**

1. **HCS Okaga** is a specific, named ship — the *Human-Confederacy Ship Okaga* — "a large dinner
   plate operating as a solar sail, with a rotating tube around the rim which provides habitable
   space," propelled by "light signalling arrays... built in populated stellar systems," crewed at
   an estimated 2,000–3,000 including colonists, and named in Lakȟótiyapi, the Lakota language.
   It runs a **galactic patrol** circuit at up to ~0.15–0.2c (owner's ceiling varies 0.15–0.2c
   across years; this document treats that as one range, not a contradiction), taking "about a
   decade" between systems.
2. **Ben** is a system named in Ely Shoshoni ("ben" = *alone*) with four bodies: **Ben-One**
   (uninhabited, hot, hostile rock), **Ben-Two** (habitable and inhabited — the Apotei Orchard,
   the North Sanazi Confederacy's territory), **Ben-Three** (rocky, mined and industrial — where
   HCS Okaga holds orbit), **Ben-Four** (gas giant, recreation complexes an *immersim* "just can't
   do justice").
3. The draft story "The Okaga" establishes: a receiving-station requisition economy (ticket
   numbers, a bar, seed envelopes by the box); an **Arrival Convention** where in-system delegates
   negotiate supplies and colonists; a plot skeleton running robbery → signalling-array sabotage →
   a lynching → thirty years marooned → a crop-blight forcing decentralized local reorganization →
   a returning patrol ship, decades later, debating whether the Confederacy's propping-up model is

## 1. The physics baseline: sail, array, light-lag

### 1.1 The ceiling, and why it's a wall, not a rule

*(HOUSE SUBSTRATE, from the physics constraint sheet, OWNER CANON numbers)*

Every crewed hull in the Confederacy is a photonic sail: a thin, engineered-reflective membrane
kilometers across, kicked to speed by a phased-array laser installation in its home system and,
critically, **caught** by a matching array at the destination. Top practical speed sits at
0.1–0.2c, matching the owner's own numbers across two different years of notes. This is not an
arbitrary limit — kinetic energy scales with v², so every doubling of transit speed costs roughly
four times the delivered beam energy (more once relativistic corrections bite), and a
crewed hull — life support, radiation shielding, cargo, people, not a gram-scale probe — sits
much further down that energy curve than an unmanned relativistic probe design ever could. Above
roughly 0.2c, the beam power, the array size, and the sail's own thermal load all become
unworkable for anything with real mass. **The ceiling is an economics problem, and that fact is
itself load-bearing**: it means faster travel is always, in principle, purchasable — with enough
beam power, enough array, enough energy — which is exactly the door §2's one conceit walks
through.

Deceleration is the harder engineering problem, and it is where the owner's own 2019 log already
gives the correct real-world answer without knowing it: arrays "aimed out toward other systems"
means **every settled system's array launches its own outbound ships and catches everyone else's
inbound ones**, decelerating an arriving hull symmetrically to how the origin array accelerated
it. This is the only known plausible way a crewed ship going 0.15–0.2c stops at all (the
alternative — magnetic-sail braking against the interstellar medium — only works over 50–100-year
timescales, useful as a slow backup for damaged-array arrivals, never as the everyday method).

**Relativity at 0.2c is real but modest** — γ ≈ 1.021, about 2% time dilation. A ten-year transit
is a ten-year transit for everyone aboard, give or take months, not decades. This matters
enormously for craft discipline: Skah's twelve real years aboard HCS Okaga (OWNER CANON) are not
a relativistic trick and this worldbook never treats them as one. Any felt time-skew in this
setting is either sociological (isolation, routine, the length of a voyage) or, once §2 exists,
literally purchased — never a free byproduct of going fast.

### 1.2 The Current: arteries and chokepoints

*(term OWNER-KEPT; network model NEW CANON PROPOSED)*

The Confederacy's settled worlds are not spread at average galactic-field density (roughly one
star per 250–300 cubic light-years near the Confederacy's core, average neighbor spacing ~4 ly).
Corridors were never built in straight lines to the "best" destination — they were built hop by
buildable hop, and a hop is only buildable if the two arrays at either end can actually catch each
other's beam at their aperture and power budget. **Corridors follow the cheapest available chain
of stars, not the shortest path between two points**, which means routes in active service run
noticeably *denser* than the galactic field average — commonly ~2 ly hop-to-hop along an
established line. This is the arithmetic under HCS Okaga's own "about a decade" between systems:
2 ly ÷ 0.2c ≈ 10 years. It also reconciles a highway with off-ramps: systems not on any built
corridor exist inside the same volume, reachable only by long, expensive, high-risk direct hops —
this is where frontier settlement and piracy both live.

This network — the sum of every launch-and-catch array and the beam-paths between them — is
**the Current**. It is the Confederacy's only fast channel for goods, people, *and* information,
because the arrays are the comms backbone too (OWNER CANON, §0.4). A system's place in the
Confederacy is entirely a function of its position in this graph:

- **Hub systems** — multiple arrays, multiple live routes, redundant. Losing one link doesn't cut
  them off. These are the Core Worlds (§4).
- **Spur systems** — one array, one route in, one route out. A single act of sabotage — exactly
  what happens to Ben in "The Okaga" — doesn't just strand the ship in orbit, it silences the
  *system*: no outbound signal, no inbound signal, nothing until either the array is rebuilt or a
  patrol ship happens by. Ben is a spur system by this model, and its plot is the spur-system
  failure mode played out in full.
- **Dark space** — everything off the Current entirely. Reachable, if at all, only the hard way.

### 1.3 Light-lag governance — the Foundation problem, named plainly

*(HOUSE SUBSTRATE, physics constraint sheet)*

A signal at c between two Current-linked systems takes years to decades one-way, full stop — no
trick reduces that for anyone who isn't the one traveling. A ship crossing the same gap at 0.2c
takes roughly five times that long in its own barely-dilated frame. The practical consequence,
stated as plainly as the setting should ever state it: **a central government separated from its
own periphery by decades of light-lag cannot govern that periphery in the ordinary sense.** It
cannot respond to a crisis before the crisis has already resolved itself one way or another. It
can only set slow-moving default law, arbitrate retroactively, and periodically re-survey.

This is not a new idea layered onto Okaga — it is the plot the owner already wrote. "The Okaga"'s
Act 3 has Ben's marooned population solve a monoculture blight by applying "the confederacy's
means of organization on a smaller level," decades before any ship could plausibly help, and the
story's own closing tension is whether the Confederacy's central government does any good at all
by trying to administer such places versus simply extracting value from them once it finally
arrives. **That is Foundation's actual premise, transplanted whole, already sitting in the source
material.** This worldbook's job is to name it as the setting's operating logic and build every
institution in §5 and §6 to match it — nothing here needs to invent the light-lag problem, only
to take it seriously everywhere at once.

What such a Confederacy *can* coordinate: shared protocols fixed in advance (ship design, array
specification, a common trade tongue, measurement standards), slow custom-and-precedent law, and
periodic census-and-arbitration visits — the Patrol circuit (§6.2), exactly as canon already has
it. What it cannot coordinate: real-time markets, live diplomacy, synchronized elections, timely
disaster response, or any notion of a single "current state" shared by more than one system at a
time.

### 1.4 The boundary, stated once, before §2 breaks it on purpose

Everything above this line is ordinary physics: momentum, energy, c as a hard ceiling, light-lag
as an unbreakable political fact. **The one exception the commission asks for lives entirely in
§2, and nowhere else.** No other technology in this worldbook is permitted to quietly relax any of
the above. If a future storylet needs faster information, cheaper deceleration, or a shortcut
around light-lag, the answer is always: buy it from a channeler, pay the price in §2, or don't get
it.

## 2. The one conceit, priced

*(NEW CANON PROPOSED throughout, worked out as the diegetic form of the house's
money=energy=time law, §0 item 5)*

> "Money is energy is time" is not a slogan here. It is a conservation law with an accountant.

### 2.1 The Fold — why it's rare

A small fraction of people are born with a neuro-developmental trait informally called **the
Fold**: a structural quirk that lets a trained nervous system open a stable, narrow aperture onto
**the Outside** — a reservoir beyond the world's four dimensions, inert and unreachable to
everyone else. The Fold is not a skill; it cannot be taught into someone who lacks it, only found.
Estimated incidence: on the order of 1 in 40,000 births. Of those, most Folds are too weak to hold
an aperture open under any load, and a meaningful fraction of the rest do not survive supervised
training (early, unsupervised channeling is close to always fatal — see §2.5). Net result: roughly
1 licensed, working **Channeler** per 700,000–800,000 population, confederacy-wide. Against a
total population in the trillions (§4), this is a genuinely small, genuinely precious labor pool —
which is exactly why it is priced the way §2.7 prices it, and exactly why it is institutionally
guarded rather than left to individuals (§6.2).

### 2.2 The loom — why it needs a building

An aperture opened unassisted collapses in seconds and takes the channeler's nervous system with
it. Every legal channeling event happens inside a **loom**: a purpose-built stabilizing cradle,
expensive, stationary or ship-mounted at significant mass and power cost, that contains the
aperture, meters the draw, and — critically — makes the transaction detectable (§2.4). Looms are
rare infrastructure by design: a handful per Core World, fewer per Established Colony, essentially
none on the Frontier. This gives channeled transport the same texture as the Current's own
chokepoints — a small number of high-value nodes that concentrate both political power and
banditry risk (§6.2's Counting House; the setting's pirates target loom convoys, not just cargo
holds).

### 2.3 What channeling buys — two levers, both bounded by relativity

A channeler at a loom spends drawn energy — **chron**, unit χ — on exactly two things, and the
one conceit is deliberately narrow: it never relaxes c, it only pays to approach it or to
compress subjective time within it.

- **Push** — a direct momentum gift to a hull beyond what its sail's beam budget bought it. Cost
  scales with the *increase* in relativistic kinetic energy demanded, same v²-and-worse curve as
  §1.1 — meaning Push is cheapest as a top-up on an already sail-boosted ship, never a
  replacement for launch infrastructure. A well-funded Push can carry a small, loom-rated hull up
  toward 0.6–0.9c for a single priority run. **It never reaches or exceeds c.** This is "warp
  travel" as the commission asked for it: real, priced, dangerous, and still causally sound.
- **Skip** — accelerating the local arrow of time inside the loom's containment field, for
  whatever mass sits within it. The ship still crosses the gap at whatever speed it's actually
  going, bounded by c like everything else — but the people and cargo inside the field experience
  fewer subjective years for the same span of galactic-frame time. Cost scales with mass in the
  field × the compression ratio × the duration compressed. This is "accelerating the arrow of
  time" exactly as the commission phrased it, and it is the lever that produces the setting's
  Hyperion texture (§5.3) without ever touching causality: **the news a Skip-traveler carries
  still only arrives when their ship physically does.** No channeling event, of either kind, ever
  transmits information faster than a physical arrival. This is the hard rule that keeps §1.3's
  entire governance model intact under the one conceit — stated once here, binding everywhere.

### 2.4 Conservation accounting, part one — the corona

Energy does not appear from nothing inside the four dimensions, even when its ultimate source is
Outside. The instant an aperture opens, the loom must source a matching quantity from within the
world to balance the books locally, and it does so by drawing down the **local flow-rate of time
itself** in a bounded shell around the loom — a **corona**: a physically real, instrumented,
measurable region of clock-rate anomaly surrounding every channeling event, proportional to the χ
drawn, for the duration of the transaction. This is the *immediate*, in-dimension half of the
conservation law — what the channeled energy displaces, right now, is the passage of time in the
volume around the transaction. It is also, deliberately, a detection mechanic: sanctioned looms
are shielded and registered; unlicensed or smuggled channeling still throws a corona, and any
station or patrol ship with a chronometer array can see one forming. This is the setting's
built-in cat-and-mouse hook — smugglers try to mask a corona's signature; the Counting House
(§6.2) exists partly to police it.

### 2.5 Conservation accounting, part two — the Toll

The corona only balances the *local* books. What's actually owed back across the aperture, to the
Outside, is time — and it is collected, deferred, in two separate ledgers.

The first is biological, and it falls on the channeler alone: every χ drawn measurably ages the
channeler's own tissue, faster than the calendar around them. A veteran who has run a career's
worth of Push and Skip jobs looks decades older than their birth-year says — grounded, retired
channelers are a setting-standard image: chronologically young, calendar-young even, and visibly,
irreversibly old. This is **the Toll**, and it is why the Fold, already rare, produces an even
smaller pool of *career* channelers: the trait is common enough to be found regularly; surviving
a working life on it is not.

### 2.6 Conservation accounting, part three — time-debt

The second ledger falls on whoever was carried, and it is the setting's Hyperion mechanic made
literal rather than metaphorical: a fraction of every Skip's temporal displacement is charged
against the *traveler's own worldline*, not just the channeler's body, as **time-debt** — a
standing, portable, checkable number, tracked by the Counting House against the traveler's
identity, not their purse. Debt is not repaid with money. It is repaid by **settling**: living out
ordinary, uncompressed time, proportional to the debt owed, during which the debtor cannot
legally book another Skip. An unpaid debt does not sit quietly — left to accrue past a threshold,
it collects itself involuntarily, in a **snap**: sudden, catastrophic correction, most often
instant aging equivalent to the unpaid years (sometimes fatal), rarest and worst, a traveler found
alive but existing measurably out of phase with everyone's clock but their own — reachable,
present, and unaging until the debt resolves on its own schedule, not theirs.

This is the mechanism behind the commission's own request, almost verbatim: *the person you left
returns older, or not at all.* A pilgrim who Skips to reach a dying relative in time arrives
having spent weeks where their family spent years — and by the time their own debt is settled,
either by choice or by force, the people who didn't travel have simply kept living. Sometimes
there is no one left to go home to. Sometimes going home at all means booking another Skip, adding
debt they cannot afford, and choosing not to.

### 2.7 The chron economy — the literal purchase of time

Ordinary Confederate commerce runs on **credits** (already house canon, §0 item 5). Chron is a
separate, Counting-House-tracked quantity, bought with credits at a posted, heavily regulated,
constantly political exchange rate — **whoever sets that rate controls who, in practice, is
allowed to buy time**, and that fact alone is enough political fuel for a hundred storylets
without needing anything else invented. The purchase chain is exactly the sentence the house
already wrote before this worldbook existed: *credits buy chron, chron buys a channeler's draw
from the Outside, the draw buys Push or Skip.* A channeler moving a ship faster than its sail, or
a family buying their elder a few extra years of witnessed life by Skipping a grandchild home
early, is not a metaphor for purchasing time. It is a line item.

### 2.8 The hard boundary, restated

No channeling event ever exceeds c. No channeling event ever transmits information faster than
its own physical arrival. Every χ drawn is repaid, in time, by someone — the channeler's body, the
traveler's worldline, or both. **These three sentences are load-bearing** (see §8) — everything
else about the conceit's flavor (chron, corona, Toll, snap, the Counting House) is free to be
renamed or reshaped without breaking the setting underneath it.

*(NEW CANON PROPOSED, built to not touch the one hard fact in OWNER CANON: HCS Okaga is a

The word already has exactly one fixed meaning: the proper name of a particular vessel, the
*Human-Confederacy Ship Okaga*, Lakota-named, dinner-plate-and-rotating-tube, currently running

**Proposed extension, for the game to have a title worth wearing:** "Okaga" becomes, by slow
informal drift among the settled worlds, the common noun for the *class* of vessel HCS Okaga
belongs to — colony-and-patrol hulls built to the same dinner-plate-sail-and-tube pattern, running

Citizens say "an Okaga is coming" the way they'd say "a patrol ship," and *the* Okaga — HCS

canon already has her. This gives players a fleet of ships to crew, name, and lose, rather than
one irreplaceable protagonist vessel, without overwriting a single sentence of what's already
written about her.
