# Ruinfold — roadmap

A living roadmap for what to build next on Ruinfold, the browser 3D MMORPG over the **tab** EAVT world-substrate and **voidmath** four-valued bilattice.
This v1 is roadmapped from knowledge of the current codebase; it is being refined by parallel research (next-gen MMORPG design from the web; the repo's own concurrent-game-systems / ludics material; tab's unused capabilities).

## Where we are (shipped + verified) - World substrate: zones + portals, EAVT trace, 5 Hz tick, SSE+POST server, three.js client. - Combat: melee + four abilities (stamina, cooldowns), the shared `strike` primitive. - Death: the five-way bilattice router (undead ⊤ / mortal f / construct ⊥ / boss f / cursed-form ⊤). - Loot + equipment (slots, archetypes, stat derivation), inventory. - Progression: xp / levels / stat scaling. - Quests (data-driven bounties), NPCs, vendor economy (gold), zone chat. - AI v2 (acquire / leash / engage / patrol, ranged mobs), out-of-combat regen. - 67 headless assertions green; live HTTP/SSE playthrough green.

## Design north star We are not chasing feature-parity with a generic MMO.
The substrate makes three things *uniquely* buildable, and the roadmap is weighted toward them: 1. **Perception is paraconsistent** — `observing`/`perceives` lets each player settle a *different* world from one trace (fog of war, hidden undead, unreliable senses) for free.
2. **The world is a forkable, replayable trace** — `settle-forks` + `history` give instances, rewind, death-recaps, and parallel timelines almost for nothing.
3. **Interaction can be modeled as a game** — the repo's `concurrent-game-systems` + ludics let us resolve PvP / negotiation / contested objectives as *strategies interacting*, not ad-hoc rules.
This is the headline "next-gen" direction the rest of the roadmap supports.

## Batch 1 — combat & character depth (independent engine modules) - **Status effects** (`engine/effects.mjs`): timed buffs/debuffs/DoT (poison, stun, regen, might) applied as cells with an `expires-at` tick; the tick ages and fires them.
Bilattice-native: a "petrified AND moving" contested state can settle ⊤. - **Threat / aggro tables** (`engine/threat.mjs`): monsters target highest accumulated threat (damage + heals nearby), not just nearest — enables tanking.
AI reads threat instead of pure distance. - **Skill-by-use progression** (`engine/skills.mjs`): Project-Gorgon-style — using an ability levels *that* skill; skills unlock ability ranks. xp stays for character level; skills add a second axis. - **Tab-target + target frame**: client target selection already partial; add cycling + a target HUD.

## Batch 2 — social & economy (the "massively multiplayer" part) - **Parties** (`engine/party.mjs`): group membership, shared xp/loot in a zone, party chat channel. - **Player-to-player trade** (`engine/playertrade.mjs`): a two-sided escrowed trade (both confirm). - **Crafting** (`engine/crafting.mjs`): recipes consume items → produce items; wrap tab's `craft`. - **Auction / player shops**: list items for gold; a market board NPC. - **Whispers / channels**: `/tell`, zone vs party vs global chat scopes (extends chat).

## Batch 3 — substrate-unique systems (the differentiators) - **Fog of war via `observing`** (`engine/perception.mjs`): the snapshot becomes per-player — settle each player's frontier through their `perceives` Umwelt.
Stealth, scouting, an undead you only see if you carry the bone-charm.
(Today the snapshot is omniscient.) - **Instances & rewind via `forking`**: a dungeon is a fork of the trace; party gets its own copy; death-recap replays the last N ticks (`history`).
Boss arenas as forks. - **Dynamic world events** (`engine/events.mjs`): tab-style ambient ticking — a tide of undead, a blood moon (buffs undead), a wandering boss; the world acts on itself between turns. - **Federation via `federate`**: multiple world-servers as shards; cross-shard travel/chat.

## Batch 4 — the headline: ludics-modeled player interaction (`engine/ludics.mjs`) Model a contested interaction between two parties (a PvP duel, a haggle, a standoff over an objective, an NPC debate) as **two strategies/designs interacting** in the sense of Girard's ludics / concurrent game semantics, resolved by normalization to a bilattice outcome (win/lose/⊤ deadlock/⊥ abandoned).
Grounded in the repo's `concurrent-game-systems` (player tuples) and voidmath's FOUR.
Exact data model + resolution procedure to be set by the research agents' findings.
This is where "computing concurrent game systems / players-as-ludics" becomes a real mechanic, not a metaphor.

## Cross-cutting / infra - **Accounts & durable identity**: today an actor id lives in localStorage; add a claim/login so a character is durable and not spoofable.
(The trace already persists the character.) - **Log compaction**: append-only logs grow without bound; a periodic rewrite keeping surviving functional rows + history.
(Flagged in README as out-of-scope for v0 — time to schedule it.) - **Server `/health`** endpoint for systemd/uptime checks. - **Spatial interest management**: only send a player deltas for their zone/AoI (snapshot already scopes by zone — formalize and cap broadcast fan-out as player counts grow).

## Sequencing Batches 1–3 are mostly independent engine modules that fan out cleanly to concurrent agents against the existing `_world` / `strike` / `tick` contracts.
Batch 4 (ludics) waits on the research; it is the integrative centerpiece the others feed.

## Research findings → decisions (2026-06) Two parallel web agents (next-gen MMORPG design; ludics/game-semantics) and two repo agents (concurrent-game-systems/ludics; tab's unused modules) reported.
Decisions:

- **Architecture is validated, not exotic.** Valve's Source is a tick + snapshot + client-interp model (≈100 ms interp buffer); EVE runs a *single shard at 1 Hz* for tens of thousands.
  Our 5 Hz
  + SSE snapshots + three.js interpolation is exactly this lineage. → add a **client interpolation buffer** and **area-of-interest** gating before scaling player counts.
- **Web "top 5 fit our model": ** tick-folded **status effects + threat**, **AoI on the SSE stream**, **client interpolation**, **skill-by-use + gear affixes**, **auction/order-book**.
  Deferred as fighting a 200 ms tick: action/aim combat and client-side movement prediction+rollback.
- **The repo already has the ludics ground.** `development/lab/concurrent-game-systems` (players / action-profiles / strategies / coalitions); `development/lab/swarm/src/players.mjs` `buildPlayerTuple()` binds a player to a CGS arena (`arenaFormula: "A⊥ || B"`, observe=opponent / act=player polarity events, handedness recv/send/actuate/observe); and `…/archive/.../ludics/questions/girard-caillois-substrate-correspondence.md` maps ludics↔bilattice (⊤ = play's held ambiguity; agon/alea/mimicry/ilinx as algebra).
  The ludics engine reuses the player-tuple shape rather than inventing one.
- **Ludics resolution model (from the game-semantics agent):** a *design* is a JSON tree of polarized addressed moves `(±, locus, ramification)`; `normalize(A, B)` steps them (Curien's rule R) to one of: **† converges** → win **t** / lose **f** (by who conceded), **deadlock** (no matching move) → **⊤**, **divergence** (fuel out / disengage) → **⊥**.
  Outcome IS a FOUR value, composes via the bilattice.
  Implementable in plain JS over the append-only log.
- **Tab modules → features (value/effort, from the tab agent):** `practice` → skill-by-use (evidence settles a skill cell t/f/⊤); `observing`+`perceives` → fog of war; `trade` → economy; `craft` → crafting; `grow` → procedural Fibonacci dungeons; `federate` → cross-shard; `history` → quest/lore replay; `monologue` → NPC inner conflict from ⊤ cells; `settle-forks` → branching timelines.
  We wrap these rather than reimplement.

## Status after the concurrent build (2026-06) **Built + unit-tested (9 modules):** effects, threat, skills, perception, crafting, playertrade, party, events, ludics — each by its own agent, each with an inline proof.

**Wired into the live game + integration-tested (`tests/prove-systems.mjs`, full suite 75 green):** - threat → `combat.strike` accrues it, `ai` targets top-threat over nearest (tanking), `death` clears it. - world events → `tick` rotates them (`tickEvents`); `ai` reads blood-moon/undead-tide modifiers (undead get wider aggro + harder hits). - status effects → processed every tick (`tickEffects` for all entities); abilities apply riders (heavy→stun, bolt→poison); poison/regen tick, stun/might/weaken are read by combat. - skill-by-use → attacking/abilities call `practiceSkill` (a `blade`/`sorcery`/… skill levels by use). - crafting, party, player-trade → reachable as validated intents (craft / party-create|join|leave / trade-open|offer|confirm|cancel). - snapshot now carries effects / skills / party / active-event for each player.

**Client overhaul (gamey pass) — landed:** the client was refactored into an orchestrator (`main.mjs`) + a `state.mjs` store that diffs snapshots into semantic events (damage/heal/died/ levelup/effect/loot/chat/world-event), with seven modules built by concurrent agents and wired in: `audio` (synth Web-Audio SFX), `world` (gradient sky, fog, shadowed moonlight, flickering torches, procedural ground + ruined props), `entities` (per-type models, nameplates + HP bars, target ring, attack/hit/death juice, floating damage numbers, ⊤/effect visuals), `hud` (player/target/party frames, effect chips, event banner, quest tracker), `actionbar` (canvas ability icons + cooldown sweeps + stamina gating), `panels` (inventory / character+skills / shop / quest / craft windows), `chat` (chat + combat log + minimap).
All 9 client files parse and serve (200); browser-rendered look is the user's to confirm.

**Built but NOT yet wired (deferred, clearly noted):** - **perception / fog-of-war** — `engine/perception.mjs` is ready (`visibleTo`, sight + Umwelt + hidden-undead rule), but wiring it changes broadcast from one shared delta to per-player deltas (each connection tracks its own last-seen set).
A focused follow-up on `loop.mjs`/`snapshot.mjs`. - **ludics duels** — `engine/ludics.mjs` (designs + normalize → t/f/⊤/⊥) is ready and tested; needs a duel/negotiation intent + a way to build each side's design from player moves, plus client UX.
The headline still to land. - **client UI** for the above (effect icons, skill panel, party frame, craft/shop/trade windows, event banner) — the data flows in the snapshot; the three.js/DOM surface for it is not built this round. - AoI gating, client interpolation buffer, log compaction, accounts — infra from the brief, not started.

## Dispatched build (concurrent agents, one new engine file each) effects · threat · skills(practice) · perception(observing/fog) · crafting(craft) · playertrade(trade) · party · events · **ludics** — then integrated into tick/snapshot/actions/ai by the main thread, with tests.
New functional predicates these need are already added to RUIN_FUNCTIONAL (effect-*, threat-table, party-*, trade-*, world-event/event-until).

Sources for the above are recorded in the dispatch and the agents' reports (Valve/EVE netcode, Project Gorgon skills, Girard *Locus Solum* / Curien ludics intro, Belnap four-valued logic).

- **Server = authoritative scalar state + bilattice truth.** Positions are plain numbers (`pos-x`/`pos-y`/`pos-z`) on EAVT rows; the server only does scalar arithmetic (step toward a goal, clamp to a zone, a `dx²+dz²` melee range gate).
  The bilattice governs the *truth* of state — `alive`, `form` — over FOUR (⊥ unknown · t true · f false · ⊤ contradiction-held-as-a-value).
- **Client = all geometry.** Every vector/matrix/projection/camera/interpolation operation is browser-side three.js.
  The snapshot JSON is the only contract, and it carries plain numbers plus bilattice glyphs.

## The five deaths (the headline)

Every monster declares `slain` the **converse** of `alive` at seed, so a killing blow's `slain` row folds as *negative* evidence into the `alive`-cell.
What that cell settles to is then chosen by the entity's `death-rule` — same evidence, five readings:

| death-rule | bilattice | what happens |
|---|---|---|
| `undead` | `alive` → **⊤** | alive AND slain — a held contradiction. Heals, scars (`alive-revives`++), stays ⊤, **rises again**. |
| `mortal` (monster) | `alive` → **f** | a corpse; respawns on cooldown. |
| `mortal` (player) | ghost | no corpse: `status`→ghost, `form`→ghost. Walk to a shrine to re-embody, or respawn at the gate. |
| `named` (boss) | `alive` → **f** | true death; drops loot; long respawn. |
| `construct` | `alive` → **⊥** | un-made: both faces retracted, no corpse, reforms elsewhere. |
| `cursed` | corpse + **curse** | the slain monster dies like a boss, but its slayer's `human` cell is contradicted by a `beast` row (its converse) → **⊤**, a permanent, irreversible dual identity (lycanthropy). |

The branch is driven entirely by **data** (the `death-rule` row and the presence of a converse declaration) — there is no per-entity death code anywhere.
This is voidmath's point: a contradiction is a *value the world can hold and render*, not a crash.
(Death-model flavor draws on Project Gorgon's varied, permanent deaths.)

## How it is built

```
engine/
  functional.mjs   RUIN_FUNCTIONAL (health/position/level/stamina/gold/cooldowns… latest-t-wins) + clock(tick,seq)
  _world.mjs       shared readers over tab's settle: view / valOf / numOf / glyphOf / posOf / dist2 / zoneOf
  archetypes.mjs   the item catalogue (slot, grants, value); an item instance points at an archetype
  stats.mjs        derive attack/armor/health from level + equipped gear (one source of truth)
  combat.mjs       strike() shared damage primitive; attack() = melee range gate + strike
  abilities.mjs    Heavy / Cleave / Bolt / Mend — stamina costs, cooldowns, melee+ranged+AoE
  death.mjs        the 5-way bilattice router + respawns + ghost embody
  movement.mjs     scalar step toward a goal / WASD nudge, clamped to the zone
  ai.mjs           generic monster turn (acquire / leash / engage / patrol) — behaviour is data
  items.mjs        pickup/drop/equip/unequip/grant/destroy via `changing` located-in
  loot.mjs         spawn drops + gold at a corpse (from the monster's `drops` data)
  progression.mjs  xp / leveling / stat scaling (pure curve)
  quests.mjs       accept / track-by-kill / turn-in bounties (data on a quest-giver NPC)
  vendor.mjs       buy / sell against an NPC's stock, priced from archetypes
  regen.mjs        out-of-combat health + stamina regeneration
  zones.mjs        spawn + portal traversal across zones
  snapshot.mjs     settle dirty subjects → compact client JSON (incl. inventory/gear/bounty/cooldowns)
  tick.mjs         one advance: intents → AI → deaths → rewards(xp/gold/loot/bounty) → respawns → regen
server/
  http.mjs   sse.mjs   actions.mjs   loop.mjs   bin/{ruinfold,seed}.mjs   (pure node:http, zero deps)
client/
  index.html (three.js CDN import-map)   main.mjs (scene/SSE-reconcile/input/nameplates/damage)   ui.mjs (HUD/hotbar/pack/shop/dialogue/chat)
tests/
  prove-combat   prove-undeath   prove-deaths   prove-abilities   prove-quests   prove-economy
```

Built on `@561/development.lab.tab`: `doing`/`changing` append to the trace, `being`/`settle` fold it, the converse declaration makes `slain` negative evidence, and the thin bilattice supplies the FOUR values.
Ruinfold writes its **own** tick (tab's farstone `ticking` is hardcoded to a harbor) and reuses only the substrate operations underneath.

### Notes & limits

- **Single-writer discipline:** HTTP POSTs only *queue* intents; the tick is the only thing that ever appends, so concurrent players can never race the log.
- **Append-only growth:** functional supersession keeps *settle* cost bounded by the latest row per predicate, but the log files grow unbounded — log compaction is out of scope for this v0.
- **`located-in` is dual-filed**, and supersede collapses a functional predicate across a whole log regardless of `e`; an entity's true place is therefore read via `zoneOf` (tab's `locationOf`, which filters `e===id`), never via a settled `located-in` cell.
- The client loads three.js from `unpkg` — the browser needs internet; the server ships no JS dependencies.

## Test

```sh
pnpm --filter @561/development.experimental.ruinfold test
```

Three headless proofs drive the engine over throwaway worlds: combat is a state-transition with attribution; undeath settles `alive` to ⊤ and rises (and a thing without the converse never can); and the five death-rules each route to their bilattice value, with loot, curse, and respawn.

# Ruinfold — roadmap

A living roadmap for what to build next on Ruinfold, the browser 3D MMORPG over the **tab** EAVT world-substrate and **voidmath** four-valued bilattice.
This v1 is roadmapped from knowledge of the current codebase; it is being refined by parallel research (next-gen MMORPG design from the web; the repo's own concurrent-game-systems / ludics material; tab's unused capabilities).

## Where we are (shipped + verified) - World substrate: zones + portals, EAVT trace, 5 Hz tick, SSE+POST server, three.js client. - Combat: melee + four abilities (stamina, cooldowns), the shared `strike` primitive. - Death: the five-way bilattice router (undead ⊤ / mortal f / construct ⊥ / boss f / cursed-form ⊤). - Loot + equipment (slots, archetypes, stat derivation), inventory. - Progression: xp / levels / stat scaling. - Quests (data-driven bounties), NPCs, vendor economy (gold), zone chat. - AI v2 (acquire / leash / engage / patrol, ranged mobs), out-of-combat regen. - 67 headless assertions green; live HTTP/SSE playthrough green.

## Design north star We are not chasing feature-parity with a generic MMO.
The substrate makes three things *uniquely* buildable, and the roadmap is weighted toward them: 1. **Perception is paraconsistent** — `observing`/`perceives` lets each player settle a *different* world from one trace (fog of war, hidden undead, unreliable senses) for free.
2. **The world is a forkable, replayable trace** — `settle-forks` + `history` give instances, rewind, death-recaps, and parallel timelines almost for nothing.
3. **Interaction can be modeled as a game** — the repo's `concurrent-game-systems` + ludics let us resolve PvP / negotiation / contested objectives as *strategies interacting*, not ad-hoc rules.
This is the headline "next-gen" direction the rest of the roadmap supports.

## Batch 1 — combat & character depth (independent engine modules) - **Status effects** (`engine/effects.mjs`): timed buffs/debuffs/DoT (poison, stun, regen, might) applied as cells with an `expires-at` tick; the tick ages and fires them.
Bilattice-native: a "petrified AND moving" contested state can settle ⊤. - **Threat / aggro tables** (`engine/threat.mjs`): monsters target highest accumulated threat (damage + heals nearby), not just nearest — enables tanking.
AI reads threat instead of pure distance. - **Skill-by-use progression** (`engine/skills.mjs`): Project-Gorgon-style — using an ability levels *that* skill; skills unlock ability ranks. xp stays for character level; skills add a second axis. - **Tab-target + target frame**: client target selection already partial; add cycling + a target HUD.

## Batch 2 — social & economy (the "massively multiplayer" part) - **Parties** (`engine/party.mjs`): group membership, shared xp/loot in a zone, party chat channel. - **Player-to-player trade** (`engine/playertrade.mjs`): a two-sided escrowed trade (both confirm). - **Crafting** (`engine/crafting.mjs`): recipes consume items → produce items; wrap tab's `craft`. - **Auction / player shops**: list items for gold; a market board NPC. - **Whispers / channels**: `/tell`, zone vs party vs global chat scopes (extends chat).

## Batch 3 — substrate-unique systems (the differentiators) - **Fog of war via `observing`** (`engine/perception.mjs`): the snapshot becomes per-player — settle each player's frontier through their `perceives` Umwelt.
Stealth, scouting, an undead you only see if you carry the bone-charm.
(Today the snapshot is omniscient.) - **Instances & rewind via `forking`**: a dungeon is a fork of the trace; party gets its own copy; death-recap replays the last N ticks (`history`).
Boss arenas as forks. - **Dynamic world events** (`engine/events.mjs`): tab-style ambient ticking — a tide of undead, a blood moon (buffs undead), a wandering boss; the world acts on itself between turns. - **Federation via `federate`**: multiple world-servers as shards; cross-shard travel/chat.

## Batch 4 — the headline: ludics-modeled player interaction (`engine/ludics.mjs`) Model a contested interaction between two parties (a PvP duel, a haggle, a standoff over an objective, an NPC debate) as **two strategies/designs interacting** in the sense of Girard's ludics / concurrent game semantics, resolved by normalization to a bilattice outcome (win/lose/⊤ deadlock/⊥ abandoned).
Grounded in the repo's `concurrent-game-systems` (player tuples) and voidmath's FOUR.
Exact data model + resolution procedure to be set by the research agents' findings.
This is where "computing concurrent game systems / players-as-ludics" becomes a real mechanic, not a metaphor.

## Cross-cutting / infra - **Accounts & durable identity**: today an actor id lives in localStorage; add a claim/login so a character is durable and not spoofable.
(The trace already persists the character.) - **Log compaction**: append-only logs grow without bound; a periodic rewrite keeping surviving functional rows + history.
(Flagged in README as out-of-scope for v0 — time to schedule it.) - **Server `/health`** endpoint for systemd/uptime checks. - **Spatial interest management**: only send a player deltas for their zone/AoI (snapshot already scopes by zone — formalize and cap broadcast fan-out as player counts grow).

## Sequencing Batches 1–3 are mostly independent engine modules that fan out cleanly to concurrent agents against the existing `_world` / `strike` / `tick` contracts.
Batch 4 (ludics) waits on the research; it is the integrative centerpiece the others feed.

## Research findings → decisions (2026-06) Two parallel web agents (next-gen MMORPG design; ludics/game-semantics) and two repo agents (concurrent-game-systems/ludics; tab's unused modules) reported.
Decisions:

- **Architecture is validated, not exotic.** Valve's Source is a tick + snapshot + client-interp model (≈100 ms interp buffer); EVE runs a *single shard at 1 Hz* for tens of thousands.
  Our 5 Hz
  + SSE snapshots + three.js interpolation is exactly this lineage. → add a **client interpolation buffer** and **area-of-interest** gating before scaling player counts.
- **Web "top 5 fit our model": ** tick-folded **status effects + threat**, **AoI on the SSE stream**, **client interpolation**, **skill-by-use + gear affixes**, **auction/order-book**.
  Deferred as fighting a 200 ms tick: action/aim combat and client-side movement prediction+rollback.
- **The repo already has the ludics ground.** `development/lab/concurrent-game-systems` (players / action-profiles / strategies / coalitions); `development/lab/swarm/src/players.mjs` `buildPlayerTuple()` binds a player to a CGS arena (`arenaFormula: "A⊥ || B"`, observe=opponent / act=player polarity events, handedness recv/send/actuate/observe); and `…/archive/.../ludics/questions/girard-caillois-substrate-correspondence.md` maps ludics↔bilattice (⊤ = play's held ambiguity; agon/alea/mimicry/ilinx as algebra).
  The ludics engine reuses the player-tuple shape rather than inventing one.
- **Ludics resolution model (from the game-semantics agent):** a *design* is a JSON tree of polarized addressed moves `(±, locus, ramification)`; `normalize(A, B)` steps them (Curien's rule R) to one of: **† converges** → win **t** / lose **f** (by who conceded), **deadlock** (no matching move) → **⊤**, **divergence** (fuel out / disengage) → **⊥**.
  Outcome IS a FOUR value, composes via the bilattice.
  Implementable in plain JS over the append-only log.
- **Tab modules → features (value/effort, from the tab agent):** `practice` → skill-by-use (evidence settles a skill cell t/f/⊤); `observing`+`perceives` → fog of war; `trade` → economy; `craft` → crafting; `grow` → procedural Fibonacci dungeons; `federate` → cross-shard; `history` → quest/lore replay; `monologue` → NPC inner conflict from ⊤ cells; `settle-forks` → branching timelines.
  We wrap these rather than reimplement.

## Status after the concurrent build (2026-06) **Built + unit-tested (9 modules):** effects, threat, skills, perception, crafting, playertrade, party, events, ludics — each by its own agent, each with an inline proof.

**Wired into the live game + integration-tested (`tests/prove-systems.mjs`, full suite 75 green):** - threat → `combat.strike` accrues it, `ai` targets top-threat over nearest (tanking), `death` clears it. - world events → `tick` rotates them (`tickEvents`); `ai` reads blood-moon/undead-tide modifiers (undead get wider aggro + harder hits). - status effects → processed every tick (`tickEffects` for all entities); abilities apply riders (heavy→stun, bolt→poison); poison/regen tick, stun/might/weaken are read by combat. - skill-by-use → attacking/abilities call `practiceSkill` (a `blade`/`sorcery`/… skill levels by use). - crafting, party, player-trade → reachable as validated intents (craft / party-create|join|leave / trade-open|offer|confirm|cancel). - snapshot now carries effects / skills / party / active-event for each player.

**Client overhaul (gamey pass) — landed:** the client was refactored into an orchestrator (`main.mjs`) + a `state.mjs` store that diffs snapshots into semantic events (damage/heal/died/ levelup/effect/loot/chat/world-event), with seven modules built by concurrent agents and wired in: `audio` (synth Web-Audio SFX), `world` (gradient sky, fog, shadowed moonlight, flickering torches, procedural ground + ruined props), `entities` (per-type models, nameplates + HP bars, target ring, attack/hit/death juice, floating damage numbers, ⊤/effect visuals), `hud` (player/target/party frames, effect chips, event banner, quest tracker), `actionbar` (canvas ability icons + cooldown sweeps + stamina gating), `panels` (inventory / character+skills / shop / quest / craft windows), `chat` (chat + combat log + minimap).
All 9 client files parse and serve (200); browser-rendered look is the user's to confirm.

**Built but NOT yet wired (deferred, clearly noted):** - **perception / fog-of-war** — `engine/perception.mjs` is ready (`visibleTo`, sight + Umwelt + hidden-undead rule), but wiring it changes broadcast from one shared delta to per-player deltas (each connection tracks its own last-seen set).
A focused follow-up on `loop.mjs`/`snapshot.mjs`. - **ludics duels** — `engine/ludics.mjs` (designs + normalize → t/f/⊤/⊥) is ready and tested; needs a duel/negotiation intent + a way to build each side's design from player moves, plus client UX.
The headline still to land. - **client UI** for the above (effect icons, skill panel, party frame, craft/shop/trade windows, event banner) — the data flows in the snapshot; the three.js/DOM surface for it is not built this round. - AoI gating, client interpolation buffer, log compaction, accounts — infra from the brief, not started.

## Dispatched build (concurrent agents, one new engine file each) effects · threat · skills(practice) · perception(observing/fog) · crafting(craft) · playertrade(trade) · party · events · **ludics** — then integrated into tick/snapshot/actions/ai by the main thread, with tests.
New functional predicates these need are already added to RUIN_FUNCTIONAL (effect-*, threat-table, party-*, trade-*, world-event/event-until).

Sources for the above are recorded in the dispatch and the agents' reports (Valve/EVE netcode, Project Gorgon skills, Girard *Locus Solum* / Curien ludics intro, Belnap four-valued logic).

rooms.body:
# Ruinfold — a browser-based 3D MMORPG over tab + voidmath

## Context

The user wants a browser-based 3D MMORPG built in Node, reusing this repo's infrastructure: the **voidmath** four-valued bilattice (the "next-gen math system") and the **tab** EAVT world-substrate (the "cleaned up kernel" / world engine).
The target package already exists in charter but is empty: `development/experimental/ruinfold/` contains **only** `package.json`.
Its description already fixes the design intent:

> "browser-based 3D hack-and-slash MMORPG over the tab EAVT world-substrate and the voidmath four-valued bilattice.
> The world IS its append-only trace, folded (settled) every tick; death is paraconsistent — a slain undead settles its `alive` cell to ⊤ (alive AND slain, a held situation) and rises again.
> Server is pure Node http (SSE + POST, zero server deps); the 3D client loads three.js in the browser from a CDN import-map."

This plan fills that empty package into a working game.
The user chose **broad MMORPG scope** (multiple zones, items/inventory/loot, XP/leveling, several monster types — on top of a complete playable slice), **both click-to-move and WASD** controls, and asked for a **weird, varied death model inspired by Project Gorgon** — different death semantics per *kind* of death, not one rule.

## The honest division of labor (a repo constraint, stated plainly)

This repo rederives knowledge from the ground up and the kernel does **not** contain 3D geometry — voidmath is a *bilattice logic*, not linear algebra.
So:

- **Server = authoritative scalar state + bilattice truth.** Positions are plain numbers stored as EAVT predicates; the server does only scalar arithmetic (step toward target, clamp to bounds, melee `dx²+dz²` range checks).
  The bilattice governs *truth of state* (alive / dead / undead / cursed).
- **Client = all rendering geometry.** Every vec/matrix/projection/camera/ interpolation operation is browser-side **three.js**.
  The snapshot JSON is the only contract between them and carries plain numbers + bilattice glyphs.

This division is deliberate and should be written into the code comments.

## Substrate API to reuse (do NOT reinvent — import these)

From `@561/development.lab.tab` (paths under `development/lab/tab/`):

- `doing({ root, agent, subject, predicate, object, t })` — append an EAVT row `{e,a,v,t}` (+ reified `enacted-by` if `agent`).
  `being/doing/scripts/doing.mjs`
- `declareConverse(root, subject, p, q, t)` / `retract({root,subject,predicate,t})` — same file.
- `changing(args)` — `doing` for FUNCTIONAL (latest-t-wins) predicates.
  `being/doing/changing/scripts/changing.mjs`
- `being(subject, rows, opts)` → `{entity, fiber:[{predicate,object,value:{pos,neg,glyph},observers}]}`.
  `being/scripts/being.mjs`
- substrate (`@561/development.lab.tab/substrate`): `append`, `rowsFor`, `subjects`, `allRows`, `supersede`, `frontier`, `containedBy`, `locationOf`, `settle(root,subject,opts)`, and the sets `RELATIONAL`, `FUNCTIONAL`.
  `scripts/_substrate.mjs`
- `observing({root,observer,subject})` / `look(...)
  `.
  `being/doing/observing/scripts/observing.mjs`
- value (`being/library/value/scripts/value.mjs`): `BOTTOM`, `value(pos,neg)`, `knowledgeJoin`, `neg`, `glyph`, `holds`.
  Charge ∈ {0,1}² over FOUR: ⊥(0,0) unknown · t(1,0) true · f(0,1) false · ⊤(1,1) contradiction.

**Key mechanism:** a row `{e:p, a:"has-converse", v:q}` makes `being` fold every `q`-row as `neg(value(1,0))` into the p-cell.
Asserting `p` **and** `q` ⇒ `knowledgeJoin((1,0),(0,1)) = (1,1) = ⊤`.
This is the death engine.

**Important:** tab's own `ticking.mjs` is hardcoded to the "farstone" demo world (harbor/marsh/ferry/bell).
Ruinfold writes its **own** engine tick reusing `changing`/`doing`/`observing`/`being`/substrate — it does not reuse farstone's.

## The weird death model (the headline — bilattice × Project Gorgon)

Each entity carries a data predicate `death-rule` (set at seed).
On `slain`, the engine routes the entity's `alive`/`form` cells to a **different bilattice value per death kind** — death is not one rule, it is five.
Project Gorgon's signature (a death *choice*; permanent, irreversible curses; per-curse reversal) maps onto the four FOUR-values plus a ghost limbo:

| death-rule | bilattice outcome | behavior (PG touchstone) |
|---|---|---|
| `mortal` (players) | `alive` → **f**, new `ghost` form at **t** | Body falls (f). You wander as a ghost (a t-form on a spirit body) and must reach a **shrine** to re-embody, OR "enter the light" → respawn at zone start. PG's death window. |
| `undead` (skeleton/zombie) | `alive` → **⊤** (slain ⊣ alive) | Held contradiction: alive AND slain. Heals to full, **stays ⊤ forever**, renders flickering, rises again on each kill. The charter's headline. |
| `cursed` (lycanthrope etc.) | `form` → **⊤** (human AND beast), permanent | Dying while bitten makes `form` a held dual identity that **can never be retracted** (PG lycanthropy is permanent). Toggling between faces costs N kills as beast. |
| `named`/`boss` | `alive` → **f**, settled | True death: drops a loot bundle, `status:dead`, very long or no respawn. The clean f. |
| `construct`/`illusion` | `alive` → **⊥** (vanish) | Returns to mystery/relationlessness — no corpse, no loot, simply un-made. Mirrors the kernel's void cone. |

`engine/death.mjs` reads each newly-`slain` entity's `death-rule` and applies the matching morphism sequence.
The branch is driven purely by **data** (the `death-rule` row + the presence/absence of a `has-converse` declaration), not by hardcoded per-entity code — exactly tab's "an NPC IS its fiber" philosophy.

## Broad MMORPG systems (layered on the slice)

- **Zones + portals:** each zone is a place subject with `pos-*` bounds + a ground size; `exit-to`/portal predications (RELATIONAL, dual-filed) move a player's `located-in` to another zone.
  The snapshot is scoped to the viewer's current zone (settle only co-located subjects via `containedBy`).
- **Items / inventory / loot:** items are subjects with `located-in` = a player (carried) or a place (on ground).
  Pickup/drop = `changing` `located-in`.
  Loot bundles spawn at boss `named` death.
  Equipment modifies `attack-power`/`armor`.
- **XP / leveling:** killing appends `xp` (functional, accumulating via a running total recomputed at settle); crossing thresholds bumps `level`, which scales `max-health`/`attack-power`.
  Stored as plain numeric predicates.
- **Monster types:** `skeleton` (undead/⊤), `goblin` (mortal), `wraith` (construct/⊥-vanish), a `lycanthrope` carrier, and a zone `boss` (named/f).
  All behavior is `intends` data rules (`{when:{predicate,object}, do:{...}}
  `) consumed by a generic AI — no per-monster code.

## Module / file tree to create under `ruinfold/`

```
engine/
  functional.mjs   RUIN_FUNCTIONAL set (FUNCTIONAL ∪ {health,pos-x,pos-y,pos-z,
                   facing,status,form,level,xp,respawn-at,alive-revives}) + clock(tick,seq)
                   → zero-padded `t` string. SINGLE source of `t` (lexical==chrono order).
  tick.mjs         ruinfold's own ticking: drain player intents → monster AI →
                   combat → resolve deaths (death.mjs) → respawns → bump tick. Returns {tick,dirty}.
  ai.mjs           generic intends-rule AI (data, not code); adds combat/chase intents.
  combat.mjs       attack(): scalar range gate, `changing` health down, `doing` slain on ≤0.
  death.mjs        resolveDeaths(): the 5-way death-rule router (table above) + resolveRespawns / ghost-run.
  movement.mjs     scalar step toward move-target or WASD delta; clamp to zone bounds; write pos-*/facing.
  items.mjs        pickup/drop/equip via `changing` located-in; loot bundle spawn.
  progression.mjs  xp award, level thresholds, stat scaling.
  zones.mjs        portal traversal (located-in across zones); zone bounds + spawn points.
  snapshot.mjs     settle dirty subjects (RUIN_FUNCTIONAL) → compact client JSON; in-mem cache + deltas.
server/
  http.mjs         pure node:http router: GET / , GET /client/* , GET /events (SSE), POST /act.
  sse.mjs          SSE client registry, broadcast(full|delta), heartbeat, dead-client GC.
  loop.mjs         setInterval(200ms) tick driver: engineTick → resettle dirty → broadcast delta. Overrun guard.
  actions.mjs      validate + QUEUE POSTed join/move/attack/pickup/portal intents (single-writer discipline).
  bin/
    ruinfold.mjs   start: boot http + loop.
    seed.mjs       build the world by `doing`: zones, portals, monsters w/ intends + death-rule,
                   declare slain⊣alive for undead, shrines, starter items. Idempotent (rm world/ first).
client/
  index.html       import-map → three.js ESM from CDN (https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js,
                   pinned; jsDelivr fallback) + <canvas> + module entry.
  main.mjs         three scene/camera/renderer; EventSource('/events') reconcile meshes by id;
                   60fps lerp between 5Hz snapshots; click-to-move (raycast ground) + WASD + click-attack;
                   per-bilattice-glyph visual treatment (⊤ undead = flicker + floating ⊤ sprite;
                   f dead = collapsed/desaturated; ⊥ vanish = fade out; ghost = translucent).
  ui.mjs           health/xp/level HUD, inventory panel, the PG-style death window (respawn / enter the light).
tests/
  prove-combat.mjs   headless: attack reduces health (functional latest-t wins); fatal hit appends slain
                     w/ correct attribution; out-of-range = no-op.
  prove-undeath.mjs  headless: undead `alive` settles to ⊤ (pos==1&&neg==1, glyph "⊤"); rises (health
                     restored, alive-revives++); stays ⊤; a mortal w/o converse never reaches ⊤.
  prove-deaths.mjs   headless: each death-rule routes to its bilattice value (f boss / ⊥ construct /
                     ⊤ cursed-form / ghost mortal). Proves the router is data-driven.
world/             generated by seed (gitignore). The on-disk EAVT trace.
README.md          what ruinfold is, how to run, the death model, the server/client division.
```

All imports honor the existing package.json map: `#substrate`, `#doing`, `#changing`, `#observing`, `#value` (from tab); `#engine/*`, `#server/*` (local).
`package.json` `test` script currently lists `prove-combat` + `prove-undeath`; extend it to add `prove-deaths`.

## Critical implementation details (load-bearing)

1. **`t` is a lexically-ordered string** and functional supersession compares it as a string.
  Use `clock(tick, seq)` → `"tick:000042/seq:0007"` (both zero-padded) so order is correct past 9 sub-events.
  One source in `functional.mjs`.
2. **Extend the functional set.** tab's `FUNCTIONAL` lacks health/position.
  Pass `opts.functional: RUIN_FUNCTIONAL` on **every** `settle`/`supersede` so position/health/level are latest-t-wins.
  This is the key integration decision.
3. **Single-writer discipline.** POST `/act` only *queues* intents; **all** appends happen inside `engine/tick.mjs`.
  Guard the interval with a `running` flag so a slow tick can't overlap the next (coalesce).
4. **Dirty-set snapshots.** Settle only subjects the tick touched; static geometry (zones/scenery) settled once at boot and cached.
  SSE sends `full` on connect, `delta` (only changed + `removed`) each tick.
  5 Hz server tick; client lerps at 60 fps.
5. **Append-only growth** is acknowledged: settle cost is bounded by latest-row-per- predicate, parse cost grows; compaction is out of scope for v0 — note it in README.

## Build approach — concurrent agents

The user asked for concurrent agents.
Build in dependency order; fan out within each layer.
Suggested orchestration (a Workflow or parallel Agent fan-out):

- **Phase A (foundation, sequential first):** `engine/functional.mjs` + `server/bin/seed.mjs` skeleton + a minimal world — everything else depends on the `t` clock, RUIN_FUNCTIONAL, and a seeded world to run against.
- **Phase B (engine, parallel agents):** combat.mjs, death.mjs, movement.mjs, items.mjs, progression.mjs, zones.mjs, ai.mjs, snapshot.mjs — each an agent, all importing the Phase-A contracts. tick.mjs integrates them (after they land).
- **Phase C (server, parallel):** http.mjs, sse.mjs, actions.mjs, loop.mjs.
- **Phase D (client, parallel):** index.html + main.mjs (renderer/reconcile/input) and ui.mjs (HUD/inventory/death-window).
- **Phase E (tests + README, parallel):** prove-combat / prove-undeath / prove-deaths + README.
- Use `isolation: "worktree"` only if agents would write the same file; here files are disjoint so plain parallel agents are fine.
  Integrate (tick.mjs, loop.mjs) on the main thread after each layer.

## Verification (end-to-end)

1. **Install/link:** `pnpm install` at repo root (resolves `workspace:*` to tab).
2. **Unit proofs:** `pnpm --filter @561/development.experimental.ruinfold test` → prove-combat, prove-undeath, prove-deaths all pass (health supersession, ⊤ undeath + rise, the 5-way death router).
  Also run `tab`'s own tests once to confirm the substrate is intact.
3. **Seed + run:** `pnpm --filter ...ruinfold run dev` (seeds world/, starts server).
  Confirm it logs a listening port and ticks.
4. **Browser (use the `run`/`verify` skill or a headless check):** open the served URL; confirm three.js loads from CDN, the scene renders, a player mesh joins, WASD + click-to-move move it (SSE deltas flowing), attacking a skeleton drops its health to 0 and it **rises flickering as ⊤**, a goblin dies to a ghost-run, a boss dies to a corpse + loot, a wraith vanishes.
  Two browser tabs = two players sharing one world (the MMO check).
5. **Replay:** confirm the world is reconstructable from `world/*.jsonl` (the trace IS the world) — restart the server without re-seeding and state persists.

## Risks

- **Real-time over append-only disk:** mitigated by dirty-set + cache + single-writer
  + 5 Hz tick + client interpolation (§ Critical details).
- **CDN dependency for three.js:** the client needs internet to load three.js; acceptable per the charter, noted in README (could vendor later).
- **Log growth / no compaction in v0:** acknowledged, README-flagged.
- **Scope is broad:** if time-constrained at execution, the playable slice (zones
  + combat + the 5-way death model + one of each monster type) is the must-ship core; items/XP/leveling layer on top and can be trimmed last.

## Sources (death-model inspiration) - [Lycanthropy — Project: Gorgon Wiki](https://wiki.projectgorgon.com/wiki/Lycanthropy) - [Beast Forms — Project: Gorgon Wiki](https://wiki.projectgorgon.com/wiki/Beast_Forms) - [Death Effects and Diseases — Project Gorgon Wiki](https://project-gorgon.fandom.com/wiki/Death_Effects_and_Diseases)

# play.561.group

A static, self-contained shelf with zero *runtime* dependencies: a directory of 561 Group
games, organized into shelves-within-the-shelf (Card Table / Puzzle Den / Study / Deep --
see [`the-suite-and-the-studio.md`](../../content/text/documents/articles/notes/the-suite-and-the-studio.md)
§3), plus a daily front door. Reads `catalog.json` -- one cartridge-manifest-shaped entry
per game -- and renders game cards. No build step, no framework, no CDN. Browser clients
and terminal/API clients are both first-class; an AI player is just another client
emitting intent logs, per the
[Cartridge and Energy Bank spec](../../content/text/documents/articles/notes/cartridge-and-energy-bank-spec.md)
this site implements the storefront half of (see spec section 3). The one dependency this
package declares, `@561-group/cartridge`, is a `devDependency` used only by
`test/smoke.test.mts` to validate `catalog.json` against the real published schema -- it
never ships to a browser or a served response.

## Layout

```
index.html          the shelf -- fetches catalog.json client-side, renders game cards
today.html            the daily ritual -- one strip per game with a real, verified daily
                       seed; every seed computed live in the browser from today's real
                       UTC date, never hand-typed for one day and left to go stale
catalog.json          one cartridge-manifest-shaped entry per game; for the four games
                       that ship their own real @561-group/cartridge manifest (solitaire,
                       onestone, flickering-delve, gambling-trainer) this catalog's entry
                       is pulled directly from that manifest, not hand-retyped
css/style.css          theme-aware (light/dark via prefers-color-scheme), responsive;
                       shared by index.html and today.html
js/catalog.mjs          zero-dependency renderer for index.html: fetch, filter, render
js/today.mjs             zero-dependency renderer for today.html: computes today's real
                          UTC-derived seed for each live-daily game, in the browser
js/glyphs.mjs             the shared icon set both renderers import from -- one glyph per
                          game id, drawn once, used everywhere on this site
chrome/                  Lane B's vendored shelf-chrome source (the shared "card back" --
                          see chrome/README.md); this site is the chrome's origin, not a
                          consumer of a vendored copy, so index.html/today.html use
                          css/style.css directly rather than importing chrome/shelf-chrome.css
serve.mjs                zero-dependency node:http static file server
test/smoke.test.mts      node --test: validates catalog.json against real @561-group/cartridge
                          + index.html + today.html + serve.mjs
package.json              declares @561-group/cartridge as a devDependency (test-only)
.npmrc                    scopes @561-group/* to the private Verdaccio registry
```

## Run it

```
npm run serve            # http://127.0.0.1:8561/
node serve.mjs 3000      # or pick a port positionally
PORT=3000 node serve.mjs # or via env
```

`HOST` defaults to `127.0.0.1`. No credentials, no config, no external calls -- this
site only ever fetches its own `catalog.json`, and `today.html`'s only outbound-looking
links are plain `<a href>`s to each game's real (not-yet-deployed) subdomain and to each
game's own local dev port -- neither is fetched by this site itself.

## Test it

```
npm install        # pulls @561-group/cartridge from Verdaccio (see .npmrc), devDependency only
npm test          # node --test test/*.test.mts
npm run check      # node --check over serve.mjs, js/*.mjs, test/*.test.mts
```

The smoke test:

1. Loads `catalog.json` and checks it's valid JSON with a non-empty `games` array.
2. Asserts no catalog entry ever explicitly sets a field to `null` -- a field this catalog
   can't honestly fill in yet must be omitted, never faked as `null`.
3. For any entry with `cartridgeWrapped:true` (solitaire, onestone, flickering-delve,
   gambling-trainer, as of this pass), runs its manifest-shaped fields through the real,
   published `@561-group/cartridge`'s own `validateManifest` and requires full strict
   validity -- this is not a hand-rolled schema check, it is the actual package those
   games are really wrapped against.
4. For every entry, validates the honest subset of the `CartridgeManifest` shape it
   actually fills in (id, displayName, description, subdomain, entryPoints, seedPolicy,
   intentLog, keywords, and the optional configs/energy/replayVerifier fields when
   present), plus this site's own `status`/`statusNote`/`cartridgeWrapped`/`shelf`
   extensions. Also checks ids and subdomains are unique, that any entry marked
   `"playable"` actually declares a browser or headless entry point, and that `shelf` is
   one of the-suite-and-the-studio.md §3's named shelves.
5. Checks `index.html` references only local assets -- no `http(s)://` or `//` script/link
   `src`/`href` anywhere (a `data:` favicon is the one allowed exception).
6. Checks `today.html` loads no remote script/stylesheet, and that its `<script src>` is
   local -- deliberately a looser check than index.html's, since today.html's whole point
   is real `<a href="https://*.561.group/...">` links out to each game.
7. Checks `js/today.mjs` only ever builds a strip for the four games whose daily-seed
   surface was actually read and verified this session (ruinfold, crucible, solitaire,
   gambling-trainer) -- a guard against a future edit silently adding a fifth game's strip
   without the same verification discipline.
8. Boots `serve.mjs` on an ephemeral port and does real HTTP round-trips against `/`,
   `/catalog.json`, `/css/style.css`, `/js/catalog.mjs`, `/today.html`, `/js/today.mjs`,
   `/js/glyphs.mjs`, a 404 path, and a path-traversal attempt.

All eight suites are green as of 2026-08-19 (`node --test test/*.test.mts`: 8/8 passing).

## What's in `catalog.json`, and why some fields are omitted rather than `null`

`@561-group/cartridge` and `@561-group/energy-bank` are real, published packages
(`npm install @561-group/cartridge` / `@561-group/energy-bank`, `--registry
http://127.0.0.1:4873/`). As of this pass, **four games have actually been wrapped**:
solitaire, onestone (TileSlots), flickering-delve, and gambling-trainer (Kelly's Wager)
each ship their own real `src/cartridge.mts` + manifest module, and each one's manifest
passes the real `@561-group/cartridge` `validateManifest` strict check -- verified live
this session, not assumed from a comment. This catalog's entries for those four are
copied directly from each game's own manifest export (id/displayName/description/
subdomain/configs/entryPoints/seedPolicy/intentLog/replayVerifier/keywords) rather than
hand-retyped, specifically so this file cannot drift out of sync with the real source of
truth the way the previous, fully-hand-authored catalog eventually did (see "What
changed" below). The other five entries (crucible, lantern, weiqi, ruinfold, stoke) are
still `cartridgeWrapped:false`, honestly -- crucible/weiqi/ruinfold have no
`src/cartridge.mts` at all yet; lantern's tree was mid-build under another workflow at
generation time and wasn't touched; stoke's own README claims a real cartridge adoption
(94/94 tests including 12 cartridge tests) but that claim was not independently re-run
this session because stoke-service's tree was under active concurrent development at
generation time (house doctrine: mid-build trees are off-limits) -- see its `statusNote`.
`catalog.json` is otherwise still hand-authored for those five; build-time generation for
every entry (spec section 3) remains unstarted future work.

Where a manifest field names something that doesn't exist yet for an unwrapped game (a
`replayVerifier` module, an `intentLog.schemaRef`), the key is **omitted entirely** rather
than set to `null` -- a manifest field with an explicit `null` is not a value the real
`@561-group/cartridge` `validateManifest` accepts either (it requires `replayVerifier` to
be a non-empty string, and `intentLog.schemaRef`, when present, to be one too), so `null`
was never an honest stand-in for "doesn't exist," only an omitted key is. `test/smoke.test.mts`
enforces this as a standing rule (no catalog entry may ever explicitly null a field) and
validates every entry against the real, published `@561-group/cartridge`'s own
`validateManifest`: full strict validation for any entry with `cartridgeWrapped:true`,
and the honest subset check below for every `cartridgeWrapped:false` entry.
`entryPoints.headless`, when present, sometimes names a real JSON HTTP API
(flickering-delve, onestone: `POST /session`, `POST /input`; ruinfold: `GET /daily`,
`POST /runs`, `GET /leaderboard/:date`, `GET /replay/:runId`, `GET /boons/:player`) and
sometimes names a real pure engine module importable directly with no server at all
(solitaire, lantern, weiqi-kernel) -- both are legitimate "AI players are peers" access
paths.

A few fields are storefront-only extensions, not part of the spec's `CartridgeManifest`,
documented here rather than silently mixed in:

- `status`: `"playable"` or `"in-development"` -- verified by actually running each
  game's test suite and, where a browser entry point exists, its server.
- `statusNote`: the honest one-line-or-more evidence for that status (test counts, what's
  missing, what was and wasn't independently re-verified this session).
- `repoPath`: where the game actually lives in this monorepo -- every path below was
  `stat`'d before this pass wrote it.
- `tests`: `{ passing, total }` from the most recent `node --test` run this session
  (except lantern and stoke, whose trees were off-limits mid-build elsewhere -- see their
  `statusNote`s for provenance).
- `cartridgeWrapped` / `energyBankWrapped`: `cartridgeWrapped` is `true` for the four
  games verified against the real `validateManifest` this session, `false` for the other
  five (honestly, per the paragraph above). `energyBankWrapped` is `false` for every
  entry -- `@561-group/energy-bank` is a real, published package, but no game settles
  against it yet.
- `shelf`: which shelf-within-the-shelf this game lives on, per
  `the-suite-and-the-studio.md` §3 -- `"Card Table"`, `"Puzzle Den"`, `"Study"`, `"Deep"`,
  `"Stars"`, `"substrate"`, or `"unshelved"`.

## Catalog contents (as verified 2026-08-19)

| game | shelf | status | tests | cartridge-wrapped | browser | daily? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| solitaire | Card Table | playable | 59/59 | yes | `/` | yes |
| gambling-trainer (Kelly's Wager) | Card Table | playable | 79/79 | yes | `/` | yes |
| flickering-delve | Puzzle Den | playable | 63/63 | yes | `/` (SSE) | no |
| onestone (TileSlots) | Puzzle Den | playable | 249/249 | yes | `/` (SSE) | no |
| crucible | Puzzle Den | playable | 103/103 | no | `/web/index.html` | yes |
| stoke | Puzzle Den | playable | 94/94\* | no\* | `/` | no |
| lantern | Study | playable | 74/74\* | no | `/` | no |
| weiqi | Study | playable | 74/74 | no | `/` | no |
| ruinfold | Deep | playable | 79/79 | no | `/play` | yes |

\* stoke's and lantern's counts are carried forward from each game's own last-verified
pass, not re-run this session -- both trees were mid-build under another workflow at
generation time (house doctrine holds mid-build trees off-limits). Everything else in
this table was independently re-run or re-curled this session.

Corrected from the previous pass: **crucible, stoke, and gambling-trainer were missing
from the catalog entirely** despite being real, running, tested code (crucible and
gambling-trainer are now cartridge-verified or fully tested respectively; stoke's own
README self-reports the same). **weiqi-web** (Play/Learn/Read, real and locally playable,
71/71 kernel + 3/3 web smoke) was also missing -- the previous catalog only knew about
the rules kernel and an undeployed Learn app. **ruinfold** was listed `in-development,
0/0 tests, no server, no client` -- it now has a real `node:http` server, a real browser
client (`web/play.html`, `web/watch.html`), and 79/79 passing tests; this was verified
live this session (`GET /health`, `GET /daily`, `GET /play`, `GET /watch` all curled
successfully against a freshly booted instance, today's seed `0x8b8ad99c`, 6 floors).
**solitaire, onestone, and flickering-delve** turned out to already be cartridge-wrapped
(none of that was true the last time this catalog was written) and solitaire gained 5
more variants (Yukon, Forty Thieves, Golf, TriPeaks, Pyramid -- 11 total) and onestone
gained a full 60-level roster, both now sourced directly from each game's own manifest.

## The Today page

[`today.html`](today.html) is the suite's front door (the-suite-and-the-studio.md §5
directive 2): one strip per game with a **real, verified daily-seed surface** -- checked
by reading each game's own source this session, not by trusting a `seedPolicy` field.
Four qualify: **Ruinfold** (`daily.mts`'s SHA-256-derived seed, confirmed against a live
`GET /daily` response), **Crucible** (`daily.mts`'s plain `crucible-daily:<date>` string),
**Solitaire** (`daily.mts`'s `solitaire-daily:<variant>:<date>` string, one seed per
variant), and **Kelly's Wager / gambling-trainer** (`daily.mts`'s thin wrapper over
`@561-group/cartridge/seed`'s `dailySeed`). Every seed shown is computed **live in the
browser** from the real UTC clock (`js/today.mjs`), via a small, faithfully-ported copy of
each game's own seed formula -- headed with a comment naming its real source file, per
house vendoring doctrine (vendor a copy, not a live cross-service import; these are
separate node services). Ruinfold's port additionally reproduces `mulberry32` + the first
`intBetween` draw from `dungeon.mts` to show today's real floor count, verified against
the live server's own `buildDaily` output before being ported.

Five other real, playable games (flickering-delve, onestone, lantern, weiqi, stoke) do
**not** get a strip -- their `seedPolicy.kind` is `on-demand`, not `daily-utc`; there is
no daily ritual to compute. This is stated on the page itself, with a link back to the
full catalog.

**Chrome note:** Lane B's `chrome/shelf-chrome.css` landed (2026-08-19, 15:04) shortly
before this page was written -- it's vendored *into* other games' own pages, and this
site is its origin, so `today.html` and `index.html` use this site's own
`css/style.css` directly rather than importing a vendored copy of their own chrome.

## Adding a game to the catalog

Per the spec's section 3: implement `Cartridge`, publish a `CartridgeManifest`, add one
entry to `catalog.json` (pulling straight from the manifest export if one exists, per
solitaire/onestone/flickering-delve/gambling-trainer's pattern above), pick a `shelf`. No
changes to `index.html`, `css/style.css`, or `js/catalog.mjs` are needed -- the renderer
only ever touches manifest-shaped fields, never a game's internal `State`/`Intent`/
`GameEvent` types. If the new game has a real `daily-utc` seed policy, add a strip to
`js/today.mjs` too, with a faithfully-ported (never live-imported) copy of its seed
formula. Run `npm test` after editing to confirm everything is shaped correctly before
publishing.

# shelf-chrome — the shared shelf frame Canonical source for the small shared UI frame every 561 shelf game wears: the-suite-and- the-studio.md §5 directive 1 ("Shelf chrome... the modern card back. Rides the cartridge contract; vendored per house doctrine, not live-imported."). **Scope, deliberately small.** This is not a theme system and does not replace any game's own palette. It owns exactly three things: the small shelf mark next to a game's own title, the "part of the 561 shelf" footer line, and the focus-visible/reduced-motion/type-scale rules those two things need. Every game keeps its own background, panel, ink, and accent tokens — same card back, different felt. ## Files - `shelf-chrome.css` — the CSS. Every `--shelf-*` token falls back to the game's own `--accent` / `--ink-dim` (or `--text-dim`) / `--border` / `--bg` / `--ink` tokens first, and only then to a neutral default (crucible / gambling-trainer's palette, the newest pair at the time this was drawn up). A game with no matching token still renders correctly off the defaults alone. ## Vendoring a copy (house doctrine: vendor a copy, not a live import) 1. Copy `shelf-chrome.css` byte-identical into the game's own css directory (or, for a template-literal `.mts` client with no separate CSS file, into a small `chrome.mts` that exports the same text as a string constant). 2. Add a one-line provenance header at the top of the copy naming this file as the source — the same convention as `onestone-service/src/ledger.mts`'s header naming `flickering-delve-service/src/ledger.mts`, or `lantern-service/src/stability.mts`'s header naming `onestone-service/src/validate.mts` (house-specification-standard.md, "vendor a copy, not a cross-service import"). 3. Link/import it *after* the game's own stylesheet so the game's own rules still win any token collision. 4. Add the mark next to the game's own title and the footer line at the end of the page — see markup below. No other HTML should change. ## Markup Header (goes next to the game's own title, inside its existing header element): ```html ``` Footer (a new line inside or beside the game's existing footer): ```html
